descriptions.approach: A multi-layered feedback mechanism adjusts real-time response parameters based on input dynamics, using adaptive filtering and dynamic regulation to preserve output consistency across changing operational conditions.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Laser technology and 3D printing for production of biopolymer-based hollow microneedles patch for biomedical applications

descriptions.problem: A method is developed to create hollow, needle-like structures with precise internal geometry from biodegradable polymer materials, using a combination of patterned surface shaping and polymer molding under controlled conditions.
descriptions.approach: A template is etched with a spiral-shaped surface using focused energy, then a polymer is molded into the shape under pressure. The internal cavity is formed by pressing the polymer against a counterform, with geometric parameters adjusted to ensure consistent hollow structure formation.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The goal is to create a method for delivering drugs through the skin that is less invasive and painless, and can be done without the need for trained people. The method aims to improve the amount of drug that is absorbed by the body.
descriptions.approach: The approach involves using a combination of laser technology and 3D printing to create a device that can deliver drugs through the skin. The device is made from a biodegradable and biocompatible material, and is designed to be easy to produce and use.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: ANALISA PENGARUH KEMIRINGAN ANTENNA (JARINGAN SISTEM CDMA 2000 1X)

descriptions.problem: This research aims to estimate the impact of antenna orientation on the quality and quantity of a communication system's signal. It predicts the effect of changing antenna tilt and power on the system's performance, specifically the Ec/Io ratio and Rx level.
descriptions.approach: The research uses simulation to compare the effects of different antenna orientations and power levels on the system's performance. It follows a procedure of modeling the system, applying different scenarios, and analyzing the results to identify the most influential factors.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The effect of adjusting a directional parameter on signal strength and reception performance is estimated and compared across different network conditions, focusing on two key metrics: signal clarity and overall received power.
descriptions.approach: A simulation model adjusts a geometric orientation parameter and evaluates its impact on signal clarity and received power under various environmental and network conditions, then compares outcomes across different configurations.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Human Peripheral Blood Macrophages As a Model for Studying Glucocerebrosidase Dysfunction

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the efficiency of different methods for growing cells from patients with a certain disease, and compares the activity of an enzyme and the levels of certain lipids in these cells. It also predicts the effectiveness of certain compounds in increasing the enzyme's activity.
descriptions.approach: The researchers compared the results of different methods for growing cells from patients and control subjects, and used a technique called tandem mass spectrometry to measure the enzyme's activity and lipid levels. They also tested the effectiveness of certain compounds in increasing the enzyme's activity in these cells.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The functional performance of a specific enzyme in human cells is measured over time, and the levels of a particular lipid metabolite are monitored to assess downstream biochemical consequences.
descriptions.approach: Cells are maintained under varying conditions, and enzyme activity is quantified using a sensitive mass-based detection method. Candidate compounds are introduced to determine their effect on enzyme function and lipid accumulation in a controlled, repeatable environment.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Copeptin levels in patients with coronary artery ectasia

descriptions.problem: This study aims to determine if a certain biomarker is elevated in individuals with a specific condition, and if so, whether it is related to the condition. The study estimates the level of this biomarker in a group of people with the condition and a group without it.
descriptions.approach: The researchers collected blood samples from two groups of people and measured the level of a specific biomarker in each sample. They then compared the levels between the two groups to see if there was a difference.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A biological marker's concentration is measured across a group of individuals with a specific anatomical condition and a matched group without it, to determine if the marker differs significantly or correlates with the condition.
descriptions.approach: Blood samples are collected and stored for later analysis. The concentration of a stress-responsive substance is quantified using a standardized assay. Results are compared between groups using statistical evaluation to detect differences or associations.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Ocular prosthesis: A case report

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the effectiveness of a custom-made replacement for a missing eye, comparing it to a standard, pre-made version. It aims to explain how this replacement improves the patient's physical and mental well-being.
descriptions.approach: The researchers use a pre-made eye shell as a base and add custom features to create a more natural-looking replacement. They follow a step-by-step procedure to assemble and test the replacement, using data from the patient's medical history and the replacement's performance to inform their design.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A device is designed to replace a missing sensory organ to restore functional and visual continuity in a patient's daily experience.
descriptions.approach: A pre-existing template is adapted to match the patient's remaining eye structure, using measured dimensions and surface features to ensure alignment and natural appearance during use.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: The Genetic Guts of Modern Agriculture

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the impact of human activities on the natural world, comparing the effects of increased human numbers and aspirations on the potential of certain plants. It also explains how these changes can reduce the potential of these plants by a certain percentage.
descriptions.approach: The approach involves using data from various sources to model the relationship between human activities and the potential of these plants. It follows a procedure of collecting and analyzing evidence, identifying patterns and trends, and using this information to make predictions and estimates.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system estimates how much performance and resilience are lost when diverse, wild forms of a species are no longer available for breeding.
descriptions.approach: It models the outcome of combining limited, domesticated variants with rare, unaltered forms to assess how resilience and function improve under stress and environmental change.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Deletion of discoidin domain receptor 2 attenuates renal interstitial fibrosis in a murine unilateral ureteral obstruction model

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the role of a protein in a disease process, comparing the effects of its presence or absence on a specific condition. It predicts the impact of the protein's activity on the disease's progression.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used data from a specific group of animals to compare the effects of the protein's presence or absence on the disease process. They then applied a treatment to see if it could improve the outcome.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The extent of tissue scarring driven by collagen accumulation is measured in response to a sustained mechanical stress stimulus, and compared across groups with and without a specific receptor pathway intervention.
descriptions.approach: A biological system is exposed to a controlled stressor, and the response is monitored over time using histological and molecular markers. A targeted intervention is applied, and its effect on collagen-related signaling and structural changes is evaluated through quantitative and qualitative assessments.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: ANALYSIS OF PHYSICO-CHEMICAL CHARACTERISTICS OF BANDAM KUNTA LAKE WATER FOR RESTORING AS A BIODIVERSITY HERITAGE SITE

descriptions.problem: Estimate the suitability of a certain environment for a specific purpose, such as agriculture or ecosystem health. Compare the conditions before and after a seasonal change to identify the cause of degradation.
descriptions.approach: Analyze data from two time points to identify patterns and correlations. Use this information to explain the reasons for degradation and recommend measures to restore the environment.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system's condition is assessed over time through seasonal sampling to detect changes in key chemical and biological indicators, identifying sources of contamination and predicting degradation trends that impair ecological balance and functionality.
descriptions.approach: Data from two distinct periods are compared to identify shifts in nutrient levels and organic load; changes are linked to human activity patterns, and mitigation strategies are proposed based on observed trends and seasonal variability.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Investigating the use of Reverse Auctions for Restorable Wetlands on the Prairies

descriptions.problem: This study investigates why some people are not interested in participating in a process to restore a valuable resource, and what factors make it difficult for them to do so. It estimates the level of interest and barriers to participation, and compares different approaches to understand what works best.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used communication records and interviews to understand the motivations and concerns of people involved in the process. They compared two different methods of allocating resources to achieve the desired outcome, and found that one method was more effective than the other.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system is evaluated to determine how effectively it allocates scarce environmental services to stakeholders, based on their willingness to engage and the clarity of value they assign to those services.
descriptions.approach: A mechanism is applied where participants submit offers for service delivery, and outcomes are compared under two rules: one where all participants receive equal value, and another where value is distributed based on offer rank and available resources.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

topic_name: Physical education and sports games research
title: Emociones en Educación Física. Una revisión bibliográfica (2015-2017) (Emotions in Physical Education. A bibliographic review (2015-2017))

descriptions.problem: This research aims to understand the current state of emotional well-being in a specific context, where students are the main focus, and the emphasis is on understanding the emotional impact of this context on students rather than on the people who work in it.
descriptions.approach: The study involves a systematic review of existing research, where relevant data is collected from a database, and then analyzed to identify patterns and trends, with the goal of identifying areas for future research and practical applications.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The extent and focus of research on affective factors in learning environments is assessed, comparing attention given to learners versus instructors and evaluating how these factors are treated as outcomes versus tools in instructional processes.
descriptions.approach: A structured analysis of published studies is conducted using predefined selection criteria, then grouped by subject focus and conceptual framing to identify patterns in research emphasis and integration with other educational variables.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Boletín de Turismo Social de la Provincia de Buenos Aires

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the number of people who benefited from a government program aimed at promoting social and recreational activities, by comparing data from three different years.
descriptions.approach: It uses historical records to make predictions about the program's impact, and optimizes its effectiveness by analyzing the data from each year.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A sequence of three reports is retrieved from a historical archive, each detailing public activities and cultural events organized by a government body during a specific administrative period.
descriptions.approach: The system identifies and compiles documents from a digital repository, then extracts and organizes information about civic engagement initiatives, their timing, locations, and key personnel involved in their execution.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: From Archived Historical Aerial Imagery to Informative Orthophotos: A Framework for Retrieving the Past in Long-Term Socioecological Research

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the changes in vegetation and land cover over time from old photographs taken from the air, but the old photographs are not accurate because they don't have the right information about the camera and the ground they were taken on.
descriptions.approach: It uses a method to figure out where the old photographs were taken from and how to make them accurate, and then it uses a computer program to do this for many old photographs at once.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A set of aerial images from a long period ago is transformed into a precise, geographically aligned representation to enable accurate comparison of land surface features over time.
descriptions.approach: Using known camera geometry and ground control points, the images are mathematically adjusted to correct perspective distortions and align spatially, producing a consistent, high-resolution map of the landscape at a specific time.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Consciousness, will and time

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the likelihood of a person performing a specific action (e.g., putting on clothes) without conscious intention, and compares it to the likelihood of the same action being performed with conscious intention. It also explains why this might happen.
descriptions.approach: The researcher uses a combination of data from past experiences (e.g., past actions, observations of others) and evidence from their own observations of their own behavior to make these estimates and comparisons.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system detects and evaluates deviations in routine behavior that occur without conscious intent, assessing whether an action was intentionally performed or executed unintentionally due to habitual or automatic processes.
descriptions.approach: The system monitors behavioral sequences over time, comparing observed actions to expected patterns, and flags inconsistencies that suggest a shift from deliberate control to habitual execution.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Climate change effects on groundwater recharge in Yucatan Peninsula. Application of water balance models to GCMs

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the impact of changes in climate conditions on the amount of water available from the land to the surface in a specific region. It predicts how this change will affect the amount of water available in the future.
descriptions.approach: The researchers use a mathematical model to compare the predictions of different climate models. They apply this model to data from five different climate models to estimate the current amount of water available and the potential future changes.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The impact of shifting temperature and moisture patterns on the long-term flow of subsurface water into aquifer systems is estimated across multiple climate projections.
descriptions.approach: A monthly cycle-based model is applied to five climate simulations, calculating the balance between input and output over time, then projecting changes in the net volume of water entering the system annually.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Continuous Fourier Transform: A practical approach for truncated signals and suggestions for improvements in thermography

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the shape of a signal's frequency content, using a mathematical technique to smooth out the signal and make it more suitable for analysis. It also compares the results to an existing method, to see if the new approach produces more accurate or consistent results.
descriptions.approach: The work uses a mathematical technique to smooth out the signal, and then applies a mathematical formula to estimate the shape of the signal's frequency content. The approach is based on a mathematical model that is applied to a set of data, to produce a new set of data that is more suitable for analysis.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system estimates the frequency content of a time-varying signal, comparing results across different sampling conditions to detect inconsistencies in amplitude and phase.
descriptions.approach: The signal is modeled as a piecewise polynomial over a defined interval, and its frequency components are derived through integration of the signal's time-domain representation over time.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Optimización de la producción de néctar mediante el método de balance de línea en la Empresa Enrique Cassinelli e Hijos S.A.C.

descriptions.problem: This research aims to improve the efficiency of a production process by analyzing and optimizing the allocation of resources. It estimates the most efficient way to use workers and equipment to produce a certain amount of output.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a method to study the times and movements of workers, creating diagrams to visualize their activities. They then analyzed the data to identify the most efficient way to use resources, resulting in increased output and efficiency.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A production process is analyzed to determine the most efficient allocation of labor across sequential tasks, aiming to reduce idle time and increase output volume per unit of time.
descriptions.approach: Task durations and worker movements are mapped through observation and sampling. Work is divided into discrete steps, and labor is reallocated to minimize idle periods and balance workload across stations.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: DemDx: An innovative digital clinical decision support software for medical students

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the effectiveness of a digital tool in supporting clinical decision making for a specific group, comparing the tool's use to a traditional teaching method. It aims to explain how the tool can improve the process of clinical decision making.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a digital tool to guide a group through a series of cases, then asked the group to reflect on their experience with the tool. They collected anonymous feedback from the group to understand how the tool was used and its impact.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system evaluates clinical scenarios to guide practitioners through a structured sequence of diagnostic reasoning, using patient history, physical findings, and test results to identify likely underlying conditions.
descriptions.approach: The system presents a sequence of questions and observations, updating the probability of various conditions based on incoming data, and directs users to next steps in diagnosis by prioritizing likely explanations and relevant investigations.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Application of structuration theory in the context of ICT: the case of DESH microfinance in Bangladesh

descriptions.problem: This research aims to evaluate how a well-structured framework can help identify and understand the connections between social issues, technology, and the practices of a leading institution in Bangladesh that provides financial services to individuals.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a case study approach, examining the connections between social issues, technology, and practices at the institution, and providing suggestions on how technology can be more meaningful to the practitioners.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system is analyzed to understand how human actions and technological tools interact and influence each other within a real-world setting involving digital tools and human decision-making.
descriptions.approach: A framework is applied that maps how practices and tools evolve together, identifying patterns where human behavior shapes technology and technology, in turn, reshapes human behavior over time.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Medial Upper Lip Vermillion Reconstruction with a Labial Artery-based Cross-lip Vermillion Flap

descriptions.problem: This work aims to estimate and reconstruct a specific part of the upper lip that is visually important and has a unique structure and color, to restore its appearance and function after damage or injury.
descriptions.approach: The approach involves creating a new, donor site-based tissue that is transplanted to the damaged area, with a procedure that involves raising and moving the tissue, followed by dividing the connecting blood vessels to complete the reconstruction.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A missing segment in a visible, sensitive area of the upper lip is reconstructed using tissue from a nearby region, with emphasis on matching color, texture, and function to the surrounding area.
descriptions.approach: A tissue segment is lifted from a lower lip region, connected by a blood supply, moved to cover the missing area, and then detached after healing to complete the reconstruction.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Apixaban Suppresses the Release of TF-Positive Microvesicles and Restrains Cancer Cell Proliferation through Directly Inhibiting TF-fVIIa Activity

descriptions.problem: This study estimates the effect of a certain compound on the release of a specific type of tiny particle from two types of cells, and compares it to the effect of another compound. It also predicts the effect of the compound on the rate at which these cells multiply.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a procedure that involves adding the compound to the cells, then measuring the release of the tiny particles and the rate at which the cells multiply. They also tested the effect of blocking a specific receptor and the compound's ability to inhibit the activity of a specific enzyme.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A mechanism is identified that links a specific protein complex to the release of signaling particles that promote uncontrolled growth in certain cell types, and how a drug selectively blocks a key enzymatic step in that process.
descriptions.approach: A compound is applied to cells exposed to a specific activator, suppressing the release of signaling particles only when the activator binds to a receptor. The effect is blocked by a receptor inhibitor or a neutralizing antibody, confirming the pathway's dependence on receptor engagement and enzymatic activity.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Using Quick Response Code in Food Packaging for Traceability and Marketing Strategies

descriptions.problem: An estimate or prediction is made about the effectiveness of a certain method of communication between companies and their customers, based on data about how well the method works in a specific context.
descriptions.approach: A procedure is followed to compare the results of using this method with the results of not using it, and to optimise the method for better performance.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system estimates the likelihood of user engagement with a product-based information channel based on product details and user interaction history.
descriptions.approach: A digital identifier is embedded in a product unit and linked to a database of product attributes and user interactions. When scanned, it retrieves and presents curated information in a structured format for immediate access.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Institution-Building in the Pacific

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the likelihood of cooperation among states in a region with diverse economic and social characteristics, and compares it to a benchmark from a more developed region.
descriptions.approach: It uses a model that considers the underlying pattern of strategic interaction among states and the conflicting goals of major powers to design a framework for cooperation.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A pattern of cooperative frameworks is assessed across diverse geopolitical settings, where regional actors balance competing objectives and adapt structures to local conditions.
descriptions.approach: A model evaluates how external pressures and internal dynamics shape the design, stability, and success of shared systems, adjusting parameters based on historical precedents and regional diversity.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Cranial burr hole with erythropoietin administration induces reverse arteriogenesis from the enriched extracranium

descriptions.problem: This research aims to improve blood flow to a damaged area of the brain after a stroke. It estimates the effectiveness of a new method to revive the brain area by comparing it to a control group.
descriptions.approach: The researchers created a blockage in the blood flow to one side of the brain, then used a small hole in the skull to allow blood to flow from the other side. They gave some rats a special protein to help their bodies make new blood vessels, and measured the results.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system is evaluated to determine whether a controlled disruption of a barrier enables the formation of new vascular connections from outside to inside a tissue region that was previously deprived of blood supply.
descriptions.approach: A physical intervention is applied to a tissue to initiate vascular signaling, followed by the delivery of a substance that modulates inflammatory and structural responses to enhance vessel growth and stability, with the process being halted by a specific inhibitor.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Multiple foraminal compression in a child with sialidosis type 2

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the effectiveness of a treatment for a child's chronic pain, comparing the child's pain levels before and after treatment. It predicts the child's pain levels will decrease over time.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used data from the child's pain levels and treatment outcomes to develop a model that predicts the child's pain levels. They tested this model by applying it to the child's data and comparing the results to the actual pain levels.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A pattern of progressive motor weakness and sensory disturbances is observed over time, with symptoms worsening and new pain responses emerging in response to stimuli.
descriptions.approach: A longitudinal imaging study tracks structural changes in neural pathways and surrounding tissues, using statistical modeling to correlate symptom onset with anatomical shifts and treatment response over time.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Human metapneumovirus as cause of severe community-acquired pneumonia in adults: insights from a ten-year molecular and epidemiological analysis

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the likelihood of a specific type of pneumonia in adults, comparing the severity of the disease to the age and health status of the individuals. It also predicts the need for mechanical ventilation and identifies biomarkers to help manage the disease.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used data from a ten-year period to analyze the characteristics of the pneumonia, including the age and health status of the individuals, and the types of bacteria that were present. They compared the severity of the disease to these factors to identify patterns and trends.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A pattern of respiratory illness in adults is analyzed to determine the likelihood of a specific pathogen causing acute respiratory failure and organ dysfunction, and to assess whether a biological marker distinguishes cases with a secondary bacterial presence.
descriptions.approach: Data from clinical records and laboratory tests are reviewed over a decade to identify disease onset timing, patient demographics, and severity scores. A statistical model compares marker levels across cases with and without a secondary infection to evaluate diagnostic utility.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Load Frequency Control in Connected Power System including Distributed Energy Resources using Iterative Gradient Method

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the optimal control action to minimize the cost of managing energy resources in a complex system, while keeping the system stable and respecting the limitations of these resources. It compares different control options to find the best solution.
descriptions.approach: The work uses a mathematical model that describes how the system behaves, taking into account the limitations of the energy resources. It follows a procedure that involves minimizing a cost function, which is calculated based on the system's performance and the resources' limitations.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system estimates how to adjust energy storage and generation to maintain balance between supply and demand over time, minimizing operational cost while respecting physical limits of storage and production capacity.
descriptions.approach: The system repeatedly refines adjustments by computing gradients of a cost function, updating decisions based on local error and system response until changes become negligible and stability is achieved.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Studies on Genetic Variability for Yield, Yield Attributing Traits, Physiological and Quality Traits in Groundnut [Arachis hypogaea L.]

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the impact of genetic differences on the performance of 30 different varieties, comparing the effects of different characteristics on growth and quality. It also predicts the effectiveness of selection in improving these characteristics.
descriptions.approach: The study uses data from 30 varieties to calculate the influence of genetic differences on growth and quality. It then uses this information to determine the best approach for improving these characteristics through selection.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The degree to which differences in performance among individuals are due to inherited factors is estimated, and the potential for improvement through selection is assessed using data from multiple environmental conditions.
descriptions.approach: Differences in performance across individuals are analyzed under varying conditions. A statistical model evaluates the influence of inherited factors versus environmental noise, and identifies which features show strong response to selection based on the consistency and magnitude of performance differences.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Aggressive large B‐cell lymphoma triggered by a parvovirus B19 infection in a previously healthy child

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the likelihood of a rare and aggressive disease in a previously healthy child, based on a viral infection. It compares the child's immune system to a normal one, and predicts the potential development of a serious disease.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a combination of clinical observations and medical tests to identify the disease. They followed up with the child over time to see if the disease developed, and analyzed the results to draw conclusions about the role of the viral infection in triggering the disease.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A sudden onset of a severe and rapidly progressing blood cell disorder is observed in a previously healthy individual, raising the possibility that a previously mild infection may have initiated the development of a malignant condition.
descriptions.approach: A longitudinal medical record is analyzed to track changes in blood cell counts and tissue structure over time, with comparisons made between early infection signs and later tissue abnormalities to identify potential causal links.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Multiple roles and regulatory mechanisms of the transcription factor GATA6 in human cancers

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the role of a protein in multiple diseases, compares its expression levels in different tissues, and optimizes its potential as a therapeutic target. It aims to explain the relationship between the protein's expression and disease development.
descriptions.approach: The study uses data from various tissues and diseases to identify patterns and correlations. It follows a procedure of summarizing and analyzing existing research to provide new insights and potential targets.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system-wide pattern of gene activity is assessed to determine how a single regulatory protein influences diverse biological outcomes across different tissue contexts.
descriptions.approach: A computational framework maps the activity of a key regulatory factor across multiple tissue types and disease states, identifying context-dependent outcomes through integration of expression profiles and functional interaction networks.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Intraoperative tension pneumothorax during posterior vertebral column resection in a child with congenital scoliosis

descriptions.problem: The researchers estimated the likelihood of a sudden, unexplained change in a patient's airway pressure and hemodynamic stability during a complex surgery, and compared it to the expected outcome. They aimed to explain the cause of this change and provide a guideline for managing similar situations.
descriptions.approach: They used a temporary, makeshift solution to drain the air that had accumulated in the patient's chest cavity, and later supplemented it with a standard device. The patient's condition improved, and they were discharged a few days later.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A sudden rise in airway pressure and deterioration in blood flow are observed during a complex surgical procedure involving extensive tissue manipulation. The cause is suspected to be a tear in a protective sac surrounding the lungs, leading to air accumulation and impaired lung function.
descriptions.approach: When unexpected changes in pressure and circulation occur, the procedure is evaluated for a breach in a sealed cavity. If confirmed, a temporary opening is made to release air, followed by standard drainage to restore normal function.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Immediate Observation in Mediated Population Protocols

descriptions.problem: A system of identical agents, each with limited memory, must reach a consistent global state based on local interactions and shared observation of neighbors' states over time.
descriptions.approach: Agents update their behavior by directly observing the current state of adjacent agents, and a global configuration is defined by tracking each agent's state and its neighbors' states during interactions, enabling deterministic convergence to a known outcome.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the capabilities of a system with limited agents that can share information through a network. It compares the performance of different systems with varying levels of information sharing.
descriptions.approach: The system uses a network of agents to share information, and the agents can record the states of the connections they use to communicate. The work analyzes the performance of the system by translating it into a new model that allows for more efficient information sharing.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Protective effect of 4-Methoxy benzyl alcohol on the neurovascular unit after cerebral ischemia reperfusion injury

descriptions.problem: This research investigates the protective effect of a compound on the brain's microenvironment after a period of reduced blood flow and subsequent return of blood flow, which can cause damage and death of brain cells. The goal is to reduce the severity of this damage and improve brain function.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a model of reduced blood flow to a specific area of the brain, and then tested the compound's effects on the brain's microenvironment using various laboratory tests. They also created a model of the brain's cells responding to reduced blood flow and then returning to normal, to see how the compound affected the brain's cells.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A substance is evaluated for its ability to stabilize a complex biological network under stress, measuring changes in key structural and functional markers across different tissue environments.
descriptions.approach: The substance is applied to stressed biological systems, and its effects are assessed through molecular and cellular analysis, focusing on protein expression levels and redox balance indicators in response to injury and recovery.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Plasma circular RNA panel to diagnose hepatitis B virus‐related hepatocellular carcinoma: A large‐scale, multicenter study

descriptions.problem: This research aims to identify a set of biomarkers that can accurately diagnose a specific type of cancer, which is more likely to occur in people with a certain virus. The researchers want to know if a certain type of molecule can be detected in the blood to predict the presence of this cancer.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a combination of data analysis techniques to identify the biomarkers. They trained a model on a large dataset and then tested it on two separate datasets to evaluate its accuracy.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A set of biomarkers in blood is used to distinguish individuals with a specific disease from those without it, based on patterns in biological samples collected from diverse patient groups.
descriptions.approach: A statistical model is trained on a group of samples to identify a combination of markers that best separates diseased from healthy individuals. The model is then tested on separate groups to confirm its ability to consistently detect the disease with high accuracy.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Comparison of Phenolic Constituent in Hibiscus sabdariffa cv. UKMR-2 Calyx at Different Harvesting Times

descriptions.problem: The relative abundance of several key bioactive compounds in a plant tissue is measured across different developmental stages, and their antioxidant potential is assessed through a chemical assay.
descriptions.approach: Samples are extracted using water and a standardized method to separate and quantify compound levels. A chromatographic technique resolves and measures compound concentrations, and a chemical test evaluates their ability to neutralize free radicals.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the amount of certain compounds in a plant at different stages of ripeness, compares these amounts to determine the best stage for harvesting, and explains how the compounds' properties change over time.
descriptions.approach: The researchers use a laboratory test to analyze the plant's compounds, and then compare the results to determine the best stage for harvesting. They use a specific method to extract and measure the compounds' amounts.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Hair pin bends of epicardial coronary arteries - a unique feature in multiple myocardial bridges

descriptions.problem: This study aims to estimate the incidence of a specific anatomical feature in a certain number of specimens, and compare it to the incidence of another feature. It also predicts the relationship between these features and a specific disease.
descriptions.approach: The researchers dissected 100 specimens and observed the presence of a specific feature in relation to another feature. They then counted the number of specimens with each feature and compared the results.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The frequency of a specific anatomical deformation is assessed in relation to the number of overlapping tissue segments that compress a vessel. This deformation is observed only when multiple such segments are present, and absent when only one is present.
descriptions.approach: A systematic examination of tissue specimens is conducted to identify the presence and pattern of a particular structural curvature. The pattern is then mapped to the count of overlapping tissue segments, revealing a consistent association between multiple segments and the curvature.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: The factors affecting the illness perception in patients staying in a state hospital

descriptions.problem: This study aims to identify the factors that influence how individuals perceive their health condition and how this perception affects their behavior and opinions. It estimates the impact of various factors on this perception.
descriptions.approach: The study collects data from a group of people receiving treatment, using a set of questions to gather information about their thoughts and feelings. It then uses statistical tests to analyze the data and identify patterns and correlations.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system identifies variables that influence how individuals interpret and respond to their health condition, using self-reported data from a group in a structured care setting.
descriptions.approach: A model evaluates patterns in responses to a set of statements about treatment outcomes and personal beliefs, applying statistical tests to detect differences and relationships among groups and individual reports.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Growth and Quality of Genotype PS-1319 Cacao Seedlings Produced Under Different Irrigation Depths

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the optimal amount of water needed to support the growth and quality of a specific type of plant, and compares the effects of different water levels on various plant characteristics.
descriptions.approach: The study used a combination of data collection and mathematical modeling to determine the best water level for the plant's growth and quality. It followed a completely randomized design, applying different water levels to a group of plants and measuring their responses.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A quantity is measured over time in response to varying input levels, and its relationship to the input is assessed across a range of conditions to identify the level that maximizes performance and quality indicators.
descriptions.approach: A set of input values is systematically applied, and outcomes are recorded for multiple growth-related metrics. A mathematical model fits the data to identify a peak response, indicating the optimal input level for desired development and quality outcomes.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Harvest Frequency and Native Warm-Season Grass Species Influence Nutritive Value

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the effect of different time intervals on the quality of a certain type of food, and compares it to different types of food. It also tries to optimize the quality of the food by varying the amount of a certain nutrient.
descriptions.approach: The researchers grew different types of food in different conditions and used a special technique to measure the quality of the food. They tested different time intervals and nutrient levels to see how they affected the quality of the food.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The effect of how often a plant is collected on its chemical composition and mineral content is estimated, compared across different types of plants and fertilizer levels.
descriptions.approach: Plants are grown under repeated collection cycles and varied nutrient inputs. Their chemical and mineral profiles are measured using spectral analysis. Results are evaluated to determine which collection frequency and plant type yield the most favorable composition.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Parameters sensitivity Analysis of the Duncan-Chang Model Based on Orthogonal Test

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the sensitivity of certain parameters to the performance of a complex system, specifically how changes in these parameters affect the system's strain and stress levels. It compares the effects of different parameter values on the system's behavior.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a combination of numerical analysis and statistical methods to test the sensitivity of eight parameters. They analyzed the variance of the system's response to changes in these parameters.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A set of physical properties influencing material behavior under load is evaluated to determine which ones most strongly affect stress and deformation responses.
descriptions.approach: Multiple combinations of property values are systematically tested using a structured sampling method. Responses are measured and compared across scenarios to identify which properties have the largest impact on outcomes.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: untitled: color body

descriptions.problem: This research estimates how people perceive color on a body, comparing their judgments to cultural influences and predicting how these influences affect their actions in social situations.
descriptions.approach: It uses a model that follows these steps: (1) collect data on people's color judgments of bodies from different cultural backgrounds, (2) compare these judgments to each other and to cultural norms, (3) use this information to predict how cultural influences affect people's actions in social situations.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: It estimates how visual perception of hue and saturation changes when applied to human forms, and how those interpretations vary across different cultural exposures and environmental contexts.
descriptions.approach: It uses repeated observations of human figures in varied lighting and settings, then applies statistical models to detect patterns in how hue is interpreted, adjusting for context and prior exposure to similar stimuli.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: The need for culturally competent school principals : K–12 school district hiring practices

descriptions.problem: This research aims to identify how districts advertise, recruit, and hire individuals with the ability to work effectively with diverse groups. It estimates the effectiveness of their hiring practices and provides insights to improve the recruitment of individuals with these skills.
descriptions.approach: The study uses a qualitative approach, collecting data through interviews and document analysis. It examines job descriptions and other documents to assess the district's hiring procedures and identify areas for improvement.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system is evaluated to determine how it identifies and selects individuals based on their ability to effectively engage with and support diverse groups within a community, particularly in educational environments where such engagement influences outcomes for different population segments.
descriptions.approach: Job postings, recruitment materials, and selection processes are analyzed to identify explicit and implicit criteria used to assess an individual's capacity to work effectively across diverse backgrounds and respond to the needs of varied community groups.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Generalized granuloma annulare

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the effectiveness of a specific treatment for a rare skin condition that affects people under 30. It compares the treatment's results to a similar condition with a different set of symptoms.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a case study to present a patient's experience with a treatment that showed significant improvement. They followed a standard procedure for treating the condition, using a specific medication and monitoring the patient's response.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A pattern of skin lesions with a ring-like structure and central ulceration is observed, and its response to a specific class of medication is evaluated to determine effectiveness in reducing inflammation and improving tissue appearance.
descriptions.approach: A patient's skin condition is monitored over time, and changes in lesion size, symmetry, and tissue integrity are assessed after initiating a standardized treatment regimen.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Agent-based modeling of how national identity affects party preferences in voting.

descriptions.problem: This work estimates how strong feelings about a group's heritage influence people's choices about which group to support. It compares the results to real-world data from a survey.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a computer simulation to model how people's feelings about their heritage affect their choices. They tested how well the simulation matched the real-world data.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: Individuals are modeled to form preferences based on social influence, with their decisions shaped by the strength of their internal sense of belonging to a collective. The resulting choices are compared to observed patterns in human decision-making data.
descriptions.approach: Each individual interacts with peers who share similar views, exchanging ideas that can shift preferences. The influence of a message depends on the individual's existing commitment to the group, and outcomes are aggregated to reflect collective choices.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: General practice research priority setting in Australia: Informing a research agenda to deliver best patient care

descriptions.problem: Estimate the most important factors influencing the quality of services provided by general practice professionals, and identify the most critical research areas to improve these services.
descriptions.approach: Use a systematic review of existing research to identify key factors, and then conduct a survey of general practice professionals to validate and refine the list, and to determine the relative importance of each factor.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A set of research goals is identified from diverse stakeholder input, based on existing knowledge and expert consensus, to guide future investigation efforts in a healthcare setting.
descriptions.approach: A structured review of prior work is conducted, followed by iterative rounds of expert evaluation and refinement to converge on a clear and actionable list of research directions.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Transcriptomic and functional analysis of the oosome, a unique form of germ plasm in the wasp Nasonia vitripennis

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the molecular composition of a unique cellular structure, compares it to a similar structure in another species, and optimizes our understanding of how this structure functions. It explains the variability in the composition of this structure across different species.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a combination of data analysis and functional testing to identify the key molecules involved in the structure's development and function. They compared the molecular composition of the structure in different species to understand the underlying mechanisms.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A set of molecular signals is identified and compared across developmental regions to determine which are selectively concentrated in a specific cellular structure during early development.
descriptions.approach: Transcript levels are measured in distinct tissue fragments, and the expression patterns of localized molecules are tested for functional roles in establishing and maintaining a specialized cell lineage.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Functional Requirements of a Mathematical Model of Muscle Contraction

descriptions.problem: This work estimates and predicts the dynamic behavior of a complex system that generates force over time, taking into account its length and rate of change. It compares and optimizes the system's performance across different conditions.
descriptions.approach: The approach uses a mathematical model that describes the system as a time and length dependent force generator, following a set of rules that relate the system's properties to its behavior.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system's output force is estimated under varying lengths and time scales, capturing how force changes with state and duration. It predicts how internal dynamics influence observable behavior across different conditions.
descriptions.approach: A dynamic framework updates force based on current state and time, using time and length as inputs. It simulates transitions between states through continuous updates, matching observed patterns in response to external and internal changes.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Nicotine smoking concentrations modulate GABAergic synaptic transmission in murine medial prefrontal cortex by activation of α7* and β2* nicotinic receptors

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the effect of a certain substance on the functioning of a specific brain region, comparing its impact on the flow of signals between neurons. It predicts how this substance affects the brain's ability to process information, and optimizes its understanding of this process.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a laboratory experiment to investigate the effect of this substance on the functioning of a specific brain region. They used a specialized technique to measure the flow of signals between neurons in this region, and compared their results to understand the underlying mechanisms.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A substance at a specific concentration is tested to determine how it alters electrical signals in neurons, including both the frequency and timing of spontaneous and evoked responses, depending on the presence or absence of selective receptor blockers.
descriptions.approach: The effect is measured by applying the substance and observing changes in signal amplitude, timing, and frequency under different receptor inhibition conditions, with results interpreted through comparisons across blocked and unblocked receptor pathways.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Influence of Adolescent Gender on Parenting Styles, Autonomy and Self- Esteem among Kenyan Secondary School Students in Wareng Sub-County; Uasin Gishu County

descriptions.problem: The influence of gender on how young people engage in decision-making and their sense of personal value is estimated from self-reported behavioral and emotional patterns in a structured population.
descriptions.approach: Data is collected through standardized questionnaires scored on fixed scales, then analyzed using statistical methods to identify patterns and differences, with comparisons made across groups using mean and variance-based techniques.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: This research aims to understand how the way adults interact with teenagers affects how teenagers feel about themselves and make decisions. It estimates the influence of the teenager's gender on these feelings and behaviors.
descriptions.approach: The researcher uses a method that looks at the relationships between the way adults interact with teenagers and how teenagers feel about themselves and make decisions. The researcher collects data through questionnaires and uses statistical analysis to identify patterns and correlations.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Hampering Herpesviruses HHV-1 and HHV-2 Infection by Extract of Ginkgo biloba (EGb) and Its Phytochemical Constituents

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the effectiveness of a common plant extract in preventing the infection of certain viruses that cause illness in humans. It compares the extract's ability to stop these viruses from infecting cells, and optimizes the extract's concentration to achieve the best results.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a combination of cell culture experiments and chemical analysis to evaluate the extract's effects on the viruses. They tested different concentrations of the extract and identified the specific compounds responsible for its effects.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A mechanism is estimated that inhibits the entry of a pathogen into host cells before it can establish infection, based on biochemical and cellular response data from treated and untreated systems.
descriptions.approach: A compound mixture is applied prior to exposure, and its effect is assessed by measuring inhibition of pathogen attachment and cellular invasion, with specific components identified as key modulators of this interference.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

topic_name: Advancements in PLL and VCO Technologies
title: A 0.83-pJ/Bit 6.4-Gb/s HBM Base Die Receiver Using a 45° Strobe Phase for Energy-Efficient Skew Compensation

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the optimal alignment of two signals to minimize errors, given variations in the signals' timing due to differences in the underlying technology. It aims to optimize the alignment to achieve a high data transfer rate with low energy consumption.
descriptions.approach: The approach uses a mathematical technique to adjust the timing of one signal to match the other, based on a specific phase relationship. This adjustment is done using a digital algorithm that generates a precise timing signal.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system estimates and corrects timing misalignments between incoming data and a reference signal to ensure accurate reception at high speed, using low energy per bit.
descriptions.approach: It uses a phase reference midway between two orthogonal signal states to realign data, applying a digital phase adjustment to maintain synchronization across varying signal conditions.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Believing and Unbelieving in the Dunciad

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the relationship between human beliefs and the nature of the world, comparing and contrasting different ideas about the existence of unseen truth. It aims to explain how these ideas are connected to the power of creative expressions.
descriptions.approach: The approach involves analyzing and linking concepts from theology and creative expressions to understand their ambiguous position in relation to empirical phenomena.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system estimates how deeply a set of ideas is tied to external observations, by analyzing patterns in how they are interpreted across different contexts and compared to known empirical outcomes.
descriptions.approach: The system maps relationships between abstract concepts and observable phenomena, adjusting its interpretation based on consistency with known data and the coherence of connections across diverse interpretive frameworks.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Effects of dietary phosphorus and calcium levels and phytase supplementation on bone metabolism of egg-laying hens

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the effects of varying levels of phosphorus and calcium on the health and development of a certain type of animal, and compares the outcomes of different levels of these minerals. It also explains how a specific substance can alleviate the negative effects of low mineral levels.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a combination of controlled feeding experiments and measurements to study the effects of varying levels of phosphorus and calcium on the health and development of the animals. They tested different levels of a substance that breaks down a specific compound to make minerals more available.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The effect of reducing mineral content in feed on animal performance and skeletal structure is assessed, comparing outcomes across different levels of mineral deficiency and the impact of a supplement that enhances mineral release from organic sources.
descriptions.approach: Animals are fed diets with varying mineral levels and supplemented with a compound that breaks down organic mineral binders. Performance, growth, and structural integrity are monitored, with results analyzed across deficiency severity and supplement dosage.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Human hand neuromechanics for the design of robotic intelligent upper limb prostheses

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the movement of a human hand from data about its surface landmarks, and predicts the forces that control its movement. It also compares the results with real-world measurements to validate its accuracy.
descriptions.approach: The approach involves creating a series of mathematical representations of the hand's movement and forces, and then optimising these representations to best match the real-world data. The process involves identifying the best way to use the data to make accurate predictions and comparisons.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system estimates how body parts move and the internal forces driving those movements, using observed motion and known physical constraints to predict internal forces and spatial relationships across joints and soft tissues.
descriptions.approach: It maps observed motion to internal forces by iteratively adjusting internal force distributions to match observed motion and physical constraints, using optimization to align predicted and measured joint responses across multiple levels of structure.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Efficacy Assessment of Radiofrequency Ablation as a Palliative Pain Treatment in Patients with Painful Metastatic Spinal Lesions: A Systematic Review

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the effectiveness of a treatment for a difficult-to-treat condition that causes significant suffering and reduces quality of life. It compares the outcomes of this treatment to conventional therapies and identifies the patients who may benefit most from this treatment.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a systematic review to gather data from multiple studies, applying a framework to assess the quality of the evidence. They then synthesized the data to draw conclusions about the treatment's effectiveness and safety.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The effectiveness and safety of a minimally invasive procedure for treating chronic, severe pain in patients with advanced disease are assessed, comparing outcomes across different treatment protocols and evaluating the consistency and reliability of reported results.
descriptions.approach: A structured review of multiple studies is conducted, extracting and synthesizing data on patient outcomes using a standardized evaluation framework. Evidence is graded based on study quality and methodological rigor to determine the strength and certainty of observed effects.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Study of the effect of four generic lambda-cyhalothrin pesticides on the reproductive function of male wistar han rats

descriptions.problem: This study estimates the effect of four different concentrations of a certain type of insecticide on the fertility of male rats. It compares the fertility of rats exposed to these concentrations to that of rats not exposed, and optimizes the minimum concentration that does not cause harm.
descriptions.approach: The researchers administered varying amounts of a certain type of insecticide to 20 male rats each, over a period of 11 weeks. They compared the effects of these concentrations to a control group that received a solvent instead.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A quantitative assessment of how varying chemical concentrations affect biological systems over time is performed, measuring changes in physiological and functional outcomes in exposed individuals and their offspring.
descriptions.approach: A controlled exposure regimen is applied over a set duration, with repeated measurements of physiological indicators and offspring production outcomes. A dose-response relationship is established by comparing outcomes across different exposure levels and identifying thresholds where observable changes begin.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Utilización de tres niveles de proteína animal en la producción de cuyes (Cavia porcellus), línea andina, en Ramón Castilla-Usquil

descriptions.problem: This research aims to determine the impact of varying levels of a key nutrient on the growth and productivity of a specific type of farm animal, and to compare the costs and outcomes of different feeding strategies.
descriptions.approach: The study uses a controlled experiment with multiple groups, each receiving a different amount of a nutrient-rich food source, and evaluates the results over a set period of time.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A quantitative assessment is made of how varying levels of a biological supplement in a diet affect growth, feed efficiency, body composition, and overall cost-effectiveness over time.
descriptions.approach: Animals are divided into groups receiving different amounts of the supplement, all fed a consistent base diet. Performance and economic outcomes are measured over a fixed duration, with results analyzed to determine the optimal dosage for cost reduction without compromising output quality.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: A Phase 2 Open-Label Study of Danicopan (ACH-0144471) in Patients with Paroxysmal Nocturnal Hemoglobinuria (PNH) Who Have an Inadequate Response to Eculizumab Monotherapy

descriptions.problem: This study aims to show that a new treatment can help patients with a rare blood disorder who don't respond well to their current treatment. The researchers want to know if this new treatment can improve the patients' condition and reduce the need for blood transfusions.
descriptions.approach: The researchers tested the new treatment in a small group of patients who didn't respond well to their current treatment. They gave the patients different doses of the new treatment and measured how well it worked compared to their current treatment.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The change in a patient's blood cell count and red blood cell survival is estimated over time, compared against baseline and prior treatment outcomes, to assess improvement in blood health and reduction in blood loss events.
descriptions.approach: A treatment is administered in escalating doses based on early biological responses; blood markers and patient-reported fatigue are monitored, and dose adjustments are made to maximize gains in blood cell levels while minimizing adverse effects.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Optimal Estimation of EMG Standard Deviation (EMG$\sigma$ ) in Additive Measurement Noise: Model-Based Derivations and Their Implications

descriptions.problem: The task is to estimate a measure of signal variability from noisy data, and to determine the best way to do this. The goal is to find the most accurate way to estimate this measure, and to understand how it behaves in different situations.
descriptions.approach: The approach is to use a mathematical model to analyze the data and determine the best way to estimate the signal variability. The model is based on the idea that the signal is a random process with some underlying variability, and that the noise is also random and independent of the signal.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A quantity representing the fluctuation intensity of a biological signal is estimated from noisy observations, and its accuracy depends on the signal's modulation and the noise's statistical properties.
descriptions.approach: The signal's fluctuation intensity is estimated by computing the square root of the difference between the signal's squared magnitude and the noise's variance, setting the result to zero if negative, and using this rule for consistent inference.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: An “Orphan” in search of a treatment: Pulmonary alveolar microlithiasis

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the rate of progression of a rare, chronic condition characterized by the accumulation of calcium and phosphate deposits in the lungs, leading to respiratory insufficiency and death. It predicts the outcome of patients with this condition, who often have minimal symptoms until respiratory failure sets in.
descriptions.approach: The researchers use data from published cases to identify the optimal time for referring patients to a life-saving intervention, which has shown benefit in end-stage cases. They analyze the outcomes of patients who have undergone this intervention and compare them to those who have not.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A rare, chronic condition is identified by the presence of spherical, calcified deposits in lung tissue that form over time and are linked to a specific genetic mutation affecting phosphate transport in a key cell type.
descriptions.approach: A model identifies patients with early signs of calcification and minimal symptoms, and recommends intervention only when respiratory function declines significantly, based on imaging and clinical progression.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Item-level psychometrics of a brief self-reported memory problem screening measure in breast cancer survivors

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the reliability and validity of a memory screening tool in a specific population, comparing its performance to other health-related measures. It aims to explain how well the tool works and whether it can be used to screen for memory problems in this group.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used statistical models to analyze data from a large sample of women, applying a combination of factor analysis and regression techniques to examine the tool's performance and identify potential issues.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A set of questions is evaluated to determine how well they measure a specific cognitive experience, assessing how individuals respond across different levels of that experience and whether responses vary systematically by demographic or clinical factors.
descriptions.approach: A statistical model fits individual responses to a latent trait, testing whether the questions behave consistently across different groups and under varying conditions of the trait being measured.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Learning from Bamboo: Building a Bamboo Structure Collectively

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the structural integrity of a structure made from a strong, fast-growing, and lightweight material, and compares it to a theoretical design. It predicts the optimal way to harvest and use this material.
descriptions.approach: The researchers define the material's characteristics and design process, then describe the learning and building process, using a systemic thinking approach to understand the experience.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A group of individuals collaboratively designs and constructs a durable, lightweight structure using a rapidly growing, locally available natural material, aiming to optimize stability and sustainability through iterative, hands-on experience.
descriptions.approach: The structure is assembled using interlocking joints secured by a simple, low-tech binding technique, with decisions refined through repeated testing, observation, and group feedback during the building process.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

subfield: Physical Therapy, Sports Therapy and Rehabilitation
title: FALLS AND MOTOR VEHICLE COLLISIONS: A LONGITUDINAL INVESTIGATION OF OLDER DRIVERS

descriptions.problem: A model estimates how a past event affecting physical stability influences the likelihood of a future driving-related incident over time, using repeated observations across a long period.
descriptions.approach: The model tracks changes in behavior and physical condition over time, adjusting risk predictions based on prior instability and frequency of driving activity, using statistical methods that account for repeated measurements in the same individuals.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Conceptual mechanism provisions for making and implementation of managerial decisions

descriptions.problem: This work estimates and predicts the quality and effectiveness of decisions based on the level of competence of management personnel. It compares the performance of different levels of management and optimizes the decision-making process.
descriptions.approach: The researcher uses a multi-factor causal model to analyze the relationship between decision-making and the process of action. The approach involves developing a hierarchy of goals to ensure the adoption and implementation of decisions.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system is designed to map how decisions are formed and carried out across different levels of an entity, linking inputs, goals, and actions through a structured sequence of interdependent stages.
descriptions.approach: A hierarchical model links actions to outcomes across levels, where each stage depends on the prior one, and feedback loops ensure alignment with overarching objectives and environmental conditions.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: “Stories we tell”: queer narratives in Kenya

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the nature of how people in Kenya express and experience their lives, particularly in relation to their desires and identities, by comparing and contrasting different aspects of their lives, such as law, religion, and cultural codes.
descriptions.approach: It uses a framework that examines how these aspects are produced, shared, and understood, and how they relate to each other, in order to gain a deeper understanding of people's experiences and identities.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A pattern of lived experiences is examined to reveal how individuals construct personal identities amid conflicting societal expectations and institutional rules.
descriptions.approach: A narrative framework is applied to analyze how individuals articulate their lives through language, memory, and social interaction, emphasizing the process of meaning-making in response to external pressures and internal reflections.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

topic_name: Synthesis and pharmacology of benzodiazepine derivatives
title: Site-Specific Conjugation of the Indolinobenzodiazepine DGN549 to Antibodies Affords Antibody–Drug Conjugates with an Improved Therapeutic Index as Compared with Lysine Conjugation

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the therapeutic index of a new treatment by comparing its effects on two different models. It predicts the benefits of a new treatment method by comparing its results to a standard method.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a systematic approach to compare the effects of two different methods of attaching a new medicine to a protein. They followed a procedure that involved attaching the medicine to the protein in a specific way, and then testing its effects on two different models.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A metric is estimated that quantifies the balance between effectiveness and safety in a targeted therapeutic delivery system, comparing outcomes across different chemical attachment strategies to a biological macromolecule.
descriptions.approach: A defined chemical pathway is used to attach a cytotoxic agent to a macromolecule at a single, controlled site, and the resulting performance is evaluated under varying biological conditions and disease contexts.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Bridge Flaps: A Hybrid Family of Bipedicled Flaps for the Forehead, Temple, and Scalp: Experience With 103 Cases

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the best way to reconstruct medium-sized areas of skin that have been damaged, using a combination of the skin's own tissues and the tissues of other areas. It compares different methods to see which one works best and is most reliable.
descriptions.approach: The researchers looked at a large database of past cases to see how well this method worked, and they detailed the steps to perform the procedure, including how to dissect and prepare the tissues.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A method is developed to reconstruct medium-sized tissue losses in regions with complex surface contours, using adjacent tissue to restore natural shape and continuity without requiring external grafts or staged procedures.
descriptions.approach: A single-step procedure transfers tissue from a nearby region, preserving its original boundaries and vascular supply, using a hybrid design that combines multiple vascular pathways to ensure stable and durable tissue survival.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: SBT and hope

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the level of positive change that individuals expect to occur as a result of their own efforts, and compares this to their confidence in their ability to achieve that change. It aims to explain the relationship between these two factors and their impact on outcomes.
