descriptions.approach: Blood samples are processed to isolate plasma, then tested for a specific antibody response. Clinical symptoms and infection levels are recorded and analyzed to determine associations between immune activity, symptom occurrence, and infection status.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

topic_name: Synthesis and pharmacology of benzodiazepine derivatives
title: Theoretical Study on the Mechanism of Alkylation At 0-6 Position of Guanine by Temozolomide and Bitc-Temozolomide

descriptions.problem: This research aims to understand how a certain type of cancer treatment works by studying how it affects a specific part of a molecule in cells. It wants to know how this treatment affects the molecule and whether it can be improved.
descriptions.approach: The researchers use a computer simulation to model how the treatment works by changing the molecule's shape and properties. They calculate the effects of the treatment on the molecule's structure and properties using a set of rules and formulas.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The mechanism by which a drug modifies a specific site on a biological molecule is investigated, focusing on the interaction dynamics and electronic features that influence the stability and reactivity of the resulting complex.
descriptions.approach: A computational model simulates molecular geometry and electronic distribution to evaluate binding preferences, using energy minimization and surface property analysis to predict favored interaction sites and reaction pathways.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

topic_name: Synthesis and pharmacology of benzodiazepine derivatives
title: Expansion of diazepine heterocyclic chemical space via sequential Knoevenagel condensation-intramolecular aza-Wittig reaction: 2-acyl-4-aryl-5 H -pyrrolo[1,2- d ][1,4]diazepines

descriptions.problem: A new class of fused ring systems is synthesized by combining two modular starting units through a two-step transformation, enabling access to complex, polycyclic structures with defined substitution patterns.
descriptions.approach: Two components are joined via a condensation reaction, followed by a ring-forming reaction under controlled conditions that reduce a reactive group and promote cyclization into a closed, strained ring system.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Indigenous Technical Knowledge (ITK) inCapture Fisheries: A Case Study in VypeenIsland of Ernakulam District

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the population of a certain group, compares their living conditions to the general population, and explains their economic status. It also predicts the value of their production and compares it to the general population's living standards.
descriptions.approach: The researchers use data from a census and government reports to gather information about the group's population, living conditions, and economic status. They then use this data to estimate the value of their production and compare it to the general population's living standards.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A pattern of human activity in a dynamic environment is observed over time, involving local knowledge passed through generations to manage resource use and predict outcomes under changing conditions.
descriptions.approach: A system maps recurring behaviors in response to environmental cues, using historical records and observational data to identify consistent rules governing resource access, timing, and success rates across generations.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: The blood cerebrospinal fluid barrier orchestrates immunosurveillance, immunoprotection, and immunopathology in the central nervous system

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the role of a specific barrier in controlling the entry of immune cells and other substances into a protected area, comparing different types of immune responses and changes in the area.
descriptions.approach: It uses data from the protected area and the immune cells that enter it, following a procedure that involves recruiting, skewing, and suppressing immune cells based on the barrier's unique properties.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system regulates the entry and behavior of immune cells based on signals from a fluid-filled compartment, adjusting their function to either defend against threats or prevent excessive responses.
descriptions.approach: Immune cells are guided through a tightly controlled interface where physical and chemical cues determine whether they become active defenders or regulatory mediators, based on real-time environmental signals.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Management of Scarring Following Aesthetic Surgery

descriptions.problem: Estimate the minimum visibility of a mark on a person's body over time, and compare it to different factors such as patient preparation, technique choice, and post-care. The goal is to minimize the mark's impact on the person's appearance.
descriptions.approach: Use historical data on mark visibility to develop a predictive model that considers patient preparation, technique choice, and post-care. The model should be able to forecast mark visibility over a 6-week to 6-month period.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A dynamic process is monitored over time to predict how outcomes evolve based on pre-existing conditions and interventions applied before and after a procedure.
descriptions.approach: A sequence of stages is tracked with time-dependent feedback, and decisions are adjusted in real-time based on patient response, using historical patterns to guide future actions and support long-term stability.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Roles of Fungal Endophytes and Viruses in Mediating Drought Stress Tolerance in Plants

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the impact of certain types of beneficial organisms on the ability of certain organisms to withstand stress caused by lack of water. It also compares the effectiveness of different types of beneficial organisms in helping the organisms withstand this stress.
descriptions.approach: The approach involves gathering and analyzing data on the effects of these beneficial organisms on the organisms' ability to withstand stress. The data is analyzed using robust statistical methods to identify patterns and relationships.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system is evaluated to determine how specific symbiotic organisms influence an organism's ability to withstand environmental challenges that reduce its performance and survival.
descriptions.approach: A synthesis of existing evidence is constructed by analyzing physiological and molecular responses across different stress conditions, then comparing outcomes when symbiotic agents are present versus absent, to identify patterns and mechanisms of resilience.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Genetic sources of economically valuable characteristics for breeding yellow lupine

descriptions.problem: This work identifies and selects the most valuable characteristics from a large collection of genetic material to improve the quality of a specific type of crop. It estimates the potential benefits of these characteristics and compares them to the characteristics of existing crops.
descriptions.approach: The researchers use a combination of data and evidence to evaluate the genetic material. They follow a procedure that involves screening, selection, and comparison of the characteristics to identify the most valuable ones.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A set of traits related to growth efficiency and environmental resilience is identified across diverse genetic materials. The goal is to determine which sources best support performance under varying conditions and predict their combined effects on yield and stability.
descriptions.approach: A systematic evaluation compares genetic variants based on performance metrics across environments. Each variant is scored for its ability to maintain performance under stress and in resource-limited settings, using historical observations and phenotypic records.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Do Older People Expect Reciprocity When Providing Care? Evidence From a National Cohort

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the motivation behind providing help to family members, comparing the influence of helping with household chores and taking care of grandchildren on the likelihood of receiving help in return. It also examines the impact of helping one's own parents on the likelihood of receiving help from one's children.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a statistical model to analyze data from a large survey, testing the relationships between helping family members and the likelihood of receiving help in return. They found that helping with household chores and taking care of grandchildren increased the likelihood of receiving help, while helping one's own parents decreased it.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A pattern of behavior is assessed based on past involvement in family-related activities and its influence on future requests for support from family members.
descriptions.approach: A statistical model links past interactions with family members to future requests for support, adjusting for regional differences and using multiple indicators of involvement to determine the strength and direction of influence.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Large-Scale Shape Transformations of a Sphere Made of a Magnetoactive Elastomer

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the deformation of a spherical object made of a material that changes shape when exposed to a magnetic field. It predicts how this material will behave under different conditions and compares its behavior to a similar material that is known to change shape in a certain way.
descriptions.approach: The researchers built a numerical model to simulate the behavior of this material under different conditions. They used this model to show that the material's shape changes in a way that is different from what was previously thought.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A material's shape under uniform external force is estimated, particularly how it deforms from a sphere to non-symmetric forms at small and moderate force levels.
descriptions.approach: A numerical model simulates incremental deformation, updating the shape based on internal stress distribution and material response, revealing deviations from simple elongation patterns.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Eco-Acoustic Indices to Evaluate Soundscape Degradation Due to Human Intrusion

descriptions.problem: This work aims to create a tool to evaluate the quality of environments and detect early signs of environmental stress caused by human activity. It estimates the impact of human presence on natural environments and predicts the effects of increasing human activity.
descriptions.approach: The analysis uses a combination of acoustic and ecological indices to distinguish between different environments. It follows a procedure of data analysis and comparison to identify patterns and correlations between human-generated noise and species abundance.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A metric is derived to quantify how changes in ambient noise levels correlate with the diversity and activity of living organisms in a given space.
descriptions.approach: Audio data is processed to extract patterns in background noise and biological vocalizations. These patterns are transformed into numerical indicators that reflect the balance between human-generated noise and natural vocal activity over time.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Redefining the Debate Over Reputation and Credibility in International Security

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the importance of a certain quality in international interactions, compares the effectiveness of different approaches to understanding this quality, and optimizes the conditions under which this quality is most influential. It explains how people make judgments about this quality based on various factors.
descriptions.approach: The authors use a framework to evaluate collective progress, critique existing research, and suggest future research directions. They follow a procedure that involves analyzing and comparing different studies to identify gaps in current understanding and propose new avenues for investigation.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The system estimates how actors interpret the reliability of others based on observable behaviors and contextual cues, comparing outcomes across different scenarios and conditions.
descriptions.approach: It evaluates patterns in behavior over time and across situations, applying rules that weigh recent actions against historical consistency to predict how others will respond to future interactions.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

topic_name: Psychiatric care and mental health services
title: The Changing Landscape of Community Mental Health Care: Availability of Treatment Services in National Data, 2010–2017

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the availability of services for people who are struggling with substance use and suicidal thoughts, and compares it to the past to see if it has changed over time. It also predicts what might happen in the future based on past trends.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used data from a large survey to examine changes in the number of facilities offering these services over a 7-year period. They looked at the proportion of facilities that offered these services and compared it to the past to see if it had changed.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The proportion of health facilities offering emergency psychiatric support and substance use interventions is estimated over time, comparing shifts in service provision across different types of care settings.
descriptions.approach: A statistical model analyzes trends in service availability by fitting observed rates to time-based patterns, adjusting for facility characteristics and regional variations to detect significant changes in service delivery.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Case report of aplastic anaemia detected in third trimester of pregnancy: dilemmas faced

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the likelihood of a rare condition occurring in a specific situation, compares the effectiveness of different treatments, and explains the outcome of a challenging case. It predicts the outcome of a treatment and optimizes the care of a patient with a serious condition.
descriptions.approach: The researchers followed a multidisciplinary approach, using a combination of supportive care and a specific treatment to manage the condition. They monitored the patient's condition closely and adjusted the treatment as needed to achieve a good outcome.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A dynamic physiological state is monitored over time, with key indicators showing abrupt and divergent trends. The system's response to an intervention is evaluated against baseline and expected outcomes to determine effectiveness.
descriptions.approach: A longitudinal tracking system records and compares vital parameters. An intervention is introduced and its impact is assessed through changes in parameter stability and recovery patterns over time.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Future Traffic Prediction from Short Period Traffic Data

descriptions.problem: This work predicts future population growth and vehicle numbers from historical data, using a combination of surveys and statistical analysis to estimate the impact on road usage.
descriptions.approach: It uses historical data on vehicle registrations, population, and economic indicators to calculate growth rates, then applies these rates to predict future numbers, taking into account design standards for road capacity.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A long-term trend in vehicle volume is estimated from short-term observations and auxiliary demographic and economic indicators across a region.
descriptions.approach: A growth pattern is derived from daily vehicle counts and population trends, then adjusted using a power-based fit. Future volumes are projected annually, and the resulting load on a transportation corridor is assessed under different lane capacities.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: LSTM-Based Dynamic Frequency Prediction

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the future state of a system's stability, specifically the frequency at which it operates, based on historical data. It aims to predict this state to inform decisions about how to maintain stability.
descriptions.approach: The system uses a type of artificial neural network to make predictions. It processes data about the system's past behavior, including factors such as energy usage and grid capacity, to make a forecast.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system estimates how a critical operational variable changes over time in response to sudden disturbances, using historical patterns and temporal dependencies to forecast future behavior under stress.
descriptions.approach: It analyzes past behavior at different time lags, identifies key influencing factors, and applies a model that learns long-term temporal patterns to generate accurate future estimates based on recent and delayed observations.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: CONCRETIZATION OF LAW: LEGAL FORMS

descriptions.problem: This research aims to evaluate the effectiveness of a set of rules in protecting the rights and freedoms of individuals, and to identify the mechanisms that make these rules more specific and enforceable.
descriptions.approach: The researchers use a method that involves analyzing the rules within a system, and tracing the uncertainty created by the person who created the rules to understand how they are implemented and enforced.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system of rules is evaluated over time to assess how well they adapt to changing societal conditions and operational demands. The effectiveness of these rules is measured by how consistently they are applied across different levels of governance and in response to evolving circumstances.
descriptions.approach: A hierarchical structure is used to break down broad policy directives into more specific, actionable guidelines. Each level refines and adjusts the previous one based on real-world feedback, economic, social, and procedural inputs.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Ear-Bot: Locust Ear-on-a-Chip Bio-Hybrid Platform

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the performance of a biological device in response to sound pulses, predicts how it will behave over time, and compares its performance to that of man-made devices. It aims to optimise the use of this biological device in a larger system.
descriptions.approach: The researchers use a biological device to detect sound pulses, record neural signals, and control the motion of a larger system. They follow a procedure where the neural signals are processed and used to make decisions about the system's motion.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system detects and responds to acoustic stimuli by translating vibrational inputs into physical movement patterns.
descriptions.approach: A biological sensory unit is interfaced with a mechanical system; neural activity triggered by sound pulses is captured and mapped to control parameters that drive motion in real time.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Not My Literary History!

descriptions.problem: A set of creative works is analyzed to identify patterns and structures that challenge established norms in how knowledge is organized and taught. The focus is on uncovering underrepresented voices and unconventional forms that resist traditional categorization and authority.
descriptions.approach: A systematic review groups diverse creative outputs by style, origin, and thematic content. It then maps deviations from dominant frameworks to reveal alternative ways of structuring meaning and influence within cultural education.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the extent to which a particular field of study has overlooked or undervalued the contributions of women, and compares the impact of different approaches to understanding this field. It also aims to explain why certain perspectives have been overlooked and optimizes the representation of underrepresented voices.
descriptions.approach: The work uses a list of key figures to illustrate the difference between traditional and avant-garde approaches to the field, and highlights the importance of considering a broader range of perspectives and voices.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Cumulative Adversity and Depressive Symptoms: Optimism as a Moderator

descriptions.problem: The strength of a negative influence across a lifetime of adverse experiences is estimated and evaluated in relation to a protective psychological trait that mitigates its effect on mental well-being.
descriptions.approach: A statistical model is built to assess how the effect of cumulative adverse exposures changes depending on the level of a protective psychological factor, using regression with interaction terms to quantify the modifying effect.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: This study estimates the relationship between exposure to various types of stressful events and the likelihood of experiencing negative mental health outcomes. It also compares the impact of these events on mental health outcomes and seeks to explain the role of a certain mindset in mitigating these effects.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a statistical model to analyze data from a large sample of individuals, examining the relationship between exposure to stressful events and mental health outcomes. They also tested the hypothesis that a particular mindset can buffer the negative effects of these events on mental health.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Humic-like acid derived from 1,2-naphthoquinone

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the properties of a new compound created by oxidizing a specific molecule in an alkaline solution. It predicts the compound's behavior and characteristics, comparing them to those of a naturally occurring similar compound.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a chemical reaction to transform the molecule, measuring the amount of the new compound produced. They then analyzed the compound's properties, such as its ability to store energy, and compared them to those of the naturally occurring compound.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A process is designed to generate complex organic materials from a simple quinone precursor using oxygen under basic conditions, with the output matching natural organic materials in composition and redox behavior across varying pH levels.
descriptions.approach: A chemical transformation is initiated by exposing a quinone to oxygen in a high-pH environment, followed by analysis of its molecular structure, redox activity, and magnetic properties as a function of pH to confirm structural and functional similarity to naturally occurring organic matter.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Umbilical cord‑derived mesenchymal stem cells exert anti‑fibrotic action on hypertrophic scar‑derived fibroblasts in co‑culture by inhibiting the activation of the TGF β1/Smad3 pathway

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the effect of a certain type of cell on the growth and behavior of another type of cell, and compares the results to a control group. It aims to explain how this cell affects the growth and behavior of the other cell, and whether this could be useful in treating a certain skin disease.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a special way of growing the cells together, and measured how the cells behaved and grew. They looked at how the cells divided, how they died, and how they moved, and also looked at the genes and proteins that were turned on or off.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The effect of a therapeutic cell type on a disease-driving cell population is assessed by measuring changes in cell growth, movement, and the production of key structural proteins associated with tissue overgrowth.
descriptions.approach: Cells are grown together in a shared environment. Growth, movement, and protein output are monitored over time. Molecular signals linked to tissue overgrowth are measured to determine if the therapeutic effect alters the activation of a key regulatory pathway.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Preliminary Development of Cold Spray Procedures for Nickel Aluminum Bronze Casting Repair

descriptions.problem: This work aims to improve the repair of a specific type of material used in naval applications, which is prone to degradation when repaired using traditional methods. The goal is to estimate the optimal conditions for a new repair method that maintains the material's performance.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a trial-and-error approach to find the best conditions for the new repair method, analyzing the results of each test to determine the optimal parameters. They plan to use these parameters to simulate and test the repair method's performance in the future.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A set of conditions is optimized to restore material integrity to a component exposed to harsh environmental degradation, based on measurements of internal structure, void content, and bond strength between layers.
descriptions.approach: A cycle of parameter adjustment is performed, evaluating deposited material properties through microscopic and mechanical analysis, until a stable and durable repair configuration is achieved.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Secreted protein acidic and rich in cysteine (SPARC) and vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) in endometrial cancer versus normal endometrial tissue

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the level of a protein in two types of tissue samples, comparing the levels in a disease state to a normal state. It predicts the relationship between the protein levels and the growth of new blood vessels in the disease state.
descriptions.approach: The researchers took tissue samples from 15 patients, extracted the genetic material, and used a special test to measure the levels of a specific protein and a related growth factor. They then compared the levels in the disease state to the normal state and looked for patterns.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A quantitative relationship is estimated between the expression levels of two biomolecules in a tissue sample and its surrounding microenvironment, assessing how changes in one correlate with changes in the other across multiple patient samples.
descriptions.approach: A statistical model compares expression levels across paired tissue samples, using reverse transcription and real-time amplification to measure relative abundance, then evaluates the strength and direction of association between the two biomolecules.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Family and cultural resources that affect an applicant’s acceptance at university

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the impact of family and social resources on the acceptance of higher learning institutions. It compares the effects of various factors, such as parental education, family income, and family motivation, on university admission.
descriptions.approach: The study uses a combination of survey data, statistical analysis, and secondary research to analyze the relationships between family and social resources and university acceptance. It follows a theoretical framework that considers the interplay between individual and family resources.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A model estimates how inherited and learned traits from a household influence an individual's chances of being selected for a structured learning program, based on observed behaviors and household characteristics.
descriptions.approach: The model evaluates household traits like income, parental background, and engagement in structured activities, then maps how these traits correlate with selection outcomes through statistical analysis of reported behaviors and outcomes.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Therapeutic anti-glioma effect of the combined action of PCSK inhibitor with the anti-tumoral factors secreted by Poly (I:C)-stimulated macrophages

descriptions.problem: A system's response to a stimulus is measured to determine how effectively it suppresses uncontrolled cell growth and reprograms surrounding cells toward a protective state.
descriptions.approach: A compound is combined with a signal that activates immune-like cells to release protective factors. The combined effect is tested in a complex environment to assess suppression of growth and reprogramming of cell behavior.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the effectiveness of a new treatment strategy that combines a specific type of protein with a substance that stimulates the immune system to fight cancer cells. It aims to improve the immune system's ability to recognize and attack cancer cells.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a combination of laboratory tests and experiments to evaluate the treatment strategy. They analyzed data from mass spectrometry and biological assays to understand how the substance affects the immune system's behavior.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Psychometric properties of the Turkish version of “Healthy Eating and Physical Activity Self‐Efficacy and Recall Questionnaires for Children”

descriptions.problem: This study estimates the reliability and validity of a questionnaire to measure the ability of a group to make good food choices and engage in regular physical activity, using data from 233 students aged 9-14.
descriptions.approach: The researchers collected data through a survey and a questionnaire, then used statistical methods to evaluate the data and determine the questionnaire's reliability and validity.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A set of behavioral indicators is assessed to determine consistency and reliability across a group of individuals using structured self-report data and demographic information.
descriptions.approach: The data is analyzed through statistical modeling to evaluate internal consistency, factor structure, and relationships between items. A model is fitted to verify that observed patterns align with expected underlying constructs, ensuring the tool performs consistently across different groups.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

subfield: Physical Therapy, Sports Therapy and Rehabilitation
title: Komparativna analiza nacionalnih kurikuluma tjelesne i zdravstvene kulture primarnog obrazovanja u Europi

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the level of physical and health education in primary education levels across different countries, comparing the emphasis on these areas and the quality of education for those who value them. It predicts the outcomes of countries that prioritize physical and health education, and explains the differences in education quality.
descriptions.approach: The procedure involves comparing data on physical and health education content, timing, and quality across different countries, using a combination of legislative and educational standards to assess the emphasis on these areas.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system evaluates how well educational programs promote holistic development through structured, outdoor-based activities, comparing the balance and emphasis given to physical, personal, and social growth across different national systems.
descriptions.approach: It analyzes time allocation, content diversity, and instructional focus by mapping activity types and their integration into daily learning schedules, using documented program structures and official guidelines as input.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Effects of Drying Methods and Onion Bulb Variety on Physicochemical and Functional Properties of Onion Powder

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the effects of different methods on the quality of a food product. It compares the quality of the product after being treated with different methods, and optimizes the method that produces the best results. The results are based on data from two types of food.
descriptions.approach: The research uses a combination of methods to analyze the quality of the food product. It follows a procedure where the food product is first treated with different methods, and then its quality is analyzed and compared.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A set of processing conditions is evaluated to determine how they influence the stability, solubility, and chemical composition of a food-based material, with variations observed across different types of raw material and processing methods.
descriptions.approach: A series of conditions are applied to a raw material, and the resulting outcomes are measured across multiple attributes. These outcomes are then compared across different processing techniques and raw material types to identify patterns and optimal configurations.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Evaluation of the ventriculocholecystic shunt—an overview of present practice in adult and pediatric hydrocephalus

descriptions.problem: A clinical decision is made regarding the suitability of a bodily cavity for diverting a fluid that accumulates in the brain to manage a neurological condition affecting cognitive and motor function.
descriptions.approach: A systematic review of published outcomes is conducted, comparing long-term results across different anatomical sites used for fluid drainage, evaluating complications, effectiveness, and patient survival over time.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The task is to evaluate the effectiveness of a medical device used to divert excess fluid from the brain, and to compare it to other options. The goal is to determine if this device is a viable alternative for patients who cannot use a more commonly used device.
descriptions.approach: The approach involves analyzing data from modern literature to assess the current status of this device as a treatment option. The analysis aims to summarize available information and evaluate the device's potential as a viable alternative.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Socioeconomic status and cardiovascular health in the COVID-19 pandemic

descriptions.problem: A pattern of health outcomes is assessed across different social conditions, evaluating how exposure to stressors and economic instability influence the likelihood of adverse health events in vulnerable populations.
descriptions.approach: A model maps social conditions to health outcomes by analyzing trends in stress exposure, access to resources, and behavioral patterns, then identifies interventions that improve access, reduce risk factors, and support long-term well-being.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: This work aims to understand how the social and economic status of individuals affects their overall health and risk of serious illnesses, such as heart problems, during a time of widespread illness and economic hardship. It also seeks to identify ways to address these issues and reduce avoidable deaths.
descriptions.approach: The study uses data to compare the health outcomes of people from different social and economic backgrounds, and to predict the impact of stress, economic recession, and quarantine on mental health. It suggests that targeted interventions, such as healthier workplaces and restrictions on unhealthy food and drink, could help reduce these risks.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: What is boredom proneness? A comparison of three characterizations

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the relationship between a tendency to experience a certain state of mind (e.g., feeling uninterested or uninspired) and various measures of well-being, such as life satisfaction and emotional state. It also compares the strength of these relationships across different characterizations of this state of mind.
descriptions.approach: The researchers tested these relationships using data from two large samples, comparing the strength of associations between the state of mind and well-being measures across three different ways of characterizing this state of mind.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A pattern of individual differences is assessed across three distinct interpretations: how often a person experiences a sense of disengagement, how strongly they feel it, and their overall evaluation of daily experiences as unstimulating. The strength and consistency of these interpretations are evaluated in relation to other outcomes related to well-being.
descriptions.approach: Three distinct dimensions are measured and compared across different groups and settings. Each dimension is tested for its ability to predict patterns in outcomes related to personal fulfillment and daily functioning, with emphasis on which dimension shows the most consistent and strong links.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: RETRACTED ARTICLE: Knockdown of circRNA_0007534 suppresses the tumorigenesis of cervical cancer via miR-206/GREM1 axis

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the effect of a specific molecule on the growth and death of a particular type of abnormal growth, and compares its impact on the growth and death of these abnormal growths in different conditions. It also explains how this molecule affects the growth and death of these abnormal growths.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a combination of experiments to measure the levels of the molecule and its effects on the growth and death of these abnormal growths. They used various techniques to analyze the relationships between the molecule and other molecules involved in the growth and death of these abnormal growths.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system's behavior is inferred from molecular interactions where a regulatory RNA sequesters a microRNA, leading to changes in a downstream gene's expression level and cellular outcomes like growth suppression and programmed cell death.
descriptions.approach: A regulatory network is mapped by measuring expression levels of key components, testing how altering one element affects another through direct binding, and validating functional outcomes in living models through controlled experimental conditions.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Internal and External Challenges to Culpability

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the importance of a certain aspect of human nature in determining a key concept, and compares it to new evidence from a different field. It also predicts how this concept will be affected by recent findings in a related field.
descriptions.approach: The approach involves maintaining a certain idea about human nature, and then evaluating how it will be impacted by new research findings and evidence from a different area of study.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The system estimates how strongly human actions depend on internal conditions and external influences, comparing the influence of internal processes to environmental factors in shaping behavior.
descriptions.approach: It models behavior as a function of internal dynamics and external inputs, using observed patterns to determine the extent to which decisions reflect internal states or are shaped by external conditions.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Principals Managing the Expectations of Instructional Leadership

descriptions.problem: This research aims to understand how individuals in a complex organization balance multiple responsibilities and adapt to changing needs. It seeks to identify the key factors that influence their ability to do so.
descriptions.approach: The study uses a combination of interviews and coding to analyze the processes and structures established by key figures in the organization. It follows a qualitative approach, focusing on themes and patterns in the data to inform recommendations for improvement.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A central figure in an educational setting is assessed on their ability to coordinate diverse responsibilities while maintaining focus on improving learning outcomes through consistent, adaptive practices.
descriptions.approach: A structured process is developed where multiple stakeholders contribute to decision-making, and regular feedback loops are established to adjust strategies in response to evolving conditions and performance indicators.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: A case of acute myocardial infarction in a patient with congenital atresia of the left coronary artery

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the likelihood of a rare heart condition in a patient, based on their age and medical history. It predicts the patient's heart condition and compares it to a normal heart condition.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a combination of clinical observations, laboratory tests, and modern medical technologies to understand the patient's condition. They followed a step-by-step procedure to identify the underlying cause of the patient's heart condition.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A sudden onset of cardiac damage is observed in a patient with a rare anatomical variation of the heart's blood supply, and the link between this variation and a viral infection is investigated to explain the triggering event.
descriptions.approach: The patient's medical history, lab results, and imaging data are analyzed to trace the sequence of events, with a focus on identifying patterns between a known infectious agent and the timing of tissue damage.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Synthesis and stability of single-phase chalcopyrite – a potential reference material for key investigations in chemistry and metallurgical engineering

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the stability of a specific compound under various conditions, comparing its properties to those of other materials. It predicts the optimal conditions for the compound's existence and explains its behavior using data from different experiments.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a combination of experiments to gather data, including measurements of the compound's structure and properties at different temperatures. They then analyzed this data to identify patterns and trends, which helped them understand the compound's behavior and make predictions about its stability.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A material's phase composition is determined from its elemental ratios and thermal behavior, with a specific phase forming only within a narrow range of composition and exhibiting a transition in atomic arrangement at a defined temperature.
descriptions.approach: A model maps elemental proportions to phase stability, detecting a structural change at a threshold temperature and identifying a continuous mixing state beyond that point, based on temperature-dependent structural measurements.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Adaptive behaviour and learning in slime moulds: the role of oscillations

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the role of a specific pattern in the brain-like network of a certain type of living being, which uses information from past experiences to adjust its behavior. It compares this pattern to the brain's own way of organizing activity.
descriptions.approach: The researchers describe the network's behavior and its patterns of activity, and then explore how these patterns might be related to learning and memory. They use this information to evaluate the network's ability to process information and sustain learning.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system adapts its structure and dynamics based on past interactions, adjusting how information flows through interconnected pathways in response to environmental inputs.
descriptions.approach: The system maintains and modifies internal patterns of activity across a network, where the timing and synchronization of these patterns influence how information is processed and stored over time.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: EVALUATION OF THE EFFECT OF PIPER BETLE L. LEAVES EXTRACT AGAINST CLONIDINE-INDUCED CATALEPSY AND MILK-INDUCED LEUKOCYTOSIS AND EOSINOPHILIA IN MICE

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the effect of a certain substance on the body's response to a specific condition, comparing the results to a standard treatment. It also predicts the outcome of a certain situation and explains the underlying mechanisms.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a combination of chemical tests and animal experiments to evaluate the substance's effect. They followed a procedure that involved preparing a substance, testing its chemical properties, and then administering it to animals to see how it affected their response to a specific condition.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A substance is tested for its ability to reduce behavioral immobility and suppress abnormal increases in white blood cell counts and specific immune cell levels in a living organism exposed to a stressor.
descriptions.approach: The substance is administered before exposure to a stressor. Behavioral and immune responses are measured over time. The results are compared across groups to determine if the substance reduces the magnitude and duration of the stress-induced effects.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Domestic Air Travel Demand Forecast for SAUDIA Airlines

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the future demand for travel within a specific region, based on historical data and various factors that influence demand. It aims to provide a long-term plan for the region's transportation needs.
descriptions.approach: The approach involves analyzing historical data to identify the most influential factors, and then using various statistical and machine learning techniques to predict future demand. The goal is to develop a model that can accurately estimate future demand and inform business decisions.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system estimates future volume of travel activity based on historical patterns and key influencing variables, identifying which variables most strongly affect the trend over time.
descriptions.approach: It evaluates historical data through statistical and machine learning models, testing combinations of variables to find the most accurate prediction. The best result comes from a method that iteratively selects and refines the most impactful variables for long-term trend projection.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Market Allocations under Ambiguity: A Survey [Allocations des biens et ambiguïté : une revue de la littérature]

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the impact of uncertainty on market behavior, comparing theoretical models of decision-making under uncertainty to experimental evidence. It aims to explain how these models affect the optimal arrangement of resources in a competitive market setting.
descriptions.approach: The researchers start with a theoretical result and test its applicability to a competitive market. They then explore the implications of these models on market behavior, including the potential for non-revelation of information and optimal arrangements.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system predicts how agents choose among options when they lack precise knowledge of outcomes, and how these choices affect overall market outcomes and information sharing.
descriptions.approach: It models agent behavior using two rules: one where decisions average outcomes with varying confidence, and another where agents pick the most favorable outcome among possible beliefs. It then simulates how these rules influence group-level decisions and market dynamics over time.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

topic_name: Synthesis and pharmacology of benzodiazepine derivatives
title: Synthesis and biological evaluation of the new ring system benzo[ f ]pyrimido[1,2- d ][1,2,3]triazolo[1,5- a ][1,4]diazepine and its cycloalkane and cycloalkene condensed analogues

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the effectiveness of a new compound against five types of cancer cells, comparing its performance to that of existing treatments. It aims to identify the compound's potential as a new cancer treatment.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a combination of chemical synthesis and biological testing to evaluate the compound's properties. They applied a specific reaction sequence to create the new compound and then tested its effects on cancer cells.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A new fused ring structure is designed and synthesized, with its biological effect measured across multiple cancer cell types to assess its ability to inhibit uncontrolled cell growth.
descriptions.approach: A reaction pathway is reversed to build the target structure efficiently, and the resulting compounds are evaluated for their impact on cell survival under conditions mimicking disease progression.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Combining Normal/Reversed-Phase HPTLC with Univariate Calibration for the Piperine Quantification with Traditional and Ultrasound-Assisted Extracts of Various Food Spices of Piper nigrum L. under Green Analytical Chemistry Viewpoint

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the amount of a specific compound in different types of food samples, comparing the results to a traditional method. It also predicts the environmental impact of a technique and compares the effectiveness of two different methods.
descriptions.approach: The technique uses a combination of data from two different methods to make these estimates and predictions. It follows a procedure that involves applying a mathematical model to the data to make the comparisons and predictions.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A quantity in a complex sample is estimated from chemical separation data, comparing results across two different extraction methods to determine which produces a higher concentration of the target compound.
descriptions.approach: A separation process is applied to extract and resolve components in a sample. A simple calibration model relates signal intensity to concentration, and the performance of two extraction conditions is evaluated using a metric that scores environmental impact.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Na2Nb8O21 microcrystalline and ceramics prepared by molten salt synthesis

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the effect of varying salt content on the crystal structure and morphologies of a specific material, and compares the results to determine the optimal salt content. It also predicts the properties of the material when it is transformed into a solid form.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a procedure involving the controlled addition of salt to a solution, heating it to a high temperature, and then analyzing the resulting material's structure and properties. They followed a rule that involved adjusting the salt content to achieve the desired properties.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A material's internal structure and surface features are adjusted by varying the amount of a specific additive to influence its physical form and performance under heat and electrical stress.
descriptions.approach: A controlled chemical process is used to modify the material's growth conditions, where increasing the additive concentration leads to larger, more uniform shapes. The resulting material is then processed into a dense form and tested for consistent performance across a wide temperature range.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Discovery of Host-Directed Antiviral Therapies

descriptions.problem: This work aims to identify the key interactions between a pathogen and its host, in order to find potential therapeutic targets. It estimates the impact of these interactions on the pathogen's ability to infect and replicate within the host.
descriptions.approach: The approach involves using a technique to 'knock out' specific genes in host cells, allowing researchers to study the effects on the pathogen. The results are then combined with data from patients and medical records to identify potential treatments.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The task is to identify key host components that influence the replication and spread of a pathogen in living systems, by measuring how changes in host biology affect pathogen behavior across different biological contexts.
descriptions.approach: A systematic perturbation method is applied to living systems to test how altering specific host elements affects pathogen dynamics. Results are analyzed using computational models to predict outcomes and link genetic variations to biological effects in real-world health data.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Continuous Dynamic Mapping of the Corticospinal Tract in Motor Eloquent Tumor Surgery: Our Experience and Evaluation of the Method

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the location of a specific structure in the brain, and predicts the outcome of surgery based on that location. It compares the results of different methods of mapping the structure and optimizes the approach to minimize damage to the surrounding tissue.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a combination of two methods to map the structure: one method involved using a probe to detect electrical signals in the brain, and the other method involved using a device to apply electrical impulses to the brain. The procedure involved monitoring the electrical signals and impulses in real-time during the surgery.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system continuously monitors neural activity in response to mechanical perturbation during invasive procedures, estimating the sensitivity of motor pathways to detect early signs of functional disruption. It compares real-time responses across time and location to assess stability and predict potential damage.
descriptions.approach: A probe is moved through neural tissue while recording thresholds for eliciting motor responses. These thresholds are tracked over time and space, and the data are used to adjust surgical actions in real time, maintaining functional integrity while enabling deeper tissue removal.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: How the wisdom of crowds, and of the crowd within, are affected by expertise

descriptions.problem: This research investigates how the accuracy of individual predictions is affected by the level of expertise and the amount of data considered. It aims to understand how combining multiple predictions from experts or non-experts impacts the overall accuracy.
descriptions.approach: The study uses a numerical estimation task where participants estimate the number of objects they see. They compare individual predictions to those of groups of participants and to expert predictions, and optimize their approach by providing feedback and adjusting their strategy.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The accuracy of individual predictions is evaluated and compared to the performance of a group of similar predictions, especially when individuals have refined their judgment through experience.
descriptions.approach: Predictions are collected and combined across individuals, but only if individual responses show meaningful variation. When variation is minimal, the group's performance is improved by including diverse, independent judgments rather than repeating the same outcome.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Caveat Emptor Doesn’t Cut It

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the impact of international medical services on the health and safety of patients in host countries, compares the economic benefits to the potential risks and drawbacks, and optimizes the allocation of resources to ensure equitable access to medical services.
descriptions.approach: The procedure involves analyzing the relationships between economic disparities, cultural differences, and the provision of medical services, using data on international medical services, economic indicators, and cultural norms to inform the analysis.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system is evaluated to determine the responsibility for outcomes when services are delivered across borders, especially when those services involve high-risk interventions and are influenced by financial incentives and cultural differences.
descriptions.approach: A framework compares risk distribution, legal jurisdiction, and cultural context across regions, using patterns of service delivery, financial arrangements, and patient outcomes to assess accountability and equity in decision-making.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

topic_name: Facial Nerve Paralysis Treatment and Research
title: Effectiveness of Early Electrical Neuromuscular Stimulation in Functional Recovery of the Facial Nerve after Excision of Benign Superficial Lobe Lesions of the Parotid Gland

descriptions.problem: This study aims to determine if a specific therapy can help recover a common complication after a surgical procedure, and whether it can be done safely and effectively at home. It estimates the recovery rate of a specific function after the therapy is applied.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a therapy that sends electrical signals to help a specific function recover, and they tested it on a group of patients who had a similar surgical procedure. They compared the results to a group of patients who did not receive the therapy.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The rate of functional recovery in a specific neural pathway is measured over time and compared to a baseline group that did not receive intervention.
descriptions.approach: Patients receive a consistent, timed external signal applied immediately after surgery, with recovery progress assessed at multiple time points using standardized functional scoring.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Identification of Circulating hsa_circ_0063425 and hsa_circ_0056891 as Novel Biomarkers for Detection of Type 2 Diabetes

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the levels of certain molecules in the blood that are associated with the presence of a particular disease. It predicts the likelihood of having the disease based on these levels and compares them to levels found in people without the disease.
descriptions.approach: The researchers use a combination of data from small groups of people with the disease and healthy people to identify the molecules. They then use a statistical model to analyze the data and identify the molecules that are most closely associated with the disease.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A set of gene-derived molecules is measured to determine their levels in biological samples, and their association with a disease state is assessed across different patient groups and clinical conditions.
descriptions.approach: Levels of specific molecules are compared between groups with and without a condition. Statistical models evaluate their predictive power, and interactions with other regulatory molecules are tested through functional assays to confirm biological relevance.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: An Effective Memory Analysis for Malware Detection and Classification

descriptions.problem: The task is to estimate the characteristics of a system's behavior when it is running, and to compare these characteristics to those of known systems to determine whether the system is behaving abnormally. This is done by analyzing the system's behavior over time.
descriptions.approach: The approach involves extracting features from the system's memory, which can reveal information about its behavior, and then using these features to train a classifier that can distinguish between normal and abnormal behavior.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system identifies and distinguishes between malicious and normal software behavior by analyzing patterns in runtime memory snapshots, focusing on interactions with the system environment and suspicious operational sequences.
descriptions.approach: Memory data is processed to extract behavioral patterns, transformed into binary representations, and fed into a classification model that learns to differentiate between normal and anomalous runtime activities based on historical examples.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Application of a Hyper-Parameter Optimization Algorithm using Mars Surrogate for Deep Polsar Image Classification Models

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the best settings for a complex model to achieve good results, using data from two real examples. It compares the performance of different models and optimizes the settings to achieve the best results.
descriptions.approach: The approach uses a special kind of computer program to automatically try many different settings and choose the best one. It follows a procedure where the program tries many settings, evaluates the results, and repeats the process to find the best settings.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system identifies optimal settings for a complex model to improve its accuracy in classifying images based on patterns in high-dimensional data.
descriptions.approach: It uses a simplified, faster model to simulate the performance of the complex model across various settings, then selects the best settings by evaluating outcomes across multiple test scenarios.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Comparative Epigenome-Wide Analysis Highlights Placenta-Specific Differentially Methylated Regions

descriptions.problem: This work compares the patterns of changes in the way genes are turned on or off in a specific type of tissue to another type of tissue. It aims to understand the unique characteristics of this tissue by comparing its patterns to those of another tissue.
descriptions.approach: The researchers compared the patterns of changes in the way genes are turned on or off in 444 samples of this specific type of tissue with 444 samples of another type of tissue. They used a computer program to identify patterns that were unique to this tissue.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A set of biological regions is analyzed for changes in chemical modification patterns across two related tissues, with the goal of identifying functional associations linked to specific cellular processes.
descriptions.approach: A computational model compares modification levels across tissue samples, then maps these patterns to known biological functions using statistical enrichment analysis to detect significant associations.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Market Research and Design of a New Dental Medical Vehicle Based on Digital Technology

descriptions.problem: A system estimates public interest in mobile health services that provide accessible medical care in underserved locations, using feedback from user surveys and geographic usage patterns.
descriptions.approach: The system evaluates potential routes and service frequencies by analyzing population density, travel behavior, and demand signals to determine the most effective deployment strategy.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: This research aims to design a new type of vehicle that helps people keep their health better by making it easier to take care of their health. It's estimated that many people don't take care of their health as well as they should, and this vehicle could help.
descriptions.approach: The research starts by looking at the types of people who might use this vehicle and how it could make their lives easier. It then uses data from market surveys to predict that more and more people will want to use this vehicle in the future.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Chronotoxicity of Semen Strychni is associated with circadian metabolism and transport in mice

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the toxicity of a substance in two different groups of subjects over time, comparing the levels of a toxic compound in their bodies and determining the impact of their natural rhythms on this compound's levels and breakdown. It also compares the effectiveness of different dosing times.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a combination of experiments to study the effects of the substance on the subjects' bodies, including measuring the levels of toxic compounds in their blood and urine, and analyzing the breakdown of these compounds in different parts of their bodies.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The timing of exposure to a compound influences its biological effects and systemic availability, with peak adverse outcomes occurring at specific times of day and reduced effects at others, depending on biological rhythms.
descriptions.approach: Exposure is administered at various times, and the resulting concentration in blood and tissue is measured. The rate of breakdown and removal of the compound is assessed across time points, revealing patterns tied to internal biological timing.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Antiviral plant preparation as a topical treatment for respiratory viral infections in adults and children

descriptions.problem: This work aims to estimate the effectiveness of a plant-based treatment in preventing and treating a common and widespread cause of death, which is a major public health concern. It compares the treatment's performance against a placebo in various clinical trials.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used cell cultures and in vivo studies to investigate the treatment's ability to stop the replication of a wide range of pathogens. They also reviewed existing clinical trials to determine the treatment's efficacy.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A treatment is evaluated for its ability to inhibit the spread of a wide range of airborne pathogens in human hosts, based on outcomes from controlled human trials and laboratory studies using cell cultures.
descriptions.approach: A liquid extract is tested across multiple pathogen strains in cell models and human trials to assess its effectiveness in reducing pathogen replication and symptom duration, with results compared across different populations and conditions to determine consistency and safety.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Health Promotion Among Home-Dwelling Elderly Individuals in Turkey

descriptions.problem: This research aims to identify and describe the most effective health-promotion practices for individuals who need support with daily tasks and maintaining their physical, mental, and emotional well-being. It estimates the benefits of these practices on the quality of life and cost-effectiveness.
descriptions.approach: The study uses a holistic approach, considering physical, social, spiritual, and cultural resources, and applies a positive model to support individual health and coping. It follows a procedure that involves analyzing data on health-promotion practices and their outcomes, and optimising these practices for maximum benefit.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system is designed to predict and optimize well-being outcomes for individuals living independently, based on social, environmental, and personal resource availability.
descriptions.approach: It evaluates patterns in daily support networks and service usage, then applies a holistic framework that strengthens resilience by integrating physical, emotional, and social inputs to promote long-term stability and adaptive functioning.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Participative modelling of a micro insurance scheme for African swine fever (ASF) in a peri-urban pig farming (PF) in Kinshasa, democratic republic of Congo (DRC)

descriptions.problem: Estimate the average number of animals lost annually due to a serious health risk, and compare the costs of losses to the total value of the affected animals. The data should be based on historical records and expert opinions.
descriptions.approach: Use a mathematical model to calculate the average number of animals lost, and then apply a formula to estimate the costs of losses based on the total value of the affected animals.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system is estimated that assigns financial risk exposure to small and large agricultural units based on loss frequency and unit size, using historical data on production decline and economic impact.
descriptions.approach: A two-part risk-sharing model is applied: one assigns 90% risk coverage to small units and 60% to large units, with compensation thresholds adjusted to reflect unit vulnerability and recovery timelines.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Using an Artificial Real-Time Response Audience in Online Sales Education to Improve Self-Efficacy in Sales Presentations: An Online Classroom Innovation

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the effectiveness of using AI technology to help people improve their ability to deliver presentations confidently and effectively, by comparing the results of students who used AI technology with those who did not.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a statistical test to compare the results of two groups, and then used the results to explain how AI technology can be used to improve people's confidence in delivering presentations.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system estimates how well an individual performs in real-time verbal communication by analyzing and adjusting vocal characteristics such as tone, rhythm, and intensity during a performance.
descriptions.approach: The system generates a responsive, interactive feedback loop that mimics human behavior in real time, adjusting vocal parameters based on observed patterns and providing immediate, personalized guidance to improve performance quality.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Microtia: A Data Linkage Study of Epidemiology and Implications for Service Delivery

descriptions.problem: This study estimates the number of cases of a birth defect in a specific population over a long period, comparing the results to a larger population. It also compares the characteristics of patients who received different types of treatment for this defect.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a method called data linkage to combine data from different sources, such as birth records and medical records, to identify patients with the defect. They then analyzed the data to identify patterns and trends.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A rate is estimated for a condition occurring in live births over time and space, and differences in access to a medical procedure are assessed across various personal and geographic factors.
descriptions.approach: Patient records are linked across databases to identify individuals with a diagnosis and their procedural history. Groupings are formed based on procedure type and personal attributes, then compared across demographic and location-based variables.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Impact of Watershed Interventions on Biophysical and Ecosystem Services in Mettur Catchment of Tamil Nadu, India

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the impact of interventions on soil erosion, water availability, and agricultural productivity, comparing the effects of different treatments on a large dataset. It also predicts the economic viability of the project and explains the need for integration with other departments.
descriptions.approach: The study uses a combination of data collection and analysis to evaluate the effects of interventions. It follows a procedure of data collection, analysis, and comparison to estimate the impact and predict the economic viability of the project.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The rate of sediment accumulation and surface runoff from land-based interventions is estimated from observed physical changes in water flow and deposited material during rainfall events.
descriptions.approach: A set of monitored sites is selected and evaluated over time; sediment deposition is measured, runoff volume is calculated, and economic returns are derived from long-term performance data to assess overall impact and sustainability.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Measurement and Crosstalk Analysis of Hexagonal TSV Bundle in 3D ICs

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the performance of a specific type of connection in a complex device, comparing the results of measurements and calculations to determine the best design. It also compares the performance of different types of connections to identify the most effective one.
descriptions.approach: The researchers use a combination of measurements and calculations to analyze the connection. They extract the necessary information from the measurements and use it to validate their calculations, which are based on a mathematical model of the connection's behavior.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The performance of a multi-conductor system is evaluated under electromagnetic coupling, comparing signal integrity across adjacent channels with and without a grounded reference structure. Return and insertion losses are measured and modeled across a wide frequency range.
descriptions.approach: Electromagnetic field distributions are computed and validated against experimental data. A de-embedding technique is applied to isolate segment-level behavior, and coupling effects are quantified through field-based analysis across frequency bands.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: The nexus of aviation and tourism growth in the South Pacific Region

descriptions.problem: This study estimates the impact of air travel from Australia and New Zealand on the number of visitors to four island nations in the South Pacific. It compares these numbers to see if there is a relationship between air travel and visitor numbers.
descriptions.approach: The researchers use a special statistical method to analyze the data, and apply it to two groups of data: the number of visitors and the number of flights. They then use this method to see if the number of flights is related to the number of visitors.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A relationship is estimated between travel volume from major source regions and economic indicators in destination regions, focusing on how changes in transport accessibility affect movement patterns.
descriptions.approach: A statistical model is applied that accounts for potential biases in observed data by using instrumental variables, then analyzes how movement patterns respond to shifts in source-region income levels.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Pengaruh Penambahan Jahe (Zingiber Officinale) Pada Sirup Rosella (Hibiscus Sabdariffa l.) Terhadap Tingkat Kesukaan Konsumen

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the effect of adding a certain ingredient to a drink on consumer preference, comparing different levels of the ingredient to see which one is most preferred. It also explains why the addition of the ingredient affects some parameters but not others.
descriptions.approach: The study uses a controlled experiment with multiple groups, each with a different amount of the ingredient added. The results are analyzed using statistical tests to determine if there is a significant difference between the groups.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A quantitative assessment is made to determine how varying amounts of a natural additive influence consumer perception of a liquid product across sensory attributes such as visual appeal, flavor, and scent.
descriptions.approach: A controlled experiment is designed with multiple dosage levels, each tested in random order across a group of evaluators. Differences in preference are statistically evaluated using variance analysis and post-hoc comparisons to identify the most favored condition.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Back to the 60s: The Heimlich Valve A patient- and family-centered care perspective

descriptions.problem: Estimate the effectiveness of a simple, low-tech solution to manage air and fluid in a confined space, and predict the outcome for a young child with a persistent condition.
descriptions.approach: Use data from a chest CT scan to compare the child's lung function and lung capacity before and after the treatment, and evaluate the effectiveness of the low-tech solution in reducing the need for repeated interventions.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A chronic condition allowing uncontrolled escape of fluid and gas from a bodily cavity is monitored over time to assess recovery and functional outcomes.
descriptions.approach: A simple, low-risk device is used to allow continuous removal of contents while maintaining internal stability. Recovery is tracked through repeated imaging and functional measurements to evaluate long-term physiological changes.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Integral imaging display with enhanced depth of field based on bifocal lens array

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the depth of a 3D object from a set of 2D images, and compares the results to a conventional method. It aims to optimise the depth of field by combining two reconstructed images.
descriptions.approach: The approach uses a combination of two lens arrays with different shapes to create two central depth regions. The reconstructed images are then compared to estimate the depth of the 3D object.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system reconstructs a three-dimensional scene by combining views from two distinct depth layers, producing a more immersive and detailed spatial representation than standard methods.
descriptions.approach: A structured optical element divides incoming light into two spatial patterns, each focused on a different depth range, then merges the resulting views into a unified spatial output using alignment and spatial mapping.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Predicting the Presence and Abundance of Bacterial Taxa in Environmental Communities through Flow Cytometric Fingerprinting
