descriptions.approach: The research uses a combination of data from tissue samples and experiments to determine the effect of the protein on tissue growth and death. It follows a procedure where the protein is increased in certain tissue samples, and the effect on growth and death is observed and measured.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: DNA methylation as a tool to explore ageing in wild roe deer populations

descriptions.problem: A quantitative estimate of biological age is derived from molecular markers in cells, comparing it to known life spans across individuals exposed to different environmental conditions.
descriptions.approach: A model is trained on molecular profiles from biological samples, adjusting parameters by sex and environment to predict age-related changes, then identifies key genomic sites where variation patterns differ between sexes and environments.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the age of animals based on changes in their genetic material, comparing the results to their actual age. It also compares the age of different sexes and identifies patterns of change in their genetic material.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a special array to measure changes in the genetic material of blood cells from a large group of animals. They trained models to predict age based on these changes and compared the results to the animals' actual age.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Features of marketing in healthcare (The example of medical tourism for the older adults)

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the effectiveness of a specific strategy in a particular context, comparing the outcomes of different approaches to understand what works best. It predicts the impact of a particular action on a specific group, based on data from previous studies and original research.
descriptions.approach: The procedure involves analyzing data from literature and original research to identify key features of a particular strategy. It then uses this information to optimize the strategy for a specific context, aiming to improve outcomes for a particular group.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A pattern of behavior is identified in individuals seeking specialized services across geographic boundaries, based on personal preferences, health goals, and available options. The frequency and nature of such decisions are compared across different populations and service environments.
descriptions.approach: A structured framework maps decisions made by individuals when selecting services based on perceived benefits, accessibility, and personal alignment. This framework evaluates how external influences and personal characteristics shape choices over time.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: The Value of Calretinin in the Diagnosis of Hirschsprung's Disease in Dakar

descriptions.problem: This study aims to determine whether a specific protein helps identify a condition where nerve cells are missing from a part of the digestive system. It estimates the effectiveness of this protein in identifying the condition, compared to other methods.
descriptions.approach: The researchers looked at old tissue samples from people who might have the condition, and used a special test to see if the protein was present. They then compared the results to other tests to see how well the protein worked.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A marker is assessed to detect the absence of ganglion cells in a segment of the digestive tract, based on tissue samples and microscopic observations of cellular structure and distribution.
descriptions.approach: Tissue sections are stained and analyzed for the presence or absence of a specific cellular signal in nerve-rich regions. Results are compared to standard histological findings to determine whether the absence of that signal correlates with a known condition involving missing nerve cells.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Lynx D2.7 Catalogue of relevant legal and regulatory datasets

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the publication status of a large collection of rules and court decisions in a specific geographic region, comparing the completeness and accessibility of these records across different sources.
descriptions.approach: It uses a systematic review of existing records to identify gaps and inconsistencies, then optimizes the data by creating a unified, standardized format for easy access and comparison.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system identifies and organizes official rules and judicial decisions across multiple jurisdictions, tracking their publication status, access conditions, and formats to support consistent retrieval and interpretation.
descriptions.approach: It maps authoritative rulings and regulations into a structured network, linking them through shared criteria, formats, and access policies, enabling automated discovery and cross-jurisdictional comparison.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Investigating immunological interaction between lymphatic filariasis and COVID-19 infection: a preliminary evidence

descriptions.problem: This research investigates the relationship between a certain disease caused by parasites and another disease caused by a virus. It aims to determine if the presence of parasites in a community affects the effectiveness of a treatment for the virus.
descriptions.approach: The researchers collected blood samples from people living in areas where parasites are common. They tested the blood for signs of the virus and the parasites, and analyzed the results to see if there was a connection between the two.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A statistical assessment is made to determine whether exposure to a chronic parasitic infection correlates with the presence of an acute infectious response in a shared population.
descriptions.approach: Blood samples are collected and tested for markers of both infections. The frequency of each marker is recorded. A measure of association between the two markers is computed using a ratio-based estimate, with confidence bounds derived from observed frequencies.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Estudio de caso de producción más limpia de la empresa Concentrados Cauca, ubicada en el Tambo, Colombia

descriptions.problem: This work aims to improve the efficiency and reduce the risk to humans and the environment in the production processes of a specific organisation, by estimating the best way to achieve this through a set of established methods.
descriptions.approach: The approach involves using a set of established methods to compare the current production processes with the most efficient ones, and to identify the best way to achieve the desired outcome, based on data and evidence from the organisation's operations.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A set of operational workflows is analyzed to identify inefficiencies and environmental impacts, with the goal of reducing waste, energy use, and emissions while maintaining output levels.
descriptions.approach: A systematic review of input-output relationships across stages is conducted, using baseline performance metrics to compare alternatives and select configurations that improve resource efficiency and reduce negative environmental footprints.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

topic_name: Advancements in PLL and VCO Technologies
title: High Resolution Asynchronous Digital Event Timer

descriptions.problem: It estimates the exact interval between two distinct occurrences, achieving finer precision than conventional methods, especially when events happen rapidly and must be recorded with sub-nanosecond accuracy.
descriptions.approach: It uses a high-frequency reference signal and a parallel sampling mechanism to resolve tiny time gaps by comparing event timestamps across multiple independent sampling phases.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the time difference between two events with high precision, and compares it to a reference value to determine the accuracy of the measurement. It also optimizes the resolution of the measurement by using a unique approach to measure the time fraction of a clock cycle.
descriptions.approach: The approach uses a high-frequency clock signal to measure the time difference, and a specialized arrangement of the clock signal to increase the resolution. The measurement is then compared to a reference value to determine the accuracy.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Microstructures Properties of barium-strontium titanate (BST) ceramics Doped with B-Li Glasses for LTCC Technology Applications

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the optimal temperature for a specific material to achieve a desired property, and compares the results to a standard method. It also explains how a new substance can improve the performance of a device.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a combination of data and experimentation to develop a new method for improving the material's properties. They tested the material at different temperatures and compared the results to a standard method.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The relationship between processing temperature and electrical performance in layered ceramic components is investigated, focusing on how material composition affects capacitance, loss, and stability across multiple layers.
descriptions.approach: A liquid-phase-assisted process is applied to reduce processing temperature; performance is evaluated by measuring capacitance and loss across varying layer counts under controlled voltage conditions.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Alternative Basic Education: teaching and learning of adults through virtual means in Peru

descriptions.problem: This work aims to understand the relationship between the effort put in by instructors and the progress made by learners in a specific type of training, where participants are isolated from their peers. It also seeks to identify which factors contribute most to the learners' success.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a method where they collected data on the learners' progress and the instructors' work, and then analyzed the data to find patterns and connections. They used a statistical test to compare the data and determine the strength of the relationships between the variables.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The effectiveness of instructional support in improving learning outcomes for individuals in disadvantaged circumstances is assessed using observed interactions and performance metrics.
descriptions.approach: A model evaluates how different facets of human engagement—such as emotional connection and digital interaction—relate to learning gains, using statistical analysis to identify which elements most strongly influence progress.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Machine Learning to Predict Medical Devices Repair and Maintenance Needs

descriptions.problem: The task is to predict the likelihood of a product failing in a certain way, based on limited information about its past performance. This prediction is used to decide on the best course of action for maintenance and repair.
descriptions.approach: A complex algorithm is used to forecast the product's failure type, taking into account various attributes such as time until failure and repair time. The algorithm is trained on a limited set of data and then tested on new, unseen data.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: Estimate the likelihood of a system encountering specific types of malfunctions over time, based on historical operational patterns and usage metrics.
descriptions.approach: Train a model to recognize patterns in operational logs and assign probabilities to different failure modes using structured statistical rules and similarity-based inference.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Toward Reconfiguring Sociotechnical Systems Design: Digitally Infused Work Systems and the “Platform-STS”

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the effectiveness of new kinds of work systems that have emerged as a result of digital transformation. It compares these systems to existing ones and suggests ways to improve them.
descriptions.approach: The approach involves identifying a new class of systems that are 'distributed' and governed by market mechanisms, and introducing a design principle called 'redundancy of connectivity' to guide design.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system is analyzed to determine how interactions between human actors and digital tools evolve across networks, predicting how performance, resilience, and control shift under decentralized coordination and market-driven incentives.
descriptions.approach: A model maps how connectivity between components increases through multiple, overlapping pathways, with performance evaluated under variable levels of autonomy, feedback, and external influence across dynamic networks.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Automated Detection of Pneumothorax Using Frontal Chest X-rays

descriptions.problem: A system estimates whether an image shows a deviation from normal tissue structure, based on patterns in pixel intensity and spatial arrangement across a two-dimensional visual field.
descriptions.approach: The method identifies boundaries of structured regions using gradient-based edge detection, then analyzes surface texture and intensity variation to classify the image as normal or abnormal using a statistical classifier trained on labeled examples.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the likelihood of a serious medical condition based on a 2D image, comparing it to a set of normal examples. It aims to improve doctors' ability to diagnose and treat diseases more accurately.
descriptions.approach: The method uses image processing techniques to extract features from the image, and then applies a classification algorithm to determine whether the image is normal or abnormal. The algorithm is trained on a set of examples to increase its accuracy.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: An Andrographolide from Helichrysum caespitium (DC.) Sond. Ex Harv., (Asteraceae) and Its Antimicrobial, Antiquorum Sensing, and Antibiofilm Potentials

descriptions.problem: This study aims to estimate the effectiveness of a compound from a plant extract against certain types of bacteria, and to compare its ability to inhibit the growth of these bacteria and prevent them from forming clusters. The compound is also compared to other substances in terms of its ability to prevent bacteria from producing a certain pigment.
descriptions.approach: The study uses a combination of chemical analysis and biological testing to isolate and purify the compound, and to test its effects on different types of bacteria. The results are compared to other substances and to the effects of the compound on the bacteria's ability to form clusters and produce a certain pigment.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A compound is identified and tested for its ability to block communication signals among microorganisms and prevent the formation of structured, protective communities that promote resistance and persistence.
descriptions.approach: The compound is extracted from a plant-based source and evaluated in controlled lab settings using assays that measure inhibition of signal production and suppression of microbial group behavior in response to environmental cues.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Scale removal in water pipeline with a magnetic field

descriptions.problem: This study aims to estimate the effectiveness of a magnetic field in removing a common problem in systems that carry a liquid: a hard, white substance that forms when minerals in the liquid combine with other substances. The goal is to find the best way to use a magnetic field to remove this substance.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a combination of experiments and mathematical models to test how different variables (orientation, speed, and strength of the magnetic field) affect the removal of the substance. They used a special machine to apply the magnetic field and measured the results over time.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system's performance is reduced by the buildup of a hard, insoluble deposit that forms over time. The rate at which this deposit is reduced is estimated based on operating conditions and their interactions.
descriptions.approach: A model maps how changes in treatment duration, input velocity, and field strength affect deposit reduction. It uses observed outcomes to predict performance and identifies optimal settings through statistical analysis of experimental results.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Ace I/D Polymorphism Associated With Muscle Strength And Its Relation To The Health Status Of People Over 60 Years Of Age

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the relationship between a genetic variation (ACE I/D polymorphism) and muscle strength in older adults, comparing the effects of different genotypes on physical performance tests such as standing time and leg strength.
descriptions.approach: The study used a questionnaire to assess physical activity, fitness tests like SPPB and Up&Go, and PCR to analyze the genetic variation. The results showed associations between genotypes and physical performance, but did not confirm a clear impact on muscle strength and health.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A pattern is estimated in how genetic variation influences physical performance metrics across a group of individuals aged 60 and above, specifically relating to muscle function and overall physical activity levels.
descriptions.approach: Genetic markers are analyzed using molecular detection to identify specific variants. Physical performance is measured through standardized tests and activity logs. Statistical comparisons are made across genotypes to determine associations with observed outcomes.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Quantification of Semi-Truck Cab Decontamination

descriptions.problem: The effectiveness of various cleaning procedures is assessed across different surface types to determine how well they reduce pathogen load over time, based on measurable signal strength from biological samples.
descriptions.approach: Multiple surface types are exposed to different cleaning protocols, then sampled and analyzed for residual biological activity. Results are compared across surface type and treatment to identify which combinations yield the lowest residual signal.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the effectiveness of different methods for removing a disease-causing agent from various surfaces, and compares the results to determine which method is most effective. It also explains why some surfaces are more resistant to removal than others.
descriptions.approach: The researcher applies a disease-causing agent to small pieces of different surfaces, then applies different methods to try and remove the agent. The results are compared to determine which method is most effective and why some surfaces are more resistant to removal.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: An asynchronous P system with a DPLL algorithm for solving a satisfiability problem

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the number of steps required to find a solution to a complex problem, and compares it to the number of steps required by other methods. It predicts the efficiency of a proposed algorithm for finding solutions to a specific type of problem.
descriptions.approach: The algorithm uses a set of rules to find a solution to the problem, and it can work in parallel or sequentially. The approach involves applying the rules in a specific order to find a solution that satisfies the conditions of the problem.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system is designed to determine whether a set of logical constraints can be simultaneously satisfied by assigning truth values to a finite set of variables.
descriptions.approach: It processes the constraints in parallel using a rule-based mechanism that iteratively refines candidate assignments, reducing the search space through systematic elimination of inconsistent configurations.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Evolution of Gram+ Streptococcus pyogenes has maximized efficiency of the Sortase A cleavage site

descriptions.problem: A system evaluates how efficiently a specific molecular signal is processed by two competing mechanisms in a cellular membrane environment, determining which pathway leads to stable attachment of a surface-bound component.
descriptions.approach: The system tests variations of a key residue in the signal sequence, measuring the outcome of two distinct enzymatic reactions that act on the same substrate but produce different functional results, favoring one over the other based on residue identity.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the optimal position of a specific amino acid residue in a protein sequence to prevent unwanted interactions with a non-essential enzyme, thereby stabilizing the protein on the cell surface.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a combination of in vitro experiments and cell membrane fractions to test the effects of mutating the amino acid residue and to identify the enzyme responsible for the unwanted interactions.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Lipid-loaded tumor-associated macrophages sustain tumor growth and invasiveness in prostate cancer

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the relationship between a type of immune cell and the progression of a disease, and compares the impact of different factors on the disease's severity. It also predicts the outcome of a treatment and explains how it works.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a technique to analyze the cells' behavior, identifying a subset that is affected by changes in how the cells process certain substances. They then tested the effect of blocking this process on the disease's growth and treatment outcomes.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A group of immune cells is identified that exhibit altered activity in metabolic pathways, and their presence is linked to worse disease outcomes and increased spread of cancer cells.
descriptions.approach: A computational model detects patterns in gene expression that reflect metabolic reprogramming. It identifies a cell subset responding to signals from cancer cells, which in turn promotes migration of cancer cells through a secreted factor, and shows that dietary manipulation amplifies this effect.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Antipsychotic drug treatment of schizophrenia in later life: Results from the European cross-sectional AMSP study

descriptions.problem: This work investigates how the age of patients affects the selection and amount of a specific type of treatment for a mental health condition, and how this affects the treatment of patients over 65 years old. It also compares different types of treatment.
descriptions.approach: The researchers looked at data from a large database of patients' treatment records, comparing the treatment given to patients of different ages and sexes. They also reviewed current guidelines for treating patients over 65 years old.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A pattern is estimated in how treatment decisions change with patient age and gender, based on observed prescribing behaviors over time.
descriptions.approach: Patient records are analyzed to map treatment choices and levels across age groups, adjusting for gender. Guidelines are reviewed to assess how well they address treatment in older individuals.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: GRaNIE and GRaNPA: Inference and evaluation of enhancer-mediated gene regulatory networks applied to study macrophages

descriptions.problem: A system is designed to infer how molecular regulators influence cellular responses across different conditions by linking regulatory elements to downstream outcomes based on observable expression patterns.
descriptions.approach: It integrates chromatin accessibility and expression data across samples, then constructs a network of regulatory relationships. It evaluates the network's predictive accuracy by testing how well it forecasts expression changes in specific cell states.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: This work aims to understand how certain DNA sequences control the activity of other DNA sequences, and how these interactions affect the expression of proteins in different cell types. It estimates the importance of these interactions and compares them to known patterns of protein expression.
descriptions.approach: The approach involves combining data from different experiments, such as how cells open up their DNA (open chromatin data) and how they express RNA (RNA-seq), to infer the interactions between DNA sequences. The method also uses data on how cells are connected (Hi-C data) to build a network of interactions.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: COMPARATIVE STUDY OF EDGES OF THERMAL IMAGES USING GRADIENT, LAPLACIAN, CANNY OPERATORS: A CRITICAL REVIEW

descriptions.problem: A system identifies and characterizes boundaries in visual data under low-illumination conditions, evaluating how well different computational techniques extract and preserve structural details in the presence of noise and variation.
descriptions.approach: A sequence of filtering and thresholding operations is applied to input data, using local gradient and curvature analysis to detect transitions, with a focus on preserving fine structural features while suppressing irrelevant variations.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: This work aims to improve the analysis of images that show the presence or absence of certain features, using a combination of mathematical techniques to extract and enhance these features. It estimates the effectiveness of different methods for this task, comparing their results.
descriptions.approach: The researchers use a series of mathematical operations to process the images, including identifying areas where the image changes suddenly or smoothly. They apply these operations to a set of images to see how well each method works.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Calculation of the Shaping of a Space Umbrella Antenna During Strong Bending of Radial Rods Connected Along Parallels by Tensile Cables

descriptions.problem: An object is bent into a curved shape, and its shape is compared to a given surface. The goal is to estimate the forces acting on the object at specific points, and to determine the stiffness of a material that connects these points.
descriptions.approach: The object is modeled as a series of flexible, inextensible elements connected at nodes. The forces acting on the elements are calculated using a combination of geometric relationships and approximations, and the stiffness of the material is determined by solving a system of nonlinear equations.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system of interconnected flexible segments is deformed under controlled forces until its structure conforms to a specified curved surface, with the shape determined by the balance of internal forces and geometric constraints at connection points.
descriptions.approach: The deformation of each segment is modeled using known bending functions with quadratic displacement correction. Iterative adjustments compute internal forces at joints until the final shape matches the target surface through local equilibrium and geometric alignment.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: The United States index of socioeconomic deprivation for individuals (USiDep)

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the level of deprivation in individuals, comparing it to their income and other measures related to deprivation. It aims to explain the relationship between deprivation and physical and mental health outcomes.
descriptions.approach: The approach involves administering a validated measure to participants, calculating correlations between the measure and other variables, and analyzing the results to identify patterns and associations.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A score is estimated for each individual based on self-reported experiences reflecting access to resources, health, and stability. This score is compared across individuals to assess its relationship with health outcomes and other measurable factors like income, education, and physical condition.
descriptions.approach: A short, structured set of questions is used to gather self-reported data. The responses are processed using a standardized scoring system that assigns a value reflecting the level of deprivation, based on patterns in the data and known associations with health outcomes.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: In vitro evaluation of antibacterial activity of fluorescein 0.5% eye drops

descriptions.problem: This study aims to determine the effectiveness of certain substances in preventing the growth of certain types of microorganisms, and to identify any potential risks or false negatives in diagnostic tests.
descriptions.approach: The researchers tested the substances against a range of microorganisms in a liquid medium, using a method that involves adding a small amount of the substance to a liquid and observing the growth of the microorganisms over time.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A liquid formulation's effect on microbial growth is assessed under controlled conditions to determine if it suppresses the development of specific pathogens.
descriptions.approach: A series of dilutions are prepared from the liquid formulation and exposed to microbial cultures. Growth is monitored over time to identify the lowest concentration that prevents visible microbial development.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Selection of URBANIZATION Indicator Species Through Naturalized Plant Distribution Analysis

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the distribution of certain types of organisms in different areas, and compares their frequency of appearance to identify the most suitable indicators of urbanization. It aims to explain the relationship between the presence of these organisms and the level of urbanization in various regions.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a statistical analysis method to analyze data from 162 cities and counties, and 1200 locations. They applied a matrix analysis to identify the most suitable indicators of urbanization by evaluating the distribution grades and appearance rates of the organisms.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: Identify a set of organisms that consistently thrive in human-modified environments and are strongly associated with urban development, based on their presence across diverse locations and time periods.
descriptions.approach: Analyze spatial patterns of organism occurrence over time and geography using frequency and distribution matrices. Rank locations by consistency of presence, then select a subset with high urban exposure and stable occurrence across multiple surveyed sites.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

subfield: Public Health, Environmental and Occupational Health
title: Pengaruh Paket "Avil-PMS" terhadap Pengetahuan Remaja Putri di SMA "X" Kota Bandung

descriptions.problem: This study aims to determine the impact of a specific health program on the knowledge of a particular group about a common health issue. It estimates the effect of the program on the group's knowledge and compares it to a control group.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a quantitative study design with a quasi-experimental approach, collecting data from 42 respondents using questionnaires and analyzing it with a dependent T-test to determine the influence of the program on the group's knowledge.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A change in an individual's understanding of a biological process is assessed after exposure to a sensory-rich instructional tool, comparing pre- and post-exposure levels of knowledge.
descriptions.approach: A statistical test evaluates differences in knowledge scores before and after intervention, using a structured questionnaire and a paired comparison method to determine if the intervention led to significant improvement.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Benchmarking Global Carrier Status in the Airline Industry

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the likelihood of an airline being a major global carrier based on its fleet size, number of international destinations, and continents served. It aims to provide a basis for assessing an airline's global reach and potential future status.
descriptions.approach: The approach involves using three key metrics to gauge an airline's global reach, ranking airlines based on these metrics, and comparing the airline's performance to its competitors.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A score is assigned to each entity based on its operational scale, geographic spread, and network diversity to determine its standing among peers in a global network.
descriptions.approach: A composite score is computed by combining fleet size, number of international connections, and continent coverage, with continent coverage weighted more heavily. The entity’s position is then evaluated relative to its immediate neighbors in the ranking to assess its competitive context.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Secondary parkinsonism and normal pressure hydrocephaly because of cranioencephalic trauma: a case report

descriptions.problem: This work investigates the relationship between brain damage and an imbalance in the brain's fluid system, which can lead to symptoms such as urinary incontinence, dementia, and stiffness. It aims to identify the importance of early diagnosis and treatment in improving outcomes.
descriptions.approach: The approach involves analyzing symptoms and imaging studies to diagnose the condition, and then using a medical procedure to test the brain's fluid system and assess its response to treatment. The goal is to optimize treatment and improve patient outcomes.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A pattern of neurological symptoms is assessed to determine whether they stem from a disorder involving fluid accumulation in brain cavities, particularly when those symptoms appear after a prior injury.
descriptions.approach: A diagnostic test is performed to evaluate the response to fluid removal; if symptoms improve significantly and persist over time, it suggests the disorder is linked to impaired fluid drainage and reabsorption.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Association between exposure to pesticides and allergic diseases in children and adolescents: a systematic review with meta-analysis

descriptions.problem: A quantitative synthesis estimates the strength of a relationship between environmental exposure and the likelihood of a health condition in young individuals, comparing results across multiple studies to determine consistency and statistical significance.
descriptions.approach: A structured search identifies relevant studies, extracts outcome measures, combines results using statistical weighting, and evaluates the overall effect size while assessing heterogeneity and confidence in the estimate.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: This study aims to determine if exposure to certain substances increases the risk of developing or worsening a specific respiratory condition in a particular age group, and if it affects another condition in the same age group.
descriptions.approach: The researchers searched for studies using a specific question and combined the results of multiple studies to draw a conclusion, using a method that ensures the quality of the findings.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Balancing a U-Shaped Assembly Line with a Heuristic Algorithm Based on a Comprehensive Rank Value

descriptions.problem: This work aims to optimize the efficiency of a production process by minimizing idle time and improving the balance of tasks. It estimates the optimal arrangement of tasks to achieve this goal.
descriptions.approach: The approach involves designing a mathematical model to represent the process, then using a rule-based method to find the best arrangement of tasks. The model is tested using multiple instances of data to compare the results and evaluate the effectiveness of the approach.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system is designed to distribute tasks across a fixed sequence of workstations to minimize idle time and ensure consistent workload across stations.
descriptions.approach: Tasks are ranked by a composite score reflecting their dependencies and durations. A rule-based method assigns each task to a workstation, adjusting assignments to maintain flow and minimize gaps in processing time.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: The Effect of Learning Strategy and Writing Motivation on the Ability to Write Short Texts during Covid-19 Pandemic

descriptions.problem: This research aims to compare the effectiveness of two teaching methods on students' ability to create short texts, and to identify the impact of students' drive to produce these texts on their quality. It also seeks to understand the relationship between the teaching method and the students' drive.
descriptions.approach: The study uses a quantitative approach, comparing the results of two groups of students who received different teaching methods. It employs a pre-test and post-test design, measuring students' ability to create short texts and their drive to produce them.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A difference in performance is estimated between two instructional methods and between individuals with varying levels of engagement in a learning environment, based on observed outcomes and self-reported involvement.
descriptions.approach: Students are assigned to one of two teaching approaches and tracked over time. Performance is measured before and after intervention, and statistical analysis determines whether differences are influenced by the interaction between teaching style and learner engagement.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

subfield: Public Health, Environmental and Occupational Health
title: Altered T lymphocyte subtypes and cytokine profiles in follicular fluid associated with diminished ovary reserve

descriptions.problem: A pattern of immune activity is assessed in a fluid surrounding reproductive structures, measuring changes in specific immune cell types and their secreted signaling molecules that may indicate declining biological function.
descriptions.approach: Immune cell populations are categorized and analyzed for activation markers. Signaling molecule levels are measured and linked to cell behavior. A key signal is shown to attract specific immune cells through a known receptor interaction.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: This research aims to understand how an imbalance in the immune system affects the growth of a specific type of reproductive organ, leading to poor reproductive outcomes. It estimates the levels of certain proteins and immune cells in a fluid surrounding the reproductive organ.
descriptions.approach: The researchers studied a group of women with reproductive problems, analyzing the structure and function of a key component of the reproductive organ. They used various tests to measure the levels of specific proteins and immune cells in a fluid surrounding the reproductive organ.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: A Projection Transformation Method for Eliminating Crosstalk in Networked Thermopile Arrays

descriptions.problem: A two-dimensional thermal map is reconstructed from indirect sensor readings affected by unintended signal mixing due to parallel pathways between adjacent elements.
descriptions.approach: A mathematical transformation is applied to align measured signals with a known non-linear response pattern, then iteratively refined to minimize discrepancies between predicted and observed values using local gradient updates.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: This work aims to improve the accuracy of measuring temperature information in a 2D grid, by eliminating the interference caused by unwanted signals. It estimates the correct temperature values from noisy measurements.
descriptions.approach: The method uses a mathematical transformation to solve a complex problem, and then uses an iterative algorithm to refine the solution. It uses a combination of simulated data and real-world experiments to test its effectiveness.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: SAR and Optical Image Matching Eased on Phase Congruency and Template Matching

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the similarity between images taken from different sources, and it compares them to determine the most accurate match. It aims to improve the matching process by considering the underlying patterns and features in the images.
descriptions.approach: The method uses a template matching procedure to find the most similar area in the entire image. It relies on a non-dimensional metric that focuses on the patterns and features of the images, rather than their light and dark changes.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system aligns two images taken under different physical conditions, where one has ambiguous brightness and contrast, and the other is clear but sensitive to lighting. It estimates the spatial position where features from one image best correspond to features in the other.
descriptions.approach: It identifies key structural patterns using a metric sensitive to consistent wave-like variations in intensity. It then searches for the best spatial alignment by comparing these patterns across the entire image.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Program for Calculation of the Optimal Distribution of the Planned Amount of Gas on the Gas Supply Network

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the optimal distribution of a certain quantity across a network of interconnected facilities, comparing different scenarios to find the best solution. It aims to explain how to allocate resources efficiently.
descriptions.approach: The procedure involves using a mathematical model to compare different distribution plans, selecting the one that minimizes waste and maximizes efficiency. The model is applied to real data from the functioning of the network, using a programming language to perform the calculations.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system estimates the most efficient way to route a fixed volume of energy through a network of interconnected nodes to meet demand at various endpoints while minimizing losses and operational costs.
descriptions.approach: It evaluates all possible flow patterns across the network, applies constraints on capacity and demand, and selects the configuration that minimizes total cost while ensuring all endpoints receive required amounts.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: GASTROPROTECTIVE EFFECT OF STANDARDIZED GINKGO BILOBA EXTRACT (EGB761) AGAINST INDOMETHACIN-INDUCED GASTRIC ULCERS IN RATS

descriptions.problem: A compound's ability to mitigate tissue damage caused by a known irritant is evaluated by measuring changes in oxidative stress markers and inflammatory response indicators in biological samples.
descriptions.approach: A compound is administered before exposure to an irritant, and after a set time, levels of oxidative byproducts, antioxidant enzyme activity, and inflammatory signaling molecules are measured to assess protective effects.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: This study investigates the protective effect of a natural substance on damage caused by a certain type of medication, which can harm the stomach lining. It aims to compare the effects of this substance alone, with another substance, and with a combination of the two.
descriptions.approach: The researchers gave a certain medication to some animals, then gave them a natural substance, and a combination of the two, to see how it affected the damage caused by the medication. They then looked at the levels of certain chemicals and markers in the animals' bodies to see the effects.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: F-18 FDG PET/CT in Relapsing Polychondritis Patients with Initial Respirotory Symptoms: Imaging Features and Association with Pulmonary Function and Disease Activity

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the extent of disease activity in a group of individuals with a condition that causes inflammation and scarring in their cartilage and respiratory system. It predicts the severity of symptoms and disease progression based on imaging data.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a type of imaging test that uses a radioactive substance to highlight areas of inflammation and scarring. They analyzed the data to identify patterns and correlations between the imaging results and the individuals' symptoms and disease activity.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A quantitative measure is derived from imaging to assess the severity of inflammation in cartilaginous tissues and its relationship to respiratory function and systemic inflammatory markers.
descriptions.approach: Imaging data is processed to compute a standardized score reflecting regional metabolic activity. This score is then correlated with functional breathing metrics and blood-based inflammation indicators to evaluate disease progression and treatment response.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: The “Life” in the Living Law: Law, Emotion and Landscape

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the impact of daily experiences on the collective understanding of a shared concept, which is shaped by the interactions of three key aspects: the physical environment, common sense, and social atmosphere. It compares these aspects to understand the complexity and instability of this concept.
descriptions.approach: The work uses a combination of semantic analysis and case studies to examine the relationships between these aspects. It follows a procedure that involves identifying patterns and meanings in the data, and then using these insights to anticipate the behavior of the concept.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system of collective beliefs and spatial patterns is analyzed to understand how human interactions and environmental contexts co-evolve over time, producing observable behaviors and societal responses.
descriptions.approach: A model maps interactions between people and places using observed patterns in daily decisions, identifying feedback loops where environment and behavior mutually influence each other over time.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Peter Goodrich, Advanced Introduction to Law and Literature (Edward Elgar, Cheltenham, UK and Northampton MA, USA), 2021.pp. 119

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the importance of literature in understanding a particular field, compares it to other related fields, and optimizes the way this field is introduced to new readers. It explains the significance of rhetoric and hermeneutics in this field.
descriptions.approach: The author reviews a new book that provides an introduction to this field, highlighting its key principles and stimulating critical thinking. The review aims to pinpoint essential ideas and offer insights that can help readers understand the subject.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A pattern of meaning in structured texts is analyzed to determine how interpretive frameworks influence the understanding of complex societal rules and their underlying motivations.
descriptions.approach: A systematic model maps how narrative elements and rhetorical structures interact to shape interpretations of formal systems, using comparative analysis of textual examples and their contextual applications.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Modelado computacional de la autoorganización espacial generada por circuitos genéticos multicelulares

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the emergence of complex structures in a system of living cells, predicting how these structures form and evolve over time. It compares different models to understand how these structures are generated and optimized.
descriptions.approach: The approach is to use computational models to simulate the behavior of these systems. The models are based on mathematical equations that describe how the cells communicate and respond to each other.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system of interacting units is studied to determine whether structured, stable spatial arrangements can emerge from dynamic molecular feedback.
descriptions.approach: A mathematical model simulates how units exchange signals and respond to local conditions, using continuous equations for simple systems or discrete units for complex ones, adjusting parameters to observe pattern formation or instability.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Getting Spiritual with Mark Twain

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the value of a person's own experiences and wisdom compared to the value of external knowledge and traditions. It predicts that people tend to prefer external sources over their own internal guidance.
descriptions.approach: The approach involves comparing internal experiences and wisdom to external knowledge and traditions, using a model that follows a step-by-step procedure of data analysis and pattern recognition.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A pattern of preference is inferred from repeated choices between two distinct options under varying conditions, where one option is personally owned and the other is externally sourced.
descriptions.approach: The system observes decisions made across multiple scenarios and assigns weights to each option based on consistency and context. It then predicts future choices by evaluating the relative value of personal versus external sources in given circumstances.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Improvement of the efficiency of using agricultural land

descriptions.problem: Estimate the efficiency of using land for growing crops, and identify areas where land is not being used effectively. Compare the quality of different types of land to determine which ones are suitable for specific uses.
descriptions.approach: Use data on land use and quality to develop a system that optimizes land allocation. Analyze historical data on land use and create maps to identify areas of inefficient land use.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system is estimated that maps underutilized parcels of land and evaluates their suitability for reassignment based on spatial and quality indicators, aiming to improve land use efficiency over time.
descriptions.approach: A spatial model processes land records and environmental data to generate maps of underused areas, assigns performance scores based on location and conditions, and proposes transfer rules using historical and current usage patterns.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: SOCIAL MEDIA ANALYSIS ON MALAY POLITICAL PARTIES IN MALAYSIA: STUDY ON THE ISSUES AND COMMENTS FACEBOOK

descriptions.problem: This study aims to identify common issues and user opinions on a specific topic, using data from social media platforms. It estimates the frequency and type of issues discussed, and compares the tone and style of user comments across different platforms.
descriptions.approach: The researchers use a qualitative method to collect data from social media platforms, analyzing the content and tone of posts over a set period. They apply a specific theoretical framework to identify patterns and trends in the data.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The frequency and thematic focus of public discourse on key societal topics are analyzed, along with the nature and tone of user-generated responses to official narratives over a defined time period.
descriptions.approach: A narrative framework is applied to categorize and compare topic emphasis and expression patterns across multiple official platforms, identifying dominant themes and recurring rhetorical strategies in user engagement.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: The role of Technical Vocational Education and Training Colleges (TVET) in higher education teaching: a higher education provided at basic education standard

descriptions.problem: This work investigates whether institutions providing basic-level training can also provide higher-level training, and whether these institutions meet the standards required for higher-level training.
descriptions.approach: The approach is to compare the standards and requirements for institutions providing higher-level training, and to argue that institutions providing basic-level training do not meet these standards.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system is evaluated to determine whether it meets the standards required to deliver advanced knowledge and critical thinking outcomes typically expected in higher-level learning environments.
descriptions.approach: A comparative analysis is conducted between the institution's internal processes and established benchmarks for academic rigor, student progression, and faculty qualifications, using official governance frameworks and outcome data as evidence.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: EPIZOOTIC MONITORING OF AFRICAN SWINE FEVER IN THE SUMY REGION

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the number of cases of a contagious animal disease in a specific geographic area over several years, based on data from testing samples from domestic animals. It also compares the incidence rate of the disease in different types of animal-keeping settings.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a specific laboratory test to analyze samples from domestic animals, and compared the results to historical data on the disease. They identified patterns and trends in the data to inform their conclusions and recommendations for improving disease monitoring.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A pattern of disease spread is tracked across a geographic area using repeated observations from multiple ownership groups. The frequency and location of cases are analyzed to identify high-risk zones and potential sources of infection.
descriptions.approach: Samples are collected from various population segments and tested for the presence of a pathogen. Results are aggregated over time and space to detect trends, and risk factors are evaluated to inform preventive actions.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

topic_name: Globalization, Historical Perspectives, and International Relations
title: Global histories and cosmopolitan ethics

descriptions.problem: A framework is developed to assess how interconnected human experiences across time and place challenge the idea of unified moral standards, evaluating the extent to which boundaries between groups are maintained or dismantled in practice.
descriptions.approach: A model maps patterns of interaction and separation across diverse human societies, using longitudinal data to simulate how shared values emerge or fade under conditions of integration or fragmentation.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the effectiveness of removing certain structures and boundaries in creating a just, fair, and peaceful world. It compares the outcomes of different approaches to achieving this goal.
descriptions.approach: The researchers use a consistent global viewpoint to evaluate the implications of exiting these structures and boundaries. They follow a procedure that involves analyzing and managing the removal of these structures and boundaries.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: The Composition of the Poetic Verse in The Poetry of Al Wahb Family

descriptions.problem: This research aims to identify the structural patterns of verse in a specific family of writers, analyzing their use of literary devices such as simile, metaphor, and rhythm to convey meaning. It seeks to understand how these patterns contribute to the overall effect of their work.
descriptions.approach: The researcher breaks down the analysis into five key steps: gathering information, organizing it, identifying patterns, testing hypotheses, and drawing conclusions. This process involves examining the structure of the verse and the devices used to convey meaning.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A pattern is identified in a sequence of structured expressions, analyzing how recurring elements are arranged and modified across multiple instances to reveal underlying design rules.
descriptions.approach: A systematic framework is applied to break down expressions into units and examine how they are assembled, altered, or omitted to form larger structures, using defined operational rules for each component.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: NCOA4 is a Prognostic Biomarker Associated with Immune Infiltrates in Glioblastoma

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the relationship between the expression levels of a protein and patient survival, and compares the survival rates of patients with varying levels of protein expression. It also aims to explain the underlying mechanisms and identify potential biomarkers for patient survival.
descriptions.approach: The study uses various computational tools to analyze data from a large dataset, including statistical tests, regression analysis, and network analysis. It follows a procedure of data collection, analysis, and model creation to identify patterns and relationships in the data.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A quantitative measure is estimated from patient data to predict survival outcomes based on the level of a specific gene's activity and its associations with immune system components.
descriptions.approach: A statistical model is built using patient records and gene expression levels, applying rank-based tests and survival analysis to link gene activity to survival time and immune component levels.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Analysis and Optimized Design of a Novel Compact Orthogonal Controllable Reactor

descriptions.problem: This work aims to improve the performance of a device that regulates a physical quantity, such as a magnetic field, by minimizing its size and increasing its range. It estimates the device's behavior under different conditions and compares it to a traditional design.
descriptions.approach: The work starts by analyzing the device's magnetic circuit theoretically, then uses a simulation model to test its behavior. It uses a combination of mathematical rules and a search algorithm to find the best parameters for the device, and finally builds a prototype to test its performance.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system's ability to adjust its resonant behavior over a wide range is evaluated, and its physical footprint is minimized while maintaining performance under varying operational conditions.
descriptions.approach: A mathematical model captures the relationship between structural dimensions and dynamic response. Parameters are iteratively refined using evolutionary rules to balance performance and size, with validation through physical testing.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Thermal vacuum tests for the ESA’s OPS-SAT mission

descriptions.problem: This research aims to estimate the performance of a complex system under extreme conditions, comparing its actual performance to its predicted performance, and optimising its design to meet the required standards. It uses data from past experiments and simulations to make these estimates and predictions.
descriptions.approach: The researchers followed a procedure that involved identifying a comprehensive test scenario, using a combination of technical expertise and data analysis to design the test, and then executing the test to gather data and evaluate the system's performance.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system's performance under extreme environmental conditions is evaluated to ensure it maintains functional stability and operational integrity across a range of external exposures and internal load variations.
descriptions.approach: A series of controlled environmental exposures are applied, with real-time monitoring of internal state changes. Test scenarios are iteratively refined based on physical constraints and observed deviations to ensure coverage of operational boundaries.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Combinational Circuits

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the optimal configuration of a complex system by comparing the performance of different designs, using a combination of mathematical models and computational simulations. It aims to explain how the system behaves under various conditions.
descriptions.approach: The approach involves breaking down the system into smaller components, analyzing their behavior, and using rules to combine them into a single, optimized design. It uses a set of predefined rules to infer the behavior of the system and to optimize its performance.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system infers the behavior of digital components from input-output mappings and predicts their output under given input conditions, including handling overflow and determining optimal bit width for precision.
descriptions.approach: It maps input patterns to output patterns using lookup tables, applies feedback suppression to prevent infinite loops, and uses standardized primitives to ensure consistent behavior across different hardware implementations.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: rTMS Reduces Craving and Alcohol Use in Patients with Alcohol Use Disorder: Results of a Randomized, Sham-Controlled Clinical Trial

descriptions.problem: This study estimates the effect of a specific treatment on two outcomes: the amount of a certain substance used and the level of a specific urge. It compares the results of two groups: one that received the treatment and one that did not.
descriptions.approach: The researchers applied a treatment to a group of people, and then compared the results to a group that did not receive the treatment. They used a specific statistical method to analyze the data and identify any differences between the two groups.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A treatment is evaluated for its effect on reducing strong urges to consume a substance and decreasing actual consumption over time, using longitudinal data from individuals who have recently stopped using it.
descriptions.approach: A structured intervention is applied to a group of individuals over a set period, and its impact is compared to a placebo-like intervention using repeated measurements over time to detect changes in behavior and urges.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Diffuse Mesangial Sclerosis

descriptions.problem: This research aims to estimate the likelihood of a child's kidney disease being fatal, based on the presence of a specific abnormality in the kidney tissue. It compares the outcomes of children with this abnormality to those without it.
descriptions.approach: The researchers use a case study approach, where they examine a single child's kidney tissue and compare it to a control group of children without the abnormality. They follow the child's health over time to determine the outcome.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A rare condition in young individuals is identified through tissue examination, where a specific pattern of cellular changes is detected early, often before symptoms become severe. The goal is to predict the likelihood of a poor outcome based on the presence and characteristics of this pattern.
descriptions.approach: A model analyzes microscopic images of tissue samples to detect a distinct cellular arrangement. It then evaluates the pattern's consistency and spatial distribution to assess the risk of adverse progression.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Institute for the Protection of Confidential Information: industry-specific features of legal regulation

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the effectiveness of various methods for managing information in different industries, comparing the outcomes of different approaches to optimise information security. It aims to explain the most suitable strategies for each industry.
descriptions.approach: The study uses a combination of data analysis and comparison of industry-specific features to identify the most effective methods. It follows a procedure of data collection, analysis, and comparison to determine the best approach for each industry.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: It identifies patterns in how rules are adapted across different sectors to address unique operational challenges and risk profiles.
descriptions.approach: It compares regulatory frameworks across domains using structured analysis of policy responses, then maps commonalities and divergences to infer underlying design principles and adaptation strategies.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Research and Practice of Differential Classroom

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the effectiveness of a new approach to learning, where the focus is on individual learners and their progress is tracked. It compares the outcomes of this approach to traditional methods.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used data on learner progress and outcomes to test the effectiveness of the new approach. They followed a procedure where the approach was applied in a controlled environment and the results were analyzed.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A structured learning environment is designed to adapt content and pace to individual needs, measuring how well diverse engagement strategies support varied understanding levels and outcomes.
descriptions.approach: A dynamic framework assigns tasks and feedback cycles based on real-time performance, adjusting complexity and support in response to individual progress and interaction patterns.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Alpha-ketoglutarate, a key molecule involved in nitrogen circulation in both animals and plants, in the context of human gut microbiota and protein metabolism

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the amount of toxic waste that can be converted into a harmless substance, and compares it to the amount of waste that is eliminated through a different process. It also optimizes the conversion process to minimize waste.
descriptions.approach: The procedure involves coupling the toxic waste to a key molecule, which then generates a harmless substance with an excess of a certain group. The process is repeated to generate the final product, which can donate groups to create other substances.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system converts a toxic form of nitrogen into a usable form by attaching it to a central molecule, then further modifies it to produce a compound that can transfer nitrogen to other molecules in a metabolic network.
descriptions.approach: A central molecule binds the toxic nitrogen, forming a first product. This product is then transformed into a second compound, which donates its nitrogen to other components, enabling the synthesis of additional nitrogen-containing molecules.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Teaching Case Discussions with Dr. Sonmezturk

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the effectiveness of a specific approach to facilitating discussions among medical professionals, using a series of case studies to compare the outcomes of different methods.
descriptions.approach: The approach involves using a set of pre-defined rules to evaluate the quality of discussions, based on a model that assesses the level of engagement and understanding among participants.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A pattern of clinical decision-making is inferred from sequences of patient encounters involving diagnostic uncertainty and real-time intervention choices.
descriptions.approach: A structured model analyzes temporal patterns in patient interactions, identifying recurring sequences of observations, responses, and outcomes to predict how decisions evolve under pressure and ambiguity.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Assessing the Documentation of Social Determinants of Health for Lung Cancer Patients in Clinical Narratives

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the importance of certain factors that affect health outcomes, and compares how well these factors are recorded in a type of written record. It aims to explain how these factors are recorded and how this can be used to improve future studies.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a computer program to analyze a large set of written records, identifying patterns and categories in the information. They then looked at how well these categories were recorded in each record.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system estimates how frequently and consistently various socioeconomic and environmental factors are mentioned across a large set of unstructured medical records.
descriptions.approach: It uses language processing to scan and classify text into predefined categories, then aggregates and analyzes the frequency of each category per individual record to identify patterns and gaps in reported information.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: New approaches to sap extraction from trees and comparison with conventional methods: new avenues for H and O stable isotopes ecohydrology

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the composition of a substance in different parts of a system, comparing the results to understand how the substance changes as it moves through the system. It aims to explain the source of the substance and the processes that affect its composition.
descriptions.approach: The procedure involves collecting samples from various compartments of a system, using a method that allows for direct sampling. The results are then compared to a standard reference point to calculate the contribution of different sources to the system.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The movement and transformation of fluid through a plant's structure is estimated, and how it changes along a vertical pathway from source to endpoint is compared across different sampling locations.
descriptions.approach: A continuous flow is sampled directly from the base to the top of a plant, and its composition is tracked as it moves through the system using real-time extraction under controlled conditions, with baseline measurements taken from a standard reference sample.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Influence of Ultrasonic Vibration towards the Microstructure Refinement and Particulate Distribution of AA7150-B4C Nanocomposites

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the effect of a specific technique on the properties of a material made from a metal alloy and a ceramic reinforcement. It predicts how the properties will change when the technique is applied to different amounts of the ceramic reinforcement.
descriptions.approach: The technique involves mixing the metal alloy and ceramic reinforcement together using a special method, and then applying a high-frequency vibration to the mixture. The researcher then examines the resulting material using various methods to analyze its properties and structure.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The effect of a controlled vibrational process on the uniformity and alignment of ceramic particles within a metal matrix is assessed, using physical and mechanical measurements to evaluate performance improvements.
descriptions.approach: A material is prepared with varying amounts of ceramic particles, subjected to a controlled vibrational treatment during mixing, then analyzed for internal structure, bonding, and strength under different conditions.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Towards a better understanding of wind-induced pressure-pumping - a chamber system to simulate dynamic fields of pressure fluctuations

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the effect of pressure changes on the movement of a certain substance through a network of tiny spaces. It compares the influence of different types of pressure changes on the movement of this substance.
descriptions.approach: The work uses a controlled system to simulate different types of pressure changes and measure their effect on the movement of the substance. It follows a procedure where pressure changes are created in a series of connected spaces and the movement of the substance is measured and compared.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The effect of oscillating pressure gradients on the movement of substances through a porous medium is estimated under controlled conditions, comparing lateral versus axial gradient dynamics across different environmental settings.
descriptions.approach: A system generates periodic pressure variations in a defined space, introducing time delays between regions to create directional pressure differences, then measures how these differences influence transport rates while isolating external variables.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Comparing electrical and infrared neural stimulation for intraoperative nerve monitoring

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the effectiveness of two methods for detecting damage to delicate tissues during a medical procedure. It compares the results of these methods to determine which one is better at detecting damage.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used data from an animal model to compare the performance of these two methods. They tested how well each method could detect damage of varying severity.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The performance of two distinct methods for detecting early signs of tissue disruption is evaluated under controlled conditions, comparing their ability to identify subtle changes in response to varying levels of perturbation.
descriptions.approach: A dynamic model simulates the response of a biological system to external inputs, applying two different signal delivery patterns and measuring the consistency and reliability of detected events across a range of perturbation intensities.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Circ_0036412 affects the proliferation and cell cycle of hepatocellular carcinoma via hedgehog signaling pathway

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the effect of a specific molecule on the growth and division of a type of cancerous tissue, comparing its impact on the rate of growth and the likelihood of the tissue dividing. It also predicts the role of another molecule in this process and explains how the first molecule affects it.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used various experiments to analyze the molecule's effect on the tissue's growth and division, including tests on the molecule's structure and how it interacts with other molecules. They also used techniques to study the molecule's role in the tissue's growth and division, such as observing how it affects the tissue's structure and function.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A regulatory RNA is overexpressed in a disease state and influences the rate of cell division and the timing of cell cycle progression by modulating a key signaling pathway.
descriptions.approach: The RNA binds to a specific microRNA to prevent its degradation, stabilizing a transcription factor. This factor enhances the activity of a downstream pathway, which in turn alters gene expression patterns that drive cell division and delay cell cycle arrest.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: The Role of Botanicals in Cardiovascular Health

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the effect of certain plant extracts on the release of a molecule that helps blood vessels relax, and compares it to the degradation of this molecule. It also predicts the potential benefits of these extracts on various health risks, such as high blood pressure and high cholesterol.
descriptions.approach: The researchers use data from preclinical studies to develop a model that predicts the effects of these plant extracts on the body. They follow a procedure that involves analyzing the data, creating a mathematical model, and testing the model with new data to refine it.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A quantity related to blood vessel function is estimated based on observed effects in living systems and laboratory models.
descriptions.approach: A model simulates how plant-derived compounds influence biological pathways, using data from controlled experiments to predict changes in vascular signaling and metabolic markers over time.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Association of retinol and carotenoids content in diet and serum with risk for Colorectal cancer: a meta-analysis

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the relationship between the levels of certain substances in food and the risk of a particular disease. It compares the risk of the disease in people with different levels of these substances.
descriptions.approach: The researchers searched for studies that looked at the levels of these substances in people's food and blood, and then combined the results to see if there was a pattern. They used statistical software to analyze the data and draw conclusions about the relationship between the substances and the disease risk.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A quantitative synthesis of evidence is performed to assess the relationship between exposure levels of specific organic compounds in food and biological samples and the likelihood of developing a particular type of disease.
descriptions.approach: Multiple studies are systematically reviewed and their numerical outcomes are combined using statistical methods to compute an overall effect size, adjusting for differences in study design, population, and measurement context.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Blue lupin (Lupinus angustifolius L.) ‒ the results of varieties and accessions study according to adaptivity and a set of commercialbiological traits
