descriptions.problem: A system's behavior under varying conditions is inferred from observed interactions and environmental signals, with focus on how dynamic shifts in cellular states influence long-term outcomes and response to external interventions.
descriptions.approach: A model tracks state transitions in response to stimuli, using feedback loops to simulate how persistent signals drive persistent changes in function and behavior over time.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Safety Features

descriptions.problem: This work aims to estimate the likelihood of patient injury from equipment malfunctions in operating rooms, and to identify the most effective ways to prevent such injuries. It compares the effectiveness of different safety protocols and procedures.
descriptions.approach: The approach involves evaluating the performance of various safety features and procedures, and optimising them to reduce the risk of patient injury. It uses data from preoperative and intraoperative checks to inform its recommendations.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system estimates the likelihood of a medical device malfunctioning due to improper physical or electrical conditions during use, based on preoperative checks and real-time operational feedback.
descriptions.approach: The system evaluates device status by comparing current operational parameters against known safe thresholds, using a structured diagnostic protocol that accounts for environmental and power system characteristics.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: General financial economic equilibria

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the optimal financial decisions for a group of entities, comparing their outcomes to a baseline scenario. It predicts the best course of action to achieve a desired level of financial stability.
descriptions.approach: The study uses a mathematical model to compare the outcomes of different financial decisions, following a procedure that involves identifying the key factors influencing financial stability, formulating a set of possible decisions, and evaluating their outcomes using historical data.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system of interdependent decisions is analyzed to determine how agents' choices collectively influence outcomes across a network of interacting components under shared constraints.
descriptions.approach: A set of rules defines how each agent's behavior responds to observed conditions and feedback from others, iteratively adjusting until no agent can improve their outcome by changing strategy alone.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Multi-Stable Origami Structures with Thick Panels

descriptions.problem: A system is designed to transition between multiple stable states, where each state is independently set and maintained under mechanical load. The transitions are triggered by small inputs, and the system maintains stability in each state without external support.
descriptions.approach: A geometric framework is built where folding patterns allow independent stabilization at distinct shapes. Each shape is supported by a network of connected segments that maintain rigidity through local curvature and distributed stress distribution.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the optimal design of structures that can switch between multiple stable states, with the ability to change the stable states as desired. It predicts the performance of these structures and compares them to simpler designs.
descriptions.approach: The approach involves designing and analyzing structures with specific properties, then manufacturing and testing them. The procedure follows a set of rules to create structures with multiple stable states, allowing for more flexibility and design options.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

topic_name: Fibromyalgia and Chronic Fatigue Syndrome Research
title: Physiotherapists’ adherence to Clinical Practice Guidelines in fibromyalgia: a cross-sectional online survey

descriptions.problem: A measure is derived from expert responses to assess how consistently practitioners apply established recommendations in managing a chronic condition involving persistent pain and functional limitations.
descriptions.approach: Respondents evaluate a set of predefined statements about patient assessment and care delivery. Their answers are grouped into categories based on alignment with standard protocols, and consensus is determined by the proportion of agreement across the group.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the level of knowledge and practice of professionals in a specific area, comparing their understanding and actions to established guidelines. It aims to explain the consistency of their practices and identify areas for improvement.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used an online survey to collect data from a large group of professionals, classifying them into three categories based on their level of knowledge and practice. They then compared the results to various factors, such as academic level and previous training, to identify statistically significant differences.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Can Hibiscus Sabdariffa Decrease Blood Pressure in Menopause Women with Hypertension?

descriptions.problem: This research aims to determine the effect of a certain substance on the pressure of a fluid in the body of women who experience a certain condition, which is known to cause the fluid pressure to rise. The researchers estimate that this substance may help reduce the fluid pressure.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a simple experiment with two groups, one that received the substance and one that did not, and compared the results to see if the substance had an effect. They used a statistical test to determine if the difference in pressure was significant.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A change in a physiological parameter is assessed over time in a group exposed to a treatment and a group not exposed, using repeated measurements to determine if the treatment induces a statistically significant shift.
descriptions.approach: Two groups are assigned a standard care and one receives an extract-based intervention. Measurements are taken before and after the intervention period, and differences are compared using statistical testing to evaluate the treatment's effect.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Depth-Guided Dehazing Network for Long-Range Aerial Scenes

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the depth of objects in images taken from far away, predicts the clarity of these images, and compares the clarity of different images to determine which one is clearer. It also optimizes the clarity of images by removing the effect of distance on the image quality.
descriptions.approach: The approach involves using a model to extract depth information from images, then using this depth information to guide the removal of distance-related effects from the image. The model integrates depth information with the features of the image to focus on the areas that need the most improvement.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A method estimates the three-dimensional structure of a wide-field view from a single two-dimensional image, using spatial variations in lighting and contrast to infer depth. It then uses this structure to refine the restoration of visual clarity across distant regions where lighting conditions vary dramatically.
descriptions.approach: The system first infers depth by analyzing how light intensity and texture change across the image. It then applies a weighted adjustment to each region, where regions at greater depth receive more influence based on their spatial context and lighting gradients.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: AGRICULTURAL ENTERPRISE DEVELOPMENT STRATEGY AND ITS EFFICIENCY IN THE MODERN ECONOMIC CONDITIONS

descriptions.problem: A system is evaluated to determine how effectively its internal operations support long-term resilience and performance under varying external pressures and disruptions.
descriptions.approach: A set of predefined response patterns is applied to simulate interactions between operational decisions and environmental changes, with performance measured across stability, adaptability, and growth under different conditions.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the efficiency of different strategies for improving the sustainability of a complex system in uncertain economic conditions. It compares the effectiveness of various approaches to achieve this goal.
descriptions.approach: The study uses a combination of systemic analysis and process thinking to develop a methodology for evaluating the sustainability of complex systems. It identifies key factors that influence the success of these strategies and provides a framework for their implementation.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Propolis Reduces Inflammation and Dyslipidemia Caused by High-Cholesterol Diet in Mice by Lowering ADAM10/17 Activities

descriptions.problem: This study investigates the effect of inhibiting certain enzymes on inflammation and heart disease in mice. It aims to estimate the impact of a specific substance on these conditions.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used mice with high cholesterol to test the effect of a substance on heart disease. They compared the results to mice without high cholesterol.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A biological system's response to a high-fat diet is assessed, measuring levels of inflammatory markers, lipid abnormalities, and enzymatic activity involved in tissue damage and immune activation.
descriptions.approach: A compound is administered to suppress a specific enzyme complex that drives inflammatory and metabolic dysfunction. Tissue and blood samples are analyzed for changes in metabolic, immune, and structural indicators over time.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Design for Office Health and Wellbeing: A Design Space Exploration

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the effectiveness of various design strategies on promoting healthy habits among employees, predicts which strategies are most likely to succeed, compares the impact of different approaches, optimizes the design of healthy environments, and explains how these strategies can be used to improve employee well-being.
descriptions.approach: The research uses a systematic analysis of 40 unique designs, applying a set of criteria to evaluate and compare the design strategies, and presents the findings in a clear and concise manner.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A set of interventions is evaluated to determine which enhance employee physical and mental engagement during routine tasks, based on observed patterns of behavior and environmental interactions.
descriptions.approach: A structured framework is applied to analyze diverse intervention methods, grouping them by mechanism and outcome, then identifying which combinations consistently support sustained attention and reduced stress in daily operations.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Inspection of defects in composite structures using long pulse thermography and shearography

descriptions.problem: This work estimates and compares the quality of composite structures, using data from thermal imaging and visual inspections to determine the size and presence of internal damage. It also optimizes the use of these methods to improve detection accuracy.
descriptions.approach: The procedure involves using thermal imaging to detect internal damage, and then using visual inspections to confirm and quantify the damage. The methods are combined to leverage their complementary advantages and improve detection accuracy.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system estimates the size and location of internal discontinuities in layered materials by analyzing responses to thermal stimulation, comparing results across different sensing mechanisms to determine which provides more accurate spatial and dimensional information.
descriptions.approach: A sequence of thermal pulses is applied to a surface, and the resulting surface response is captured over time. The data from two distinct sensing strategies are processed and cross-validated to infer the size and position of internal anomalies, with adjustments made to minimize measurement error.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Synthesis of Poly(diphenylenephthalide) from 3,3-Bis(4-bromophenyl)phthalide

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the yield of a chemical reaction and optimizes the conditions for a more efficient process. It compares the results of different methods to determine the best approach.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a specific type of catalyst to speed up the reaction and a controlled environment to test different conditions. They applied a chemical reaction to a specific type of molecule to create a new material.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A repeating chain structure is formed from a monomer and a coupling agent, using a transition metal catalyst to link molecular units through a specific bond formation pathway.
descriptions.approach: A monomer is activated and reacts with a halogenated aromatic compound via a metal-catalyzed bond-forming reaction, resulting in a polymer chain through repeated condensation and bond formation.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Relapsing polychondritis associated with pustular psoriasis successfully treated with secukinumab: a case-based review

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the effectiveness of a treatment for a rare condition that combines two separate diseases, one of which is an autoimmune disorder affecting cartilage and connective tissue, and the other a skin condition characterized by inflammation and lesions.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a new treatment to try and cure the condition, and monitored the patient's symptoms over time to see if the treatment was successful.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A pattern of chronic inflammation affecting connective tissues and skin is observed in a patient with comorbidities. The relationship between this inflammation and a distinct skin condition is evaluated to determine if shared underlying mechanisms exist.
descriptions.approach: A treatment is initiated and monitored over time. Clinical responses are tracked to assess whether a single therapeutic agent can resolve both systemic and skin manifestations of the condition.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

topic_name: Parasitic infections in humans and animals
title: Comparison of clinicopathological features between cerebral cystic and alveolar echinococcosis: analysis of 27 cerebral echinococcosis cases in Xinjiang, China

descriptions.problem: This work estimates and compares the characteristics of two types of diseases that affect the same organ, trying to distinguish between them. It aims to explain the differences in how these diseases manifest clinically, through imaging, and through microscopic examination of tissue samples.
descriptions.approach: The researchers collected data from 27 cases of a specific disease, comparing the clinical features, imaging results, and microscopic characteristics of two types of the disease. They then analyzed and compared these data to identify the differences between the two types of disease.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A distinction is made between two types of disease based on clinical, imaging, and microscopic traits, aiming to identify patterns that differentiate one from the other in terms of onset age, spread, and tissue structure.
descriptions.approach: Cases are analyzed by comparing age at onset, number and location of affected areas, imaging appearance, and tissue structure under magnification, using standardized criteria to classify and interpret differences in morphology and surrounding tissue response.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: MORINGA OLEIFERA, FUNCTIONAL INGREDIENT: NUTRITIONAL PROPERTIES AND HEALTH BENEFITS

descriptions.problem: This study aims to determine the effects of a certain plant on people's physical and mental well-being, specifically its ability to improve concentration and reduce fatigue. It estimates the benefits of consuming this plant in different amounts.
descriptions.approach: The researchers divided participants into two groups and asked them to consume varying amounts of the plant over a set period. They then asked participants to fill out surveys before and after consuming the plant to assess the effects.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A group of individuals consumes a specific plant-based substance at two different dosages over a set period and evaluates changes in their daily energy levels, mental clarity, and overall physical sensations before and after consumption.
descriptions.approach: Participants are assigned to two dosage groups and complete structured self-assessments at baseline and after a fixed duration. Responses are compared across groups to determine the relative impact of dosage size on perceived physiological and cognitive outcomes.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

subfield: Public Health, Environmental and Occupational Health
title: P-515 The morphokinetic signature of high-level mosaic embryos in time-lapse ART analysis

descriptions.problem: This study estimates the time it takes for certain types of cells to develop and mature in a laboratory setting, comparing how fast they develop compared to cells with no abnormalities and cells with a small number of abnormalities.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a technique called time-lapse imaging to observe the cells in real-time, taking note of how long it takes for them to go through certain stages of development, and then compared these times to see if there were any differences.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system estimates how quickly a biological process unfolds across key developmental stages, comparing outcomes between samples with different genetic composition levels.
descriptions.approach: It analyzes time intervals between sequential events in a dynamic process, using statistical models to detect differences in timing patterns based on the proportion of cells with altered genetic content.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Unauthorised Access to Computer Information: The Motives for Committing a Crime

descriptions.problem: This study aims to identify the underlying reasons that drive individuals to secretly access and use information from computers. It examines a large dataset of court cases related to this issue.
descriptions.approach: The researchers analyzed 300 court cases, looking for patterns and commonalities. They categorized the cases into two groups: those driven by financial gain and those not driven by financial gain.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A pattern is identified in a set of incidents where individuals gain unauthorized entry to protected systems, with a focus on the underlying personal reasons driving such actions, especially when financial or personal outcomes are involved.
descriptions.approach: Incidents are grouped by the nature of the personal goal behind the action—whether financial benefit, data acquisition, or personal retribution—and analyzed to determine which patterns correlate with specific behavioral outcomes.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Physicochemical properties and in silico binding interaction with gyrase B of antibacterial compounds from aquous extract of Hibiscus sabdariffa L.

descriptions.problem: This study aims to identify which substances in a plant extract have strong interactions with an enzyme that helps bacteria grow, and to predict how these substances might behave in the body.
descriptions.approach: The researchers first evaluated the properties of 10 substances using a set of rules, and then used a computer simulation to see which ones interacted best with the enzyme. They then used another computer tool to predict how these substances might behave in the body.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A set of molecular candidates is evaluated for their interaction strength with a key bacterial enzyme target, with emphasis on binding affinity and safety profiles derived from physicochemical and toxicity predictions.
descriptions.approach: Molecular candidates are filtered by structural rules and binding energy scores. High-affinity binders are assessed for metabolic stability and adverse effects using computational models to rank their potential as effective and safe agents.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Visual effects on tactile stimulation and its perception: A pilot study using near-infrared spectroscopy

descriptions.problem: This work investigates how visual information affects brain activity when people try to trace a shape with their finger, and whether the shape's complexity affects this effect. It aims to understand the underlying mechanisms of how our brain processes visual and sensory information.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a non-invasive technique to measure brain activity while participants traced a shape with their finger, comparing the results to when they didn't trace anything. They tested different shapes and visual information levels to see how it affects brain activity.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The system estimates how visual input influences physical interaction perception, and how the detail of physical movement patterns affects brain responses during repeated actions.
descriptions.approach: It compares neural responses when visual cues align with or conflict with physical movement, using varying movement frequencies and controlled movement conditions to isolate the impact of visual-motor alignment.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: The Mechanical-Electrical-Thermal Integrated Design Method for the Stable In-Orbit Electrical Performance of the Cable-Membrane-Truss Antenna

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the performance of a complex system under various conditions, compares its performance to a baseline, and optimizes its design to achieve a desired level of stability. It uses data from the system's initial state and its performance at different points to make predictions and improvements.
descriptions.approach: The system is analyzed using a combination of different fields of study, including the way the system's components interact with each other and their environment. The analysis is done using a simulation model that takes into account the system's initial state and its performance at different points.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system's performance under varying environmental conditions is predicted and optimized to maintain consistent output across a range of operational states.
descriptions.approach: A unified model links structural behavior, environmental exposure, and functional output. Design parameters are adjusted to minimize variation in performance, using real-time environmental and structural data as input.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Monoallelic missense variants in MAB21L1 cause a novel autosomal dominant microphthalmia

descriptions.problem: A genetic factor is identified that, when present in one copy of a gene, leads to a specific pattern of developmental abnormalities limited to the eyes, distinct from a different condition involving multiple organ systems.
descriptions.approach: Genetic data from affected individuals are analyzed to detect a single-copy change in a gene. This change is then correlated with clinical features across multiple families to determine its association with a specific eye-related disorder.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: This research investigates the relationship between a specific gene and a particular condition, estimating the likelihood of the gene causing the condition in individuals. It compares the genetic data from multiple families to determine the frequency and impact of the gene on the condition.
descriptions.approach: The researchers use a combination of genetic data and literature reviews to identify the gene's role in the condition. They then analyze the genetic data from multiple families to determine the inheritance pattern and clinical presentation of the condition.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Oral immunization against foot-and-mouth disease virus using recombinant Saccharomyces cerevisiae with the improved expression of the codon-optimized VP1 fusion protein

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the effectiveness of a new way to make a specific part of a virus that causes foot-and-mouth disease in animals. It compares the immune response of mice to different versions of this part of the virus.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a combination of trial and error to find the best way to attach a specific part of the virus to a microorganism. They tested different versions of the attachment and found that one version worked best.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system is designed to produce a specific antigenic component in a living host cell culture, optimizing its yield through genetic modifications and environmental control to trigger a measurable immune response when administered orally.
descriptions.approach: A genetic construct links the antigen to a stabilizing partner sequence, with expression boosted at lower temperatures. Immune markers are measured in response to the administered agent in a living organism.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Methods for Studying Signaling Proteins and Networks

descriptions.problem: This work aims to estimate the structure and function of complex networks of molecules that transmit information within living organisms, comparing and optimising their interactions to understand how they work.
descriptions.approach: It uses various tools and approaches to characterise and characterise these networks, including analysis of individual components and characterisation of entire systems within living organisms.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system's dynamic behavior is inferred from observations of how components interact over time, including changes in activity levels and response patterns under varying conditions.
descriptions.approach: A mathematical framework maps input stimuli to output responses through a network of interacting units, using temporal sequences of measurements to update state transitions and predict future behavior under new conditions.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: The mechanism for the formation of a rational fund of gas turbine engines

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the economic benefits of creating a pool of spare equipment for emergency use. It compares the costs and benefits of this approach to other options.
descriptions.approach: The method involves modeling the performance of a complex system to identify the most efficient way to maintain it. It uses data from the system's operation to inform the model and make predictions about its future performance.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system is evaluated to determine the optimal set of backup units to deploy under variable operational demand, based on usage patterns, failure rates, and economic costs across different scenarios.
descriptions.approach: A simulation model integrates historical operational data and stochastic failure probabilities to predict demand fluctuations and assigns units to reserve pools based on cost-benefit analysis and availability thresholds.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: COGNITIVE CAPABILITIES AND PROSPECTS OF A NEW LOOK AT THE NATURE AND NATURE OF MANAGEMENT DECISIONS

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the effectiveness of different approaches to finding the best solution from a variety of options, and compares them to identify the most efficient one. It aims to explain how individuals can use their cognitive abilities to make better decisions.
descriptions.approach: The approach involves designing a process to create an effective sequence of micro-solutions, taking into account both logical and accidental factors. It seeks to understand the nature of individual decision-making and use it to improve decision-making processes.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system identifies and evaluates a set of possible outcomes from a complex environment, aiming to determine the most effective sequence of small, actionable choices.
descriptions.approach: It models the process as a dynamic sequence where each step is influenced by both structured reasoning and unpredictable elements, using iterative refinement to build a coherent and adaptive pathway from initial options to final action.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Fecal microbiome predicts treatment response after the initiation of semaglutide or empagliflozin uptake

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the impact of a new class of medications on the balance of tiny life forms in the digestive system of people with a certain health condition. It also tries to predict how well these medications will work based on the types of tiny life forms present at the start.
descriptions.approach: The researchers analyzed samples of waste and bodily fluids from people before and after taking these medications, and used statistical methods to compare the results and identify patterns.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A model estimates how pre-existing biological conditions influence changes in clinical outcomes following the start of a therapeutic intervention, using longitudinal physiological measurements and compositional data from biological samples collected over time.
descriptions.approach: The model analyzes repeated observations from individuals over several time points, applying statistical tests to detect associations between early biological states and later outcome shifts, then identifies patterns that correlate with measurable response changes.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: A Case of Posterior Tracheal Wall Rupture During Tracheostomy Treated With Sternocleidomastoid Muscle Reinforcement

descriptions.problem: A rare but life-threatening complication of a medical procedure is being treated with a surgical intervention to repair damage to a vital organ. The goal is to prevent further damage and promote healing.
descriptions.approach: A surgical procedure is being used to repair damage to a vital organ, with a secondary goal of reinforcing a weakened area to prevent further damage. The procedure involves a combination of direct suturing and a secondary surgical intervention to achieve this goal.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A critical breach in a central airway structure occurs during a medical intervention, leading to uncontrolled fluid escape due to impaired patient awareness. The extent and risk of further leakage are assessed from clinical observations and real-time physiological feedback.
descriptions.approach: A surgical repair is performed using a nearby tissue with strong structural integrity and reliable vascular supply. The tissue is repositioned and anchored to stabilize the weakened area, with both open and minimally invasive techniques used to ensure secure closure.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Mental health and its relationship to the development of positive thinking among a sample of students at the University of Baghdad

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the relationship between the well-being of a group of young people and their ability to develop a more optimistic outlook on life. It compares the effects of different factors on this relationship.
descriptions.approach: The researcher uses data from a sample of young people to build a model that predicts how their well-being affects their outlook on life. The model is based on a series of steps that involve collecting data, analyzing it, and using the results to make predictions.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A pattern of internal cognitive orientation is assessed to determine its influence on an individual's resilience and emotional regulation under academic stress.
descriptions.approach: A statistical model correlates observed behavioral and emotional responses with self-reported cognitive tendencies, adjusting for environmental and social variables to identify predictive relationships.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Optimal Auction Design with User Coupons in Advertising Systems

descriptions.problem: The task is to estimate the optimal way to design a system where users can buy products or services at a lower price in exchange for seeing ads, and to compare the revenue and welfare of the system with and without this feature.
descriptions.approach: The system uses data on how users interact with ads to determine the best way to offer discounts, and then uses this information to optimize the revenue of the system.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system estimates the best way to offer incentives to users to influence their engagement and conversion with a product, aiming to maximize revenue while ensuring users benefit and are motivated to act.
descriptions.approach: The system evaluates different incentive levels across user interactions, models user response patterns, and selects a strategy that balances user participation and platform gains under constraints of fairness and motivation.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Make Graph Neural Networks Great Again: A Generic Integration Paradigm of Topology-Free Patterns for Traffic Speed Prediction

descriptions.problem: This work aims to estimate the future speed of moving objects in urban areas, using patterns that are not dependent on the connections between these objects. It also compares and optimizes these patterns to improve the accuracy of the predictions.
descriptions.approach: The approach involves developing a new model that can learn patterns that are not dependent on the connections between objects, and then using this model to improve the accuracy of existing models that rely on connections.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system estimates future values of a dynamic process based on historical observations and spatial relationships, while also capturing non-spatial, scale-invariant patterns that evolve over time.
descriptions.approach: A model learns from multi-scale temporal and spatial features using a structured attention mechanism. It then transfers knowledge from a pre-trained system to a new model, enabling the latter to combine spatial structure with independent, non-geometric dynamics.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: VEXAS syndrome was in front of us for decades

descriptions.problem: A pattern of disease presentation is identified in older individuals with specific inflammatory and blood-related symptoms, and a subset of patients is suspected to have a previously unrecognized condition based on shared clinical features and laboratory findings.
descriptions.approach: A search is conducted across medical literature using combinations of symptom terms and blood disorder indicators. Patient groups with overlapping signs and blood abnormalities are analyzed to detect a consistent, previously overlooked disease pattern.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the prevalence of a rare disease in a specific population, comparing it to other conditions. It predicts that this disease may have been previously identified in clinical research, but was not correctly diagnosed.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a combination of keywords to identify relevant studies, then reviewed articles that mentioned both the disease and other conditions that might be related to it. They excluded articles that didn't meet certain criteria, such as narrative reviews or case reports.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

topic_name: Psychiatric care and mental health services
title: Evaluating Adherence to Rapid Tranquilization Protocols in Psychiatric Emergencies: An Audit of a Tertiary Care Facility in Pakistan

descriptions.problem: This study estimates the effectiveness of a specific treatment protocol in a psychiatric facility, predicts the likelihood of certain interventions, and compares the actual practices to established guidelines. It also explains the reasons behind the deviations and optimizes the treatment process.
descriptions.approach: The researchers analyzed patient records to assess the sequence of interventions, the choices of interventions, and the documentation of patient monitoring. They applied statistical methods to analyze the data and identify areas for improvement.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A pattern of intervention sequences is evaluated to determine how consistently prescribed care steps are followed, including pre-treatment checks and monitoring after action. The frequency and timing of actions are compared across cases to identify deviations and gaps in procedural consistency.
descriptions.approach: Patient encounter logs are reviewed to trace the sequence of actions taken. Each step is checked against a defined care pathway, and deviations are recorded. Post-action observation is assessed for completeness and timing.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: The efficacy of low/lactose-free milk powder in the treatment of lactose intolerance in infants: A protocol for systematic review and meta analysis

descriptions.problem: This work aims to estimate the effectiveness of a specific type of food in helping a common condition in young children, and to compare the results of different studies to provide evidence-based guidance. It also aims to explain the benefits of this food in a way that can be applied to real-world situations.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a systematic search of existing studies to gather data, and then analyzed the results using a statistical software program to identify patterns and trends. They compared the results of different studies to draw conclusions about the effectiveness of this food.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A quantitative assessment is made to compare how well a dietary intervention reduces symptom duration and improves patient outcomes relative to standard care, using data from controlled studies involving human participants.
descriptions.approach: Studies are systematically identified, data extracted, and combined using statistical methods to evaluate differences in outcome measures between groups receiving the intervention and those receiving standard care.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Analysis of Water Discharge and Draining Time for Pump Types in Ship Leakage Draining Systems

descriptions.problem: This research aims to determine the most efficient method for removing excess liquid from a vessel, given a specific type of leak, and to compare the performance of different types of devices used for this purpose.
descriptions.approach: The study used a controlled experiment with a prototype vessel, with a small leak introduced, and tested four different types of devices that can remove excess liquid. The results were then compared to determine which device is most effective.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The rate at which fluid is removed from a compromised enclosure is measured under controlled conditions, and the time required to empty the enclosure is predicted for different removal mechanisms.
descriptions.approach: A physical setup simulates fluid ingress through a defined aperture. Four distinct removal systems are tested under identical conditions, and their performance is evaluated by tracking the volume of fluid removed per unit time and the time to achieve full evacuation.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: A Comprehensive Review on Melamine: Insights into Risks and Detection Techniques

descriptions.problem: A system estimates the presence and concentration of a nitrogen-rich compound in a food-based product that is intentionally added to misrepresent its protein content, using chemical and physical signals from the sample.
descriptions.approach: A model analyzes signals from multiple detection methods to identify and quantify the compound, comparing results across techniques to determine its level and consistency in different sample types.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: This work aims to estimate the risks and detection techniques for a common additive used to artificially increase the protein content of various food products and industrial materials. It compares the effects of this additive on human health and the environment.
descriptions.approach: The approach involves comparing the effects of this additive on human health and the environment, using data from various sources, including news reports and scientific studies. It uses analytical techniques such as mass spectroscopy and high performance liquid chromatography to detect and quantify the additive's presence.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Mutual Support Phenomenon: Voices of Students With Written Language Disorders

descriptions.problem: A pattern of interaction is identified in which individuals share experiences and strategies to enhance understanding and performance in a challenging context.
descriptions.approach: A structured analysis is applied to observed behaviors and exchanges, identifying recurring roles such as role modeling, validation, and collaborative problem-solving during learning episodes.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: This study aims to understand how individuals with a specific learning difficulty support each other, and how this support affects their learning outcomes. It estimates the importance of certain social skills, such as seeking recognition and modelling learning activities, in this process.
descriptions.approach: The researchers use a method that involves gathering data from individuals with this learning difficulty, and then analyzing this data to identify patterns and relationships. They follow a procedure that involves collecting and categorizing the data, and then using this data to make predictions about the effectiveness of different support strategies.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Association of Nosocomial Burns and Bacterial Colonization in Iraqi Patients

descriptions.problem: This study aims to identify the types of bacteria that cause infections in patients who have been injured by a severe form of trauma, and to determine which antibiotics are effective against these bacteria.
descriptions.approach: The researchers collected samples from the injured patients and tested them in a laboratory to see which bacteria grew, and then tested the bacteria to see which antibiotics they were resistant to.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The relative frequency of microbial species present in wound environments is estimated from physical samples collected under controlled conditions, and their response to various antimicrobial agents is assessed.
descriptions.approach: Microbial growth is detected through culture-based detection, and species identity is determined by biochemical and automated testing. Antimicrobial effectiveness is evaluated by measuring survival under exposure to a set of chemical agents.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Examining the Effects of Cultural Context on Consumer Behavior

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the impact of a complex set of influences on individual behavior, comparing different dimensions and trends to understand how they shape attitudes, beliefs, and actions.
descriptions.approach: It uses a multidimensional framework to analyze how various categories, such as geographical location and group affiliations, affect thinking and behavior, and optimizes its findings by considering current trends and influences.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A pattern of human actions and decisions is analyzed to determine how shared societal norms and inherited beliefs shape individual choices in response to environmental and social cues.
descriptions.approach: A structured model groups individuals by inherited social frameworks and evaluates how these groupings influence behavior under varying conditions, using repeated observations and contextual variables to identify consistent behavioral trends.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Analisis finansial usaha ternak ayam ras petelur (studi kasus CV Muara Puncak di Desa Muara Putih Kecamatan Natar)

descriptions.problem: This research aims to evaluate the financial viability of a business by comparing its expected income and expenses, and determining whether it is a good investment opportunity. It estimates the potential return on investment and payback period.
descriptions.approach: The study uses a case study approach, analyzing data from primary and secondary sources. It calculates key financial metrics, such as net present value, internal rate of return, and return on investment, to make a feasibility judgment.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system's profitability is assessed by estimating key performance indicators from operational and financial data, including return on investment, time to recover costs, and rate of return relative to capital expenses.
descriptions.approach: Data from a single operational unit is analyzed using a structured model that computes net value over time, evaluates cost recovery thresholds, and compares expected returns to baseline investment costs.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: (Invited) Large Electromechanical Coupling in Zr-Doped Ceria

descriptions.problem: This work investigates how the addition of a small amount of a certain metal ion to a material affects its ability to change shape in response to an electric field. It estimates the amount of change and compares it to other materials.
descriptions.approach: The researchers use a combination of data and calculations to understand the changes. They compare their results to other materials and use computer simulations to model the changes.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A material's response to an electric field is measured, including how much it deforms and how its internal structure changes under field influence, especially when the field is strong and rapidly varying.
descriptions.approach: A model simulates how atomic-scale distortions shift in response to electric fields, showing that certain small impurities cause large, dynamic deformations that persist across a wide range of frequencies and lead to significant structural changes.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Advancing polar motion prediction with derivative information

descriptions.problem: This study aims to improve the accuracy of predicting the position of the Earth's axis over time, which is essential for various applications such as navigation and climate studies. It estimates the position of the axis based on historical data and optimizes the model to reduce the error.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a combination of two methods: one that uses historical data to make predictions and another that uses a mathematical formula to analyze the patterns in the data. They tested this approach with different sets of data and compared the results to find the most accurate one.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system estimates the future values of two continuously changing variables based on past observations and their rates of change, aiming to improve accuracy in short-term predictions.
descriptions.approach: The model combines linear fitting with a statistical method that links current and past values of the variables and their rates of change, testing multiple input sets to determine which yields the most consistent and precise future estimates.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Participation of Chloride Channels in Cardiovascular and Kidney Health. Effects of High Chloride Diets on Blood Pressure in an Experimental Model of Saline Overload

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the effect of high salt intake on blood pressure in a model of excessive salt consumption. It predicts the role of chloride channels in this process and compares the effects of different salt and chloride combinations.
descriptions.approach: The study uses an experimental model with rats, where different groups are fed with varying salt and chloride combinations for a set period. The researchers then measure and compare various physiological and biochemical markers to understand the effects of these combinations.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The influence of a high concentration of a negatively charged ion on physiological stress responses and blood pressure regulation is assessed using animal models exposed to varying ionic environments over time.
descriptions.approach: Animals are exposed to controlled ionic conditions for a set duration, then monitored for changes in systemic pressure, tissue inflammation markers, and gene expression related to ion transport and stress response pathways.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Industrial Development Report 2024

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the impact of a certain sector on overall economic and social progress, comparing its contribution to green innovation and its effect on job creation in other sectors. It aims to explain why this sector is crucial for achieving a set of global development goals.
descriptions.approach: The report uses data on green innovation and job creation to estimate the sector's impact. It compares the sector's contribution to other sectors and explains why it is essential for achieving the desired development goals.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system estimates the economic ripple effects of technological innovation, predicting how growth in one sector influences employment and output across interconnected domains.
descriptions.approach: It models sectoral interdependence using weighted feedback loops, where innovation in one domain triggers downstream activity, and evaluates the relative contribution of different technological pathways to long-term environmental and social outcomes.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: A Novel TCN-LSTM Hybrid Model for sEMG-Based Continuous Estimation of Wrist Joint Angles

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the angles of a joint in the human body from a signal that reflects the electrical activity of muscles. It aims to improve the accuracy of this estimation by combining two different types of neural networks.
descriptions.approach: The approach combines two neural networks: one that looks at local patterns in the signal and one that remembers long-term patterns. The combined model is then tested on a dataset of real signals to see how well it works.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system estimates real-time changes in a joint's angular position from continuous physiological signal streams, using patterns in the signal over time and across short and long temporal windows.
descriptions.approach: A model processes signal segments with local pattern recognition followed by long-term temporal context integration, combining short-term feature extraction with memory of past signal dynamics to refine predictions.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Outcomes of children with long-segment and total colon Hirschsprung disease following pull-through.

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the outcomes of a group of individuals with a congenital disorder that affects their digestive system, caused by the absence of certain nerve cells. It predicts the likelihood of certain problems, such as bowel movements and infections, and compares the results across different groups.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a descriptive analysis approach, examining data from individuals who underwent a specific surgical procedure to treat the disorder. They followed up with these individuals over time to assess their outcomes and identify any potential issues.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The functional recovery and risk of post-surgical inflammation are estimated from clinical records of individuals who undergo a specific surgical intervention for a congenital condition involving absent nerve cells in the digestive tract.
descriptions.approach: A structured surgical procedure is applied, and outcomes are evaluated using standardized scoring systems for bowel control and signs of inflammation, with results compared across different surgical techniques and patient subgroups.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Evaluation of the Polyphenolic Content and of Acetylcholinesterase Inhibition Activity of Ginkgo biloba (Ginkgo biloba L.) Leaf Extracts Obtained in Subcritical Water

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the effectiveness of different methods for obtaining a substance from Ginkgo biloba leaves, and compares the results to determine which method produces the most effective substance. It also explains the relationship between the substance's properties and its effectiveness.
descriptions.approach: The procedure involves using a substance obtained from Ginkgo biloba leaves in different ways, and measuring the effect of each method on the substance's properties. The method used is to compare the results of different methods to determine which one produces the most effective substance.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A quantitative relationship is established between the concentration of specific bioactive compounds in a plant material and the strength of its ability to inhibit a key enzyme involved in a biological process affecting neural function.
descriptions.approach: Samples are prepared under varying conditions, and their compound levels are measured alongside enzyme suppression data. A statistical model links compound concentration to inhibition potency, identifying optimal conditions for maximizing biological effect.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Recent updates on the influence of iron and magnesium on vascular, renal, and adipose inflammation and possible consequences for hypertension

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the impact of certain substances on the health of specific organs and tissues, and compares their effects to determine the most effective treatment. It also predicts the consequences of these substances on the overall health of an individual.
descriptions.approach: The researchers use data from animal studies and experiments to develop a treatment plan. They follow a procedure that involves identifying the substances' effects on specific organs and tissues, and then testing the effectiveness of a treatment, such as chelation therapy, to reduce the negative impact.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The effect of internal nutrient levels on tissue responses in metabolic and circulatory systems is assessed, particularly in contexts where chronic disease states are linked to persistent cellular stress and immune activation.
descriptions.approach: A computational model evaluates how changes in nutrient availability influence cellular behavior across multiple organ compartments, using longitudinal data from biological systems under varying conditions to predict outcomes and identify intervention points.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: CoSec: On-the-Fly Security Hardening of Code LLMs via Supervised Co-decoding

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the likelihood of generating vulnerable software from a large language model, predicts the effectiveness of a security model in guiding the model's generation towards more secure code, and compares the results across different models.
descriptions.approach: The approach involves training a smaller security model to guide the generation of a target model, adjusting the probability distributions of model outputs during each step, and improving the average security ratio of the target model by 5.02%-37.14% while maintaining its functional correctness.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system estimates the likelihood that generated software artifacts contain flaws, using external evidence from known secure patterns and real-time feedback during creation.
descriptions.approach: A compact model is trained to evaluate and prioritize safe outputs, then dynamically adjusts the generation process by influencing the probability of selecting safer options at each step without altering the core model's internal structure.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Associations between income/employment status and diabetes care processes, health behaviors, and health outcomes in Japan: A cross‐sectional study using claims data linked to a questionnaire survey

descriptions.problem: This study estimates the associations between income level and various health behaviors and outcomes, such as medication use, health habits, and hospitalization rates, in a specific population. It compares these associations across different income groups.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a combination of data from health records and surveys to analyze the relationships between income level and health outcomes. They used statistical models to identify patterns and associations in the data.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The task is to quantify how different levels of financial stability and time spent in structured activities relate to patterns of health-related behaviors and outcomes across a population.
descriptions.approach: It uses statistical models to compare groups based on income and activity levels, adjusting for known influences, and estimates the strength and direction of associations through weighted comparisons and regression analysis of observed patterns.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Load frequency control performance enhancement of an electric vehicle integrated time-delay multi-microgrid system

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the performance of a system that manages the balance of energy supply and demand, comparing different scenarios to determine the best outcome. It predicts how the system will behave under various conditions and optimizes the results to achieve the best possible outcome.
descriptions.approach: The system uses a mathematical model to simulate different scenarios and test the performance of a proposed solution. It follows a procedure that involves optimizing a complex system using a specific algorithm to achieve the best possible outcome.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system with multiple interconnected units responds to sudden changes in power demand or supply. The performance of this response is evaluated based on how quickly and accurately key operational variables return to equilibrium under varying conditions and uncertainties.
descriptions.approach: A dynamic control mechanism is tuned using an iterative optimization process. It adjusts its parameters in response to time delays and system variations to minimize response time and improve stability across different operating scenarios.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Nonepisodic angioedema with eosinophilia subsequent to acute parvovirus B19 infection

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the occurrence of a specific condition in a subset of individuals who have been exposed to a particular stimulus. It predicts the likelihood of this condition developing in response to the stimulus.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a combination of clinical observations and laboratory tests to identify the condition and determine its cause. They followed the individual's symptoms over time and used a specific treatment to alleviate the symptoms.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A single, prolonged episode of localized swelling in the limbs is observed alongside a rise in a type of white blood cell count, occurring after a viral illness with known acute onset and recovery.
descriptions.approach: A clinical timeline is constructed from symptom onset and laboratory markers, and the response to a short-term anti-inflammatory treatment is evaluated to determine if the swelling and cellular response are linked to the illness and resolve with intervention.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Effects of blood extraction and ecophysiological experiments on stress in adult males of Liolaemus attenboroughi

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the effect of laboratory experiments on the stress levels of a certain type of animal, comparing stress indicators from blood samples to various physical characteristics. It aims to explain how these experiments affect the animal's stress state and physical condition.
descriptions.approach: The researchers took blood samples from the animals at different times and analyzed the data to compare the stress indicators with the animal's physical characteristics, such as temperature, speed, and body condition.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A quantitative measure of an organism's physiological state is assessed over time in response to handling and experimental manipulation. Changes in this measure are compared across different time points and conditions to determine the impact of disturbance on internal balance.
descriptions.approach: A repeated sampling protocol is applied to monitor a biological indicator over several days. Data are aggregated and compared across time points to detect trends, with statistical analysis identifying significant shifts in response to external handling.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Elizabethkingia meningoseptica Bacteremia in a Newborn at the University Hospital Yalgado Ouedraogo, Burkina Faso: A Case Report

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the risk of infection from a certain type of environmental microorganism in a specific population, and compares it to the effectiveness of various treatments. It aims to reduce the number of deaths and illnesses caused by this type of infection.
descriptions.approach: The researchers use data from a specific medical facility to identify cases of infection and compare the outcomes of different treatments, with the goal of finding the best approach to prevent further infections.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A clinical outcome is monitored over time in a vulnerable patient group, with attention to infection severity and response to treatment based on available medical records and laboratory results.
descriptions.approach: A sequence of health indicators is tracked, and treatment decisions are evaluated against known patterns of disease progression and antimicrobial resistance in similar cases to guide future interventions.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: UCTB: An Urban Computing Tool Box for Building Spatiotemporal Prediction Services

descriptions.problem: A system estimates how environmental conditions evolve over space and time, using local patterns and regional boundaries to improve accuracy and clarity of forecasts.
descriptions.approach: It integrates domain-specific rules with spatial segmentation, applies advanced predictive models, and iteratively refines outputs based on regional behavior and historical trends.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: This work aims to improve the performance and interpretability of a complex system that predicts future events based on past data, taking into account various types of knowledge and different ways of dividing the data into regions.
descriptions.approach: It uses a novel workflow that combines two key factors to design and implement a system that can handle multiple types of knowledge, support different methods for dividing the data, and use advanced models simultaneously.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Journalism, Social Media, and Wars of Position

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the impact of a new technology on the balance of power between different groups, comparing the benefits and drawbacks of its adoption. It predicts how this technology will shape the relationships between these groups over time.
descriptions.approach: The study uses historical data on the use of a particular medium to understand how it has influenced the balance of power. It then applies this understanding to the new technology, using a combination of quantitative and qualitative analysis to identify its potential effects.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The extent to which diverse populations can influence public discourse through digital tools is assessed, especially in settings where traditional channels are restricted.
descriptions.approach: A model analyzes patterns of communication flow and user engagement across networks, identifying how information spreads and gains traction under different conditions of access and control.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Adenocarcinoma of the appendix presenting as chronic small bowel obstruction: A case report

descriptions.problem: An unknown growth in the small intestine is causing severe and persistent problems, such as heavy bleeding and weakness, and needs to be diagnosed and treated. The growth is likely to be a type of cancer, but it's rare and can be difficult to diagnose.
descriptions.approach: A medical team used imaging tests to find the problem, and then performed surgery to remove the growth and affected tissue. The team also used laboratory tests to confirm the diagnosis and monitor the patient's recovery.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A rare, slowly progressing tumor is identified in a patient with persistent digestive blockage and unexplained systemic blood loss, despite normal responses to common gastrointestinal triggers.
descriptions.approach: Imaging detects a localized mass causing mechanical disruption of the digestive tract. Surgical exploration confirms the mass, and histological analysis determines its cellular characteristics, guiding a comprehensive resection and long-term monitoring plan.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Possible Mechanisms Of Action Of Light Inert Gases On Chemiluminescence Arising As A Result Of Lipid Peroxidation

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the effect of a certain type of molecule on a biological process that occurs when a molecule breaks down and releases energy. It predicts how this effect might happen and compares it to other known effects on the same process.
descriptions.approach: The procedure follows two possible ways: one involves changing the way the molecule interacts with a key component of the biological process, and the other involves changing the way the molecule affects the way energy is released from the broken-down molecule.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system's response to a physical perturbation is estimated, particularly how that perturbation alters the rate and efficiency of a chain reaction involving reactive intermediates and energy transfer.
descriptions.approach: The perturbation is introduced in a medium with distinct phases, altering local environment properties. A model evaluates how changes in phase boundary dynamics and energy dissipation affect reaction kinetics and the stability of transient states.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Learning with Structural Labels for Learning with Noisy Labels

descriptions.problem: The task is to train a complex model using imperfect data, where the model's performance is compromised by incorrect or misleading information. The goal is to improve the model's performance despite the presence of incorrect data.
descriptions.approach: The approach involves using a complex algorithm to refine the model's performance by selecting the most accurate data points and reducing the impact of incorrect data. The algorithm uses a technique called reverse k-NN to improve the model's feature representation and prevent over-fitting.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system estimates correct outcomes from uncertain observations by identifying consistent patterns in how data points relate to one another across a network of associations.
descriptions.approach: It uses a reverse neighborhood rule to find stable groupings in data, then refines predictions by emphasizing consistency among related instances during training.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Chemistry of Mandarin Citrus reticulata

descriptions.problem: A pattern of bioactive molecules is identified across different plant tissues, with their chemical structures and biological effects being assessed to determine which types are most prevalent and functionally significant.
descriptions.approach: A systematic analysis groups molecular structures by functional groups and biological activity, then maps their abundance and known effects across various plant parts and environmental conditions.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the properties of various substances found in a plant, and compares them to known effects on the body. It predicts how these substances might interact with other substances in the body.
descriptions.approach: The study uses data from various experiments and observations to identify and summarize the substances found in the plant, and their effects on the body.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Soil Water Flow Affected by Vegetation Root Water Uptake in the Semiarid Region of Mu Us Sandy Land, China

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the impact of roots on the movement of moisture through the ground in a dry region, comparing the effects of different types of plants on the moisture levels and evaporation rates.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used field experiments to study the movement of moisture through the ground, measuring the moisture levels and evaporation rates in different areas with and without plant roots, and comparing the results to understand the effects of roots on moisture movement.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system observes how plant roots influence the movement and distribution of moisture in the upper layers of land, affecting how much moisture is lost to the atmosphere and how much enters deeper layers.
descriptions.approach: The system simulates a natural landscape with and without plant roots, tracking moisture flow over time. It adjusts the flow based on root activity, modeling how moisture is drawn from the upper layers and redirected, altering surface and subsurface dynamics under stress conditions.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Integrated transcriptomics and metabolomics analysis reveal the molecular mechanism of unsaponifiable matter in delaying aging

descriptions.problem: This research aims to understand how a certain substance delays the effects of aging on cognitive function. It estimates the impact of this substance on aging and cognitive dysfunction.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a controlled experiment with mice to test the substance's effects. They analyzed changes in the mice's bodily functions using various methods to identify the underlying mechanisms.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system is analyzed to understand how a compound influences biochemical activity in a biological context, specifically by measuring changes in small molecule levels and gene expression patterns across different conditions.
descriptions.approach: A computational model integrates data from molecular and genetic profiles to identify pathways affected by a compound, then maps interactions between metabolic fluxes and gene regulation to infer functional outcomes in cellular function.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: EVALUATION OF THE EFFECTIVENESS OF WEBSITES OF JCI ACCREDITED HEALTHCARE FACILITIES: A COMPARATIVE GLOBAL ANALYSIS FROM A HEALTH TOURISM PERSPECTIVE

descriptions.problem: This research aims to evaluate the effectiveness of certain online platforms used by facilities that provide medical services to visitors from other countries. It estimates the level of quality and usefulness of these platforms.
descriptions.approach: The researchers analyzed data from 139 online platforms to compare their content and effectiveness in providing information and services to visitors. They used a content analysis procedure to identify areas for improvement.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system evaluates how well digital platforms convey service details, support visitor navigation, and present facility features to attract users seeking reliable, accessible, and well-informed experiences across diverse geographic regions.
descriptions.approach: A structured analysis compares digital content across multiple locations using predefined criteria, assessing performance in clarity, completeness, user guidance, and alignment with user expectations through systematic observation and scoring.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Basal Implant - A Boon to Immediate Implant Loading: A Case Report

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the effectiveness of a new type of device in rehabilitating a patient with a road traffic injury, and compares it to traditional methods. It predicts the success of the device in various scenarios, including cases with poor quality tissue.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a combination of data and evidence to evaluate the device's performance. They inserted the device into the patient's tissue and loaded it with a fixed dental appliance, then assessed the results.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A restoration strategy is evaluated for stability and success under functional loading in scenarios where the supporting structure is irregular or compromised.
descriptions.approach: A set of anchoring elements is placed directly into compromised or non-uniform tissue sites and connected to a fixed prosthesis, enabling early functional use without prior tissue augmentation.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: APPLICATION OF DIGITAL TECHNOLOGIES IN THE MANAGEMENT OF THE EDUCATIONAL INSTITUTION

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the impact of new technologies on educational institutions, comparing their effectiveness to traditional methods. It aims to explain how these technologies can improve the learning process and administrative activities.
descriptions.approach: The study follows a procedure where it examines current trends and examples of technology application, using data and evidence from various sources to inform its conclusions.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system estimates how changes in operational procedures affect learning outcomes and administrative performance across different institutional settings.
descriptions.approach: It analyzes patterns in recorded activities and resource usage to simulate outcomes under various management strategies, adjusting inputs to find configurations that balance efficiency and student engagement.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Evaluation and pollution analysis of water environment of state-controlled river in Zaozhuang City from 2016 to 2022

descriptions.problem: A system's environmental health is assessed over time using physical, chemical, and biological indicators collected from multiple locations. The performance of the system is evaluated across years, with trends in pollutant levels and overall condition being compared to identify patterns and sources of degradation or improvement.
descriptions.approach: A composite scoring model aggregates multiple measured properties into a single health metric. This metric is computed annually and compared across locations and time periods to detect changes, identify dominant pollution sources, and guide targeted intervention strategies.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: This research estimates and compares the quality of a certain environment over time, using data from various parameters and pollutants. It aims to explain the factors that affect this quality and propose strategies for improvement.
descriptions.approach: The study uses a combination of data analysis and evaluation indices to assess the environmental quality. It then identifies the main sources of pollution and proposes control measures and optimization strategies based on these sources.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Interesting, oftentimes even trendy! Attitudes of medical students regarding spa medicine

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the level of interest in a certain type of health treatment among a group of young people, and compares it to their own health behaviour. It also predicts which groups of people are more likely to be interested in this type of treatment.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a survey to collect data from a large group of young people, and then analyzed the results to identify patterns and trends. They used a visual scale to measure people's opinions about the treatment, and compared the results to their own health habits.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A group of future healthcare professionals is assessed on their interest in and personal engagement with health practices involving natural environments and thermal interventions, and how these relate to their views on the relevance of such practices in formal education.
descriptions.approach: Respondents rate their belief in the modernity and effectiveness of specific wellness routines using a continuous scale. Their self-reported participation in related behaviors is recorded and linked to perceived relevance of these practices in medical training.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Meckel's diverticulum: A challenging diagnosis

descriptions.problem: This research aims to understand and describe the characteristics and outcomes of a specific medical condition in a subset of patients who present with unusual or challenging cases. It estimates and explains the patterns and barriers to identifying this condition.
descriptions.approach: The researchers collected data from a group of patients who were diagnosed with this condition and presented with unusual cases. They used statistical methods to analyze the data and identify patterns and barriers to identifying the condition.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman
