descriptions.approach: The researchers use a specific technique to analyze the food samples, and then compare the results to established limits. They follow a procedure that involves extracting the substances from the food, then using a machine to detect and measure their levels.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Drugs of the future: humic acids

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the potential benefits of a naturally occurring, organic compound on human health, comparing its effects to those of other substances. It aims to explain how this compound can be used to improve health outcomes, particularly in relation to cancer treatment.
descriptions.approach: The study uses data on various types of cancer and their treatment, as well as information on the compound's properties and effects on human physiology. It follows a procedure that involves analyzing and comparing the compound's effects to those of other substances.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system's impact on biological and environmental health is evaluated across diverse applications, including disease resistance, productivity, and protective effects in living organisms and ecosystems.
descriptions.approach: A model analyzes interactions between natural organic compounds and biological systems using empirical observations from varied environments, adjusting predictions based on exposure history and response patterns across species and conditions.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Predicting postoperative complications after cytoreductive surgery and hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy: retrospective cohort study

descriptions.problem: A model estimates the likelihood of a negative clinical outcome following a major surgical procedure, based on patient characteristics measured before surgery.
descriptions.approach: The model uses binary logistic regression to identify which pre-surgical factors are linked to adverse events. It then combines these factors into a single predictive score that assigns a probability to each patient.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: Estimate the risk of severe outcomes after a treatment that is effective but potentially highly morbid, based on variables that can be measured before the treatment.
descriptions.approach: Use a mathematical model to combine these variables and predict the risk of severe outcomes, and then test this model on a separate set of data to see how well it works.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Leiomyomatosis peritonealis disseminata associated with large uterine myoma without history of surgery: A case report and review of literature

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the presence of a rare benign disease in a patient with a large abdominal mass, comparing it to known cases and reviewing the literature. It predicts the disease's association with a specific type of tissue and its potential link to a particular medical procedure.
descriptions.approach: The researchers use a combination of clinical observations, pathological examination, and review of existing literature to identify the disease and its characteristics. They follow a procedure that involves closely examining the patient's abdominal cavity and performing a specific medical operation to confirm the diagnosis.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A pattern of widespread smooth muscle growth is identified on the inner lining of the abdominal cavity, occurring alongside a large, solitary mass in a patient with no prior invasive procedures or hormonal exposure.
descriptions.approach: A postoperative examination of tissue samples reveals extensive, well-defined nodules with a uniform cellular structure, and the pattern is correlated with the presence of a large, solitary mass and absence of prior invasive events.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Diagnostic Performance of Uric Acid‐to‐Albumin Ratio for Detecting the Presence and Severity of Isolated Coronary Artery Ectasia

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the presence and severity of a condition that affects the inner lining of a major blood vessel, and compares it to other indicators of inflammation. It aims to identify individuals at high risk of developing this condition and to guide preventive measures.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used data from 440 patients, comparing different groups to see if a specific ratio of two substances in the blood is higher in those with the condition. They also looked at how well this ratio predicts the severity of the condition and how it compares to other markers of inflammation.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A numerical ratio derived from two biological measurements is evaluated to distinguish individuals with a specific condition from those without it, and to assess its ability to predict disease severity across different clinical subgroups.
descriptions.approach: The ratio is computed from lab values and compared across groups using statistical tests. Its association with disease presence and progression is assessed through correlation and regression analysis, adjusting for known confounding factors.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Human monocyte inflammation in patients with Lp(a) or atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease is not accompanied by changes in chromatin accessibility in circulating classical monocytes

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the effect of high levels of a certain protein on the behavior of a type of cell, and compares it to cells from people with low levels of the protein. It also predicts the levels of certain chemicals in the blood of people with high levels of the protein.
descriptions.approach: The researchers collected blood samples from people with high and low levels of the protein, and analyzed the behavior of a specific type of cell from these samples. They used various techniques to measure the behavior of these cells and the levels of certain chemicals in the blood.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The level of a specific lipid-related protein in the blood is associated with increased expression of a gene involved in interferon signaling, and elevated levels of a chemokine are observed in individuals with high lipid levels.
descriptions.approach: Blood samples are collected from individuals with varying levels of a lipid-related factor and matched for age and sex. Gene expression and protein levels are measured in isolated immune cells. No differences in the openness of regulatory DNA regions are found between groups.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Preface

descriptions.problem: Estimate the number of researchers attending the conference, and compare the results to the actual attendance. Also, explain the theme of the conference and how it relates to the attendees' backgrounds.
descriptions.approach: Use a statistical model to analyze the data from the organizers' report, and apply a regression analysis to predict the attendance based on the number of invited speakers and the conference theme.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system is designed to forecast how changes in one environmental factor affect interconnected outcomes in isolated communities, using observed patterns from multiple local settings.
descriptions.approach: It applies a relational model that maps input variables to output indicators through iterative comparison and adjustment, using historical and real-time data from diverse regional sites to refine predictions over time.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Distribution and antibiotic susceptibilities of Stenotrophomonas maltophilia isolates detected in Ümraniye Training and Research Hospital

descriptions.problem: A pattern is estimated in a population of bacterial infections over time, tracking how frequently they appear and how strongly they resist common antimicrobial treatments across different patient groups and sample types.
descriptions.approach: Data from patient samples are collected annually and categorized by source and clinical setting. Resistance trends are computed by comparing resistance frequencies across years and sample types using standardized testing protocols.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: This study estimates the distribution of a certain type of bacteria in patients' samples from different clinics, and compares the resistance rates of this bacteria to various antibiotics over time. It also explains the increasing importance of this bacteria due to the rising prevalence rates and antibiotic resistance.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a device to identify the bacteria in 410 samples from 295 patients, and then tested the bacteria's susceptibility to various antibiotics using established guidelines. They compared the results over three years to see if the bacteria's distribution and resistance rates changed.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Modernization of Shilajit Processing: Comparative Phytochemical Screening, Antioxidant Potential, and Phenolic Content in Standardized vs. Non- Standardized Extracts

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the composition and properties of a substance, comparing its quality and safety in different forms. It predicts the effects of processing on the substance's properties and optimizes the process to enhance its safety and efficacy.
descriptions.approach: The procedure involves analyzing the substance's composition and properties using various techniques, such as spectroscopy and microscopy. The results are then compared and validated to determine the effects of processing on the substance's quality and safety.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A process is evaluated to determine how effectively it preserves and enhances the concentration of bioactive molecules while removing harmful inorganic components present in a natural substance.
descriptions.approach: A controlled workflow is applied to transform the substance through physical separation and purification steps. The resulting product is analyzed using spectral and chemical techniques to compare molecular profiles, functional group signatures, and elemental presence across different batches.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Effect of Lifestyle Modifications on Fertility and Menstrual Regularity among Infertile Obese Women with Polycystic Ovarian Syndrome

descriptions.problem: This research aims to determine the impact of changes in daily habits and physical activity on the ability to conceive and regulate body cycles in individuals with a hormonal disorder, who are overweight and have irregular periods.
descriptions.approach: The study uses a comparison method, where a group of people with a hormonal disorder, who are overweight and have irregular periods, are compared to a control group after making changes to their daily habits and physical activity over a period of six months.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A change in daily habits is evaluated to determine its impact on reproductive function and cycle consistency in individuals with hormonal imbalances and elevated body mass.
descriptions.approach: Participants undergo a structured intervention involving dietary adjustments and physical activity tracking over six months, with outcomes measured through repeated assessments of hormonal response and cycle pattern stability.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Manual annotation of Robson criteria and obstetric entities: Inter-annotator agreement and initial NER models implementation

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the accuracy of a classification system for medical records, comparing the results of different models to determine which one performs best. It also explains the effectiveness of these models in identifying specific entities within the records.
descriptions.approach: The researchers created a dataset of medical records, manually identifying and categorizing specific information. They then trained and evaluated several machine learning models to see which one could accurately identify these entities.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system identifies and classifies specific pieces of information within medical records, distinguishing between different types of events, treatments, and outcomes based on patterns in textual data.
descriptions.approach: The system trains on manually reviewed examples to recognize key events and their associated details, then applies learned rules to new records using models that weigh evidence and adjust predictions based on context and consistency.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Is ozone a reliable proxy for molecular oxygen?

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the relationship between two quantities: one is a measure of the presence of a certain molecule (molecular oxygen), and the other is a measure of the presence of a different molecule (oxygen's photochemical product). The goal is to determine if the second quantity can be used to infer the first quantity.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a combination of mathematical models and computer simulations to explore this relationship. They varied the levels of the second quantity and the levels of a third quantity (a reducing species) to see how it affects the relationship.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system is analyzed to determine how the presence and concentration of a reducing compound affect the stability and production of a photochemically formed gas, depending on the energy output of the light source and the overall chemical environment.
descriptions.approach: Simulations are run across a range of gas concentrations and light intensities to track the rates of formation and destruction of the photochemically formed gas, adjusting for chemical feedbacks and energy absorption in different environmental conditions.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: School Adjustment

descriptions.problem: This work aims to estimate the level of adjustment in a group of individuals, comparing their internal feelings to the perceptions of teachers and parents. It also seeks to identify the characteristics of those who adjust well to a particular environment.
descriptions.approach: The approach involves using data from multiple sources to predict the adjustment level of individuals. It follows a procedure of comparing and optimising the fit of different models to the data.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A pattern of discrepancy is observed between external observations of an individual's engagement in structured environments and their internal sense of belonging and progress within those settings.
descriptions.approach: A framework evaluates reported behaviors, achievements, and emotional responses across multiple sources to detect mismatches. It then maps these to internal self-reports and adjusts weights based on consistency across time and context to infer underlying emotional and cognitive alignment.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

subfield: Public Health, Environmental and Occupational Health
title: Long-term mitochondria-endoplasmic reticulum complexes in the oocytes and early embryos of a matrotrophic pseudoscorpion Chelifer cancroides

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the role of a specific structure in the growth and development of a type of female reproductive cell. It predicts how this structure changes and behaves over time, and compares its behavior to other cellular components.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used various microscopy techniques to observe and analyze the structure's behavior and changes. They followed the structure's behavior over time, from early growth to early embryonic development.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system tracks the spatial and functional state of cellular energy units during development, estimating how their activity and distribution change over time in response to developmental cues and cellular organization.
descriptions.approach: The system observes and records the movement, shape, and metabolic state of energy units in a structured cellular environment, then models their integration into stable, low-activity partnerships that persist through early developmental stages and are unevenly distributed during cell division.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Why come to the office? Investigating employee return to office in hybrid work

descriptions.problem: The system estimates why individuals select or reject a shared physical environment for work, based on personal needs, environmental control, and social interactions, using self-reported experiences and observed behaviors in real-world settings.
descriptions.approach: It analyzes patterns in user reports and sensor-derived activity logs to map how routines, preferences, and social behaviors align with environmental features and usage frequency over time.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: This study investigates why people choose to work from home or come to a central location, and what factors influence their decision. It aims to understand the reasons behind people's preferences for working from home or in a central location.
descriptions.approach: The study uses a combination of interviews with people who work from home and those who work in a central location to gather information. It involves asking questions about their experiences, challenges, and preferences, and analyzing the data to identify patterns and trends.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Ayurveda Management of PCOS Related Anovulatory Infertility: A Case Study

descriptions.problem: This research aims to estimate the effectiveness of an alternative treatment approach for a specific health issue, comparing the outcomes of this approach to conventional treatments. It predicts the success rate of this approach in improving a particular health outcome.
descriptions.approach: The research follows a holistic treatment protocol, involving a combination of detoxification, nourishment, and hormonal regulation techniques. It uses a case study to evaluate the success of this approach in improving a specific health outcome.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A treatment protocol is applied to a patient with prolonged reproductive failure and irregular menstrual cycles, aiming to restore hormonal balance and improve the likelihood of conception through a structured, individualized intervention.
descriptions.approach: A multi-step regimen begins with systemic detoxification, followed by targeted nutritional and hormonal support, and concludes with a procedure designed to influence central regulatory mechanisms governing reproductive function.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction and Coronary Artery Pseudoaneurysm

descriptions.problem: This work identifies a rare condition where a blood vessel is damaged and filled with blood, causing symptoms that can range from mild to severe. It estimates the likelihood of this condition occurring without any known cause.
descriptions.approach: The researchers use data from electrocardiography, echocardiography, and imaging tests to diagnose the condition. They follow a procedure that involves comparing the test results to identify the damage and estimating the severity of the condition.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A rare condition is identified where a structural abnormality in the heart's vascular network presents with electrical signal patterns typical of tissue damage, despite no clear cause or prior intervention.
descriptions.approach: Electrical activity is monitored over time to detect abnormal waveforms. Structural imaging is used to locate a mass that fills a cardiac chamber and responds to contrast injection, revealing a vascular malformation with unexpected electrical features.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

topic_name: Synthesis and pharmacology of benzodiazepine derivatives
title: AFFINITY OF NEW POTENTIAL LIGANDS OF THE GABAA-RECEPTOR COMPLEX AND TSPO RECEPTORS OF THE CNS – cis-3-ARYLIDENE-7-BROMO-5-ARYL-1,2-DIHYDRO-3H-1,4-BENZODIAZEPIN-2-ONES

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the affinity of new compounds for specific binding sites in the brain, comparing their ability to displace known radioligands. It predicts the effect of introducing a chlorine atom into the molecule on its affinity for these sites.
descriptions.approach: The procedure involves synthesizing new compounds, studying their affinity using radioligand analysis, and determining the effect of substituent positions on their binding tropism.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The binding strength of a class of molecules to two distinct biological targets is assessed, using experimental data from in vitro binding assays with labeled probes to measure displacement efficiency.
descriptions.approach: A systematic variation of substituent position and type on a core molecular scaffold is introduced, and the resulting binding potency is evaluated through competitive inhibition assays in membrane-derived biological samples.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Single immunization with the attenuated strain “Volgograd/14c” of the ASF virus does not protect piglets from infection with the homologous strain “Stavropol 01/08”

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the effectiveness of a single immunization with a weakened virus against infection with a similar, more virulent virus, and compares the outcomes in vaccinated and unvaccinated groups. It aims to explain why a particular vaccine candidate failed to protect against a specific disease.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a weakened virus to immunize a group of animals, then challenged them with a more virulent version of the same virus to see how their immune systems responded. They measured the animals' immune responses and clinical signs to determine the vaccine's effectiveness.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The protective effect of a single dose of a weakened pathogen is assessed against a virulent version of the same pathogen, using biological indicators of infection and immune response.
descriptions.approach: Animals are exposed to a weakened version of the pathogen to trigger an immune response. Later, they are challenged with the full-strength version. Disease progression, immune markers, and viral load in blood are monitored and compared across groups.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Exploring Anti-TNF Therapy in Relapsing Polychondritis with Co-Existing Ulcerative Colitis: A Case Report and Literature Review

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the effectiveness of a treatment for a rare condition that causes inflammation in joints and airways, and compares it to another treatment for a related condition that causes inflammation in the digestive system. It also predicts whether a different treatment might be more effective.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used data from a patient's medical history and literature reviews to inform their decision. They followed a procedure where they tested the first treatment, then considered alternative treatments based on the results.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A pattern of co-occurring conditions is evaluated to determine whether one condition may be triggered or worsened by treatment for another, based on observed responses over time.
descriptions.approach: A patient's response to a specific intervention is monitored and compared to historical cases. If the intervention suppresses one condition but not another, a different intervention is proposed based on prior outcomes in similar situations.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Grammar and Genre: A Short Study in Imagism

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the patterns of how thoughts and experiences are structured into a specific type of text, in order to help understand how to translate these thoughts into that text. It compares different patterns to see which ones work best.
descriptions.approach: It uses a combination of existing ideas and data to develop a new way of thinking about how to structure thoughts and experiences into a specific type of text. The procedure involves analyzing patterns in a type of text and using this analysis to make predictions about how to structure thoughts and experiences in a similar way.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The process estimates how abstract mental states are transformed into structured sequences of meaning through selective omission and emphasis of elements.
descriptions.approach: It applies a rule-based transformation that prioritizes concise expression by removing redundant or explanatory components, then evaluates how such reductions affect the coherence and emotional impact of the resulting form.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Use of Stingless Bee Honey (Meliponinae Subfamily) in Wound Treatment: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis

descriptions.problem: This research aims to summarize and compare the effectiveness of a natural substance in treating a specific type of injury, particularly in cases where the injury is difficult to heal. The goal is to determine if this substance is a viable alternative to existing treatments.
descriptions.approach: The researchers will analyze data from studies that tested the substance's ability to reduce the size of the injury, promote tissue growth, and prevent infection. They will compare the results to those of standard treatments or no treatment.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The effectiveness of a natural, bioactive substance in promoting tissue repair and reducing infection in chronic conditions is evaluated across diverse biological models and human trials.
descriptions.approach: A structured review of studies is conducted, extracting outcomes related to tissue recovery and infection suppression. Data from multiple sources are combined and analyzed to determine the overall impact and consistency of the effect across different settings and conditions.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

topic_name: Food Security and Health in Diverse Populations
title: Housing costs and food purchasing characteristics: The role of SNAP participation and SNAP purchasing power

descriptions.problem: The relationship between living expense pressure and daily consumption patterns is examined, specifically how local cost pressures influence the quantity and nutritional value of items acquired by individuals and families.
descriptions.approach: A statistical model evaluates how variations in local cost burdens affect consumption behavior, adjusting for household and regional differences, and identifies when higher costs lead to reduced intake or shifts in item selection.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the association between housing costs and how households allocate their budget for basic needs, such as food. It also explores how the level of support from a government program affects this association.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used data from a large survey to analyze how housing costs affect households' budget for basic needs. They used a statistical method to compare the effects of housing costs on households' budget and the impact of government support on these effects.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Thermographic Evaluation of Thermophysical Properties in Bio-Based Foams for Automotive Interior Components

descriptions.problem: This study aims to estimate the thermal properties of materials made from waste cooking oil, and compare them to those made from virgin materials. It also predicts how these materials will behave under different conditions.
descriptions.approach: The researchers use a non-destructive technique to analyze the materials' thermal behavior without touching them. They compare the results to those from established methods that measure density and thermal conductivity.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The system estimates how variations in material composition affect heat transfer dynamics across a sample's surface over time, using spatially resolved temperature responses under controlled heating conditions.
descriptions.approach: A periodic heating pulse is applied to a sample, and the resulting surface temperature changes are recorded over time. These responses are analyzed to infer internal structural and compositional differences through pattern recognition and signal decomposition.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: SOLSPEC-NG: a compact UV spectrometer for high-precision solar spectral irradiance monitoring on a CubeSat platform

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the amount of energy from a specific type of light that is emitted by the Sun and affects the Earth's atmosphere. It aims to provide precise and continuous measurements of this energy to study its impact on the atmosphere and improve space weather forecasting.
descriptions.approach: The approach involves using a compact device with two mirrors that rotate to measure the light in a specific range, providing high-resolution data. The device is designed to be small and portable, making it suitable for use on a small satellite platform.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A precise, continuous measurement of ultraviolet light intensity across a defined wavelength range is estimated from time-series observations of incoming electromagnetic radiation in a specific atmospheric window.
descriptions.approach: A dual-filter system rotates around a central axis to separate and record light intensity at fine wavelength intervals using diffraction-based separation, with data processed to resolve variations in light distribution across a narrow band.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Diverging associations of traditional versus social media with government trust

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the relationship between traditional media use and trust in government, predicts the effect of social media use on trust, and compares the impact of traditional and social media on trust across different groups. It aims to explain why some people trust government more when they use traditional media.
descriptions.approach: The researchers use a large dataset with multiple waves of participants to analyze the associations between media use and trust. They follow a procedure where they first analyze the data, then control for other factors, and finally compare the results to identify patterns and relationships.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A pattern is estimated in how different forms of information exposure relate to public confidence in authority figures, especially when considering how these exposures change over time and differ across demographic groups.
descriptions.approach: A longitudinal model compares the timing and strength of associations between information consumption habits and shifts in confidence, adjusting for individual-level differences and identifying when one behavior precedes changes in belief.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Improvement in Safety and Productivity in Underground Mining Operations: A Review of the Role and Efficiency of Autonomous Mining Technologies

descriptions.problem: This work aims to estimate the efficiency of using autonomous technologies to improve safety and reduce costs in a complex, high-risk environment where workers are exposed to hazards such as unstable structures, accidents, and toxic substances.
descriptions.approach: The approach involves comparing the effectiveness of autonomous technologies, such as robots and sensors, with traditional methods to identify areas for improvement and optimize safety and efficiency.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system estimates the impact of automated systems on human risk exposure and operational output in a constrained, high-risk environment where environmental conditions change dynamically and human presence is limited.
descriptions.approach: It analyzes historical operational data and real-time sensor inputs to model outcomes under varying automation levels, then compares performance across scenarios to identify patterns in risk reduction and output stability.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Appendix: Animal Bones from Area B

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the number of animal bones found in a specific area, compares it to a known quantity, and optimizes a model to make a more accurate prediction. It uses data from various sources to support its findings.
descriptions.approach: The procedure involves collecting and analyzing data from different types of evidence, such as drawings and photographs, to make a more accurate estimate. The model is optimized through a process of comparison and refinement, using a team of experts and laborers to guide the process.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A pattern of material remains is analyzed to determine the relative abundance and distribution of different types of biological remains across a defined spatial region.
descriptions.approach: A grid-based sampling method is applied to group observations by location. Statistical clustering identifies recurring associations between types of remains and environmental contexts, enabling inference about past human activity and resource use.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Statutes of the International Committee on Systematics of Prokaryotes – July 2025 revision

descriptions.problem: An estimate of the outcome of a vote among a group of experts is presented, along with the actual outcome and the text of the revised rules that were approved.
descriptions.approach: The outcome of the vote was estimated based on the opinions of the group's members, and the revised rules were presented as a result of this estimation, with the actual outcome being the approved text.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A group of experts has evaluated and finalized a set of governing rules for an organizational framework, deciding on the most appropriate version based on consensus and input from members.
descriptions.approach: The process involves collecting feedback from stakeholders, analyzing proposed changes, and selecting a version that achieves broad agreement through structured voting and iterative review.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Using the EU Environmental Permitting Framework to Promote the Energy Transition in the Western Balkans – The Case of Kosovo

descriptions.problem: A system is evaluated to identify obstacles preventing the integration of new, low-emission power sources into a national grid, based on historical project approvals and spatial planning records.
descriptions.approach: A standardized assessment framework is applied to each project, evaluating alignment with environmental and spatial criteria, and recommending procedural changes to improve consistency and reduce delays in approval processes.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: Estimate the effectiveness of a set of policies aimed at increasing the use of renewable sources and energy storage systems, and identify the main barriers to their implementation.
descriptions.approach: Use a set of tools and guidelines to assess the current situation and propose practical reforms to overcome the identified barriers and advance the transition to cleaner sources.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Failure mechanisms of landslide dams with different materials: laboratory experiment and physical analysis

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the impact of different materials on the failure of structures that obstruct rivers and are prone to natural disasters. It predicts the peak flow generated by the failure of these structures and compares the results with experimental data.
descriptions.approach: The study uses a numerical simulation model to analyze the failure process and a large-scale experiment to test the model's predictions. The model's reliability is validated by comparing the results with the experimental data.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The rate and intensity of a sudden release of material from a barrier are estimated under identical inflow conditions, comparing how different internal compositions affect the speed and volume of the release.
descriptions.approach: A physical setup simulates the barrier's response to water pressure, and a computational model reproduces the dynamics using known physical laws, adjusting parameters to match observed outcomes and identifying key factors influencing the release behavior.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Pengaruh Tayangan TVRI Sumsel Terhadap Minat Masyarakat Dalam Konten Budaya Lokal

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the influence of a local program on people's interest in local content, predicts whether the program will have an effect, compares the effect to other factors, optimizes the content to make it more engaging, and explains the results based on data from a survey, observation, and documentation.
descriptions.approach: The research uses a quantitative approach with a survey, observation, and documentation to collect data, and then analyzes the data using statistical methods to determine the relationship between the program and people's interest in local content.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A measure of public engagement with locally relevant content is estimated based on observed viewer responses and program exposure data. The relationship between exposure to a public media source and interest in regional traditions is assessed using statistical analysis of survey and observational evidence.
descriptions.approach: A model evaluates how frequent and consistent exposure to a regional media program correlates with viewer interest in local traditions. It uses regression and hypothesis testing to determine if changes in exposure lead to measurable shifts in public attention.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Hand, foot, and mouth disease in children: forecasting of future research direction using bibliometric analysis

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the future direction of research in a common health problem that affects many people, especially in a specific geographic region. It predicts which areas of research will continue to develop and identify potential new areas to improve treatment.
descriptions.approach: The study uses a large dataset of published research to identify patterns and trends. It then uses a network approach to map the predicted research directions and identifies potential new areas to improve treatment.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A pattern of scientific inquiry is identified across a 27-year period of published work, aiming to forecast emerging research priorities based on evolving thematic focus and connectivity among studies.
descriptions.approach: A network of thematic clusters is constructed from keyword frequencies, then analyzed to detect growth trends and high-impact connections, guiding predictions about future development in intervention strategies and mechanistic understanding.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: EVALUATING PERCEIVED AFFECTIVE QUALITY (PAQ) IN INFORMAL LEARNING ENVIRONMENTS: A COMPARATIVE STUDY OF ADHD AND NON-ADHD STUDENTS

descriptions.problem: This research aims to understand how individuals with a certain attention disorder perceive their surroundings differently from those without it. It estimates and compares how these individuals experience and evaluate their learning environments.
descriptions.approach: The researchers selected participants using a convenient sampling method and measured the sound levels in four environments using a specific standard. They then analyzed the data to compare how individuals with and without the disorder evaluate these environments.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A group of individuals with varying cognitive sensitivities is assessed to determine how they experience the acoustic character of shared physical spaces, particularly in relation to environmental noise and overall comfort.
descriptions.approach: Acoustic levels are measured in situ across multiple locations during typical use. Participants rate their subjective experience of the space's noise, structure, and emotional tone, and these ratings are compared across groups with differing sensory responsiveness.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Decision Revise: How Effortful is Boredom? Studying Self-Control Demands Through Pupillometry. Round#1

descriptions.problem: This work estimates how much people allocate their mental resources to a task, and compares this to how much they think they should allocate resources to the task. It also tries to explain why people allocate resources in different ways.
descriptions.approach: The researchers use a combination of self-reported feelings and objective measures to understand how people's mental resources are allocated. They compare these measures to see if one is more important than the other.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The system estimates how much mental energy is allocated to a task based on perceived challenge and lack of engagement, and compares this allocation across different task conditions and time points.
descriptions.approach: It models mental resource distribution by tracking changes in performance and subjective feedback, then adjusts the allocation estimate using real-time responses to task stimuli and internal evaluation signals.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

topic_name: Food Security and Health in Diverse Populations
title: Abstract 4371648: Association Between Food Insecurity and Diagnoses of Cardiovascular Disease and Stroke: National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (2005-2020)

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the risk of serious health problems (such as heart attacks and strokes) in people who lack access to enough nutritious food, compared to those who have enough. It also compares the risks of these problems in people who are struggling to get by financially.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a large dataset of health information from a national survey, and analyzed it using statistical models to identify patterns and relationships. They adjusted for other factors that might affect the results, such as age, income, and health insurance.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A statistical model estimates the relationship between limited access to essential resources and the likelihood of experiencing a specific health condition, adjusting for demographic and behavioral factors.
descriptions.approach: The model uses weighted data from a longitudinal population sample, applying a statistical framework to compare outcomes across groups with and without access to resources, while controlling for age, social status, and lifestyle behaviors.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Soundscapes of Life

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the impact of human activities on the environment, predicts the effects of climate change, and compares the consequences of different scenarios. It aims to explain the importance of understanding the emotional and psychological connections between humans and the natural world.
descriptions.approach: The approach involves using a combination of data analysis and qualitative research to develop a new framework for understanding the emotional and psychological connections between humans and the natural world. This framework is based on a set of tools and methods that help people directly experience and understand the emotional and psychological impacts of human activities on the environment.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A pattern of environmental degradation is assessed through continuous, multi-sourced observations over time, including changes in natural rhythms and human behaviors. The goal is to identify correlations between these patterns and shifts in collective well-being.
descriptions.approach: A structured process is applied that integrates personal and environmental observations into a shared narrative. This narrative is refined through iterative feedback loops involving diverse participants to detect subtle shifts in perception and response to change.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Clinicopathological significance of Kruppel-like factor 15 and epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition related factors in bladder cancer

descriptions.problem: This research investigates the relationship between a specific gene and its role in a process that affects how cells change and move, and how this process is connected to the characteristics of tumors and patient outcomes. It aims to identify factors that can predict the likelihood of tumor recurrence and survival.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a technique to analyze tissue samples from patients, looking for the presence of specific proteins and their connections to other proteins. They also collected data on patient characteristics and outcomes, and used this data to identify patterns and make predictions about patient survival.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system-wide pattern of protein activity is assessed to determine its relationship with disease progression and survival outcomes across a group of tissue samples.
descriptions.approach: Protein expression levels are measured in tissue samples and correlated with clinical outcomes. A statistical model identifies which protein interactions and expression levels independently predict survival and disease spread.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Differentiating Between Dysgraphia And Dysorthographia

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the existence of two distinct conditions that affect people's ability to produce written text, and compares their features, causes, and impact on learning and development. It aims to explain the differences between these conditions to improve diagnosis and treatment.
descriptions.approach: The study uses a combination of international standards and cross-cultural perspectives to identify the key characteristics of these conditions. It follows a procedure that involves analyzing data and evidence from various sources to draw conclusions and make recommendations.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system estimates the nature and origin of errors in a structured output process, distinguishing between those arising from motor control limitations and those stemming from rule-based error patterns in symbol formation.
descriptions.approach: The system analyzes patterns of error frequency, consistency, and context to build a model that maps error types to underlying cognitive or physical constraints, then uses this model to assign a probability to each possible cause.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Prompt Loading of Implant-Backed Fixed Prostheses in Back Regions: A Systematic Exploration of Evidence

descriptions.problem: This work aims to estimate the best cases for a specific treatment to shorten the time it takes to fix a broken tooth in the back of the mouth, making it more efficient and cost-effective. It compares different approaches to find the most suitable ones.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a systematic search of existing studies to gather evidence, looking at data from various databases. They then manually reviewed the findings to identify the most effective cases.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The task is to evaluate the likelihood of successful long-term stability in a fixed restoration supported by anchoring elements in regions subject to high mechanical stress, based on available clinical and biomechanical records.
descriptions.approach: A structured review of published outcomes is conducted, filtering studies by design, duration, and follow-up, then comparing results across different anchoring strategies and patient profiles using standardized metrics.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: SUBJECTIVE ASSESSMENT OF GYM NOISE

descriptions.problem: An estimate is made of how much noise from falling weights bothers people, and this is compared to the actual noise levels on different floors. The goal is to understand how people perceive and react to noise levels.
descriptions.approach: A set of questions is used to gather information about people's reactions to different types of noise, and their responses are rated on a scale of 1 to 11. The impact of sound levels on each floor is measured and compared to the responses.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A group of individuals evaluates how disruptive specific types of sudden, short-duration vibrations are to their perception, comparing responses across different physical environments and sound intensities.
descriptions.approach: Participants rate the level of disturbance caused by sudden vibrations, using a structured scale, while responses are analyzed across varying conditions and locations to identify patterns in human reaction to abrupt mechanical events.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Higher-order $p$-form asymptotic symmetries in $D = p + 2$

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the number of independent charges that can be associated with a certain type of field in a specific space-time, and compares these charges to a known charge. It also explains how these charges are related to each other and to a fundamental concept in the field.
descriptions.approach: The researchers use a mathematical technique called symplectic renormalization to identify these charges, and then apply a process called Hodge decomposition to understand their structure. They also use a power expansion to analyze the field's behavior.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system of fields is analyzed to determine a set of conserved quantities that depend on the behavior of the fields at large distances, with each quantity defined by a function that varies smoothly across rotational directions.
descriptions.approach: The field strengths are expanded in powers and logarithmic terms, with the gauge choices adjusted to preserve directional consistency. The conserved quantities are derived by combining contributions from different field components in a structured, recursive way.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Transition to What? Uncontentious Politics and West Virginia’s ‘Just’ Transition

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the effectiveness of economic transition programmes in southern West Virginia, comparing their outcomes to a baseline of no transition. It also predicts the impact of these programmes on local communities and optimises the allocation of resources to achieve the best results.
descriptions.approach: The authors use historical data and personal reflections to understand the shift from contentious to uncontentious economic transition efforts, blending discussion of funding programmes with contextual analysis.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A pattern of economic change is assessed, where initiatives aim to shift local economic structures from extractive models to alternative models, and the underlying power dynamics within those shifts are evaluated for consistency and equity.
descriptions.approach: A framework maps funding allocations and project designs to local conditions, then compares how these initiatives address or overlook structural imbalances in control, resources, and decision-making authority.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: The Political Economy of Harmful Cultural Practices: Dowry and Son Preference as Economic Institutions

descriptions.problem: This research aims to understand the prevalence and impact of certain social practices, rooted in outdated gender norms and superstition, on public health, human rights, and social development. It estimates the number of publications on this topic, compares different perspectives, and identifies gaps in the literature.
descriptions.approach: The study uses a systematic search of academic databases to identify relevant publications, and then analyzes the data using network visualization and thematic clustering techniques to identify key themes and trends.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The task is to map and analyze patterns in scholarly work focused on socially entrenched behaviors that disproportionately affect specific groups, identifying dominant themes, evolving research trends, and gaps in interdisciplinary coverage over time.
descriptions.approach: A systematic review of published works is conducted using co-authorship and keyword networks, then visualized and clustered to reveal thematic groupings, institutional contributions, and temporal shifts in research focus and collaboration.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Pengaruh Green Perceived Quality dan Corporate Social Responsibility Terhadap Niat Beli Melalui Green Trust Sebagai Variabel Mediasi Produk Innisfree (Studi Kasus Pada Konsumen Pembeli Produk Innisfree di Wilayah Jabodetabek)

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the effect of perceived environmental quality and commitment to social responsibility on the willingness to buy products from a particular brand, with trust in the brand's environmental practices as a key factor. It compares the influence of these factors on buying decisions and finds that some factors have a stronger impact than others.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a quantitative approach, collecting data from 350 consumers of a particular brand of natural beauty products. They analyzed this data using a statistical method to identify relationships between variables and test hypotheses about the influence of environmental quality and social responsibility on buying decisions.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The strength of a consumer's willingness to engage with a product is estimated based on their perception of its environmental benefits and the organization's demonstrated commitment to ethical practices, with a focus on how trust in those practices mediates the relationship.
descriptions.approach: A statistical model links environmental attributes, organizational transparency, and trust to consumer behavior using observed data, testing whether the influence of environmental attributes on behavior is strengthened through trust in the product's values.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: SynergyImage: image-based model for drug combinations synergy score prediction

descriptions.problem: A system estimates the strength of interaction between two substances based on their structural and biological profiles, using patterns derived from visual representations of molecular and cellular states.
descriptions.approach: It converts molecular and cellular data into visual formats, extracts spatial features using image analysis, reduces dimensionality, and applies a layered network to compute interaction strength from the resulting patterns.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the potential of combining two substances to enhance a biological effect, using data about their chemical structures and how cells respond to them. It aims to predict which combinations will have the most beneficial effect.
descriptions.approach: The approach involves analyzing images of the substances' chemical structures and transforming data about how cells respond to them into these images. It then uses a neural network to identify patterns that indicate a beneficial effect when combined.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: The psychology of space perception and the influence of design on the emotional state

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the impact of design elements on how a group feels about a given environment. It predicts how different design choices will affect the overall mood of a space.
descriptions.approach: The study uses data from various studies on human behavior and design to develop a model that compares the effects of different design elements on a group's feelings. The model follows a step-by-step procedure to optimize the design for the desired emotional outcome.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: It estimates how environmental features affect human feelings of comfort and tension, based on observed reactions to physical arrangements and sensory cues.
descriptions.approach: It models responses by adjusting parameters like form, contrast, and movement patterns, then evaluates how changes in these elements shift subjective experiences across different settings.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Resistance grade of different Triticum species toward Sitophilus oryzae L. (Coleoptera: Curculionidae)

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the resistance of different types of grains to being infested by a certain insect, and compares the effectiveness of various grain traits in preventing infestation. It also predicts the potential fitness advantage of insects that can feed on larger seeds.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a combination of experiments to evaluate the resistance of different grain types, including tests to measure how many insects can survive and reproduce on each type of grain, and how much the grain's hardness affects this. They also compared the preferences of the insects for different types of grains.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The performance of different cereal varieties under insect attack is assessed by measuring survival, reproduction, and physical traits of the pest, and the relationship between seed characteristics and pest outcomes is evaluated.
descriptions.approach: Insects are exposed to multiple seed types under controlled conditions to observe survival and reproduction. Seed hardness and size are analyzed for their influence on pest behavior and output, using statistical comparisons to identify patterns and correlations.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Transanal ligation of fistula during laparoscopically assisted anorectal pull-through for rectourethral bulbar fistula—a case series

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the effectiveness of a new surgical technique for treating a specific type of complication in a certain medical condition. It predicts that this technique can reduce the incidence of urologic complications and improve patient outcomes.
descriptions.approach: The technique involves introducing a thread into the pelvic region to encircle and secure a specific abnormal connection. The procedure is performed during a minimally invasive surgery, and the thread is left in place for a period of time after the surgery.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A surgical procedure is designed to isolate and secure a persistent anatomical defect in the pelvic region that may lead to urinary complications after a complex reconstructive surgery.
descriptions.approach: A thread is passed through a defined anatomical pathway and used to encircle and tightly bind the defect, ensuring complete separation from surrounding structures during a reconstructive procedure involving pelvic reorganization.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Differential Diagnosis of Thrombotic Microangiopathy in a Patient with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus: A Case Report

descriptions.problem: This research aims to identify the underlying cause of a patient's kidney damage, which is characterized by abnormal blood tests and kidney biopsy results. The goal is to determine the most likely cause of the patient's kidney damage and to explain the underlying mechanisms.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a combination of clinical data, laboratory tests, and kidney biopsy results to identify the underlying cause of the patient's kidney damage. They compared the patient's test results to those of patients with known kidney diseases to make a diagnosis.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A pattern of progressive organ damage is assessed to distinguish between causes involving immune-mediated clotting, drug-induced injury, or systemic vascular dysfunction, using clinical, laboratory, and tissue-based evidence.
descriptions.approach: A stepwise evaluation compares vascular changes in tissue sections with blood markers and clinical symptoms, prioritizing findings of widespread vessel occlusion, normal complement levels, and specific autoantibody presence to determine the most likely underlying mechanism.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Dysbiosis and Dyslipidemia: Unraveling the Microbiome's Role in Lipid Metabolism and Therapeutic Potential

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the impact of an imbalance in the community of microorganisms living in the digestive system on the levels of cholesterol in the blood, and compares it to the levels of cholesterol in people with and without this imbalance. It aims to explain how this imbalance affects the body's ability to regulate cholesterol levels.
descriptions.approach: The researchers use data from studies on people with and without this imbalance, and analyze the effects of different types of food on the levels of cholesterol in the blood. They follow a procedure that involves identifying the types of microorganisms that are most affected by the imbalance, and testing the effects of different types of food on these microorganisms.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system is estimated that links internal microbial activity to host metabolic outcomes, particularly in regulating fat-related physiological states and their long-term health consequences.
descriptions.approach: A dynamic model integrates environmental inputs and host responses to simulate how microbial byproducts influence metabolic pathways, adjusting behavior based on real-time feedback from host physiology and dietary factors.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: ירושלים, העיר העתיקה, רחוב חב"ד

descriptions.problem: An estimate or prediction is made about the past, based on physical evidence from a site where construction work damaged some historical items. The goal is to understand what was present at that site before it was damaged.
descriptions.approach: A team of experts uses a combination of observations, measurements, and documentation to reconstruct the past state of the site, following a procedure that involves surveying, drafting, and recording the findings in a systematic way.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A pattern of human activity over time is inferred from physical remains found in a specific location, using spatial and temporal data from construction records and surface observations.
descriptions.approach: A sequence of events is reconstructed by aligning material findings with known construction timelines, using spatial mapping and contextual evidence to determine the order and nature of past interactions with the site.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Single-cell analysis reveals shared adaptive responses across different types of podocyte injury

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the molecular mechanisms underlying different types of damage to a crucial component of the glomerular filtration barrier, and identifies the shared adaptive responses of these damaged cells. It compares the effects of different types of damage on the same cells and explains the underlying disease mechanisms.
descriptions.approach: The researchers analyzed data from 16 samples of cells from healthy individuals and patients with different diseases, identifying 11 major cell types and analyzing their responses to damage. They used a combination of computational analysis and experimental validation to confirm their findings.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system-wide response is inferred from cellular gene expression patterns across diverse disease conditions, identifying common molecular trajectories despite different initial triggers.
descriptions.approach: Cells are grouped by similar expression profiles, and dynamic changes in gene activity over time are mapped to detect shared adaptive phases, using high-resolution molecular data from individual cells.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Wellness Tourism in Himachal Pradesh: A boon for locals

descriptions.problem: This research aims to estimate the potential economic benefits of a specific type of travel that focuses on physical and mental well-being, and its impact on local development. It compares the opinions of local stakeholders on the opportunities created by this type of travel.
descriptions.approach: The researcher collected data from primary and secondary sources, including interviews with 100 local stakeholders, to examine their perceptions of the benefits of this type of travel. The data was analyzed using descriptive statistical tools to identify patterns and trends.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A set of stakeholders is surveyed to assess the potential for a growing economic activity centered on personal and physical well-being, based on local environmental and lifestyle factors.
descriptions.approach: Data is collected through structured interviews with a diverse group of individuals, then analyzed using summary statistics to determine consensus on the expected benefits of a new economic model driven by natural resources and individual health priorities.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: It is their duty: a commentary on filial discrepancy and perceived neglect among older adults

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the relationship between a certain value in family relationships and the well-being of a specific group of people. It compares the effects of this value on their mental health and quality of life.
descriptions.approach: The study uses data from this group to weigh the importance of this value in their lives. It follows a procedure where the researchers analyze the data to see how this value affects their quality of life.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A pattern of unmet expectations in intergenerational relationships is assessed to determine its impact on emotional well-being and sense of isolation among individuals in later life stages.
descriptions.approach: Relationship dynamics are analyzed through observed behaviors and reported experiences, then mapped to emotional outcomes using established thresholds for perceived disconnection and distress.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Pouvoir, Espace et Algorithmes : une étude ethnographique d'équipes projet interculturelles de systèmes d'information

descriptions.problem: This study investigates how changes in work arrangements and technology influence the dynamics of teams with diverse backgrounds. It aims to understand the impact of these changes on team behavior and decision-making.
descriptions.approach: The research uses a case study approach, gathering data through ethnographical fieldwork. The data is then analyzed using a method that identifies patterns and relationships in the data to gain insights into the team's behavior and decision-making processes.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The system's behavior is observed and interpreted across diverse human groups working together to develop and maintain digital tools, with attention to how decisions, narratives, and technical processes shift based on group interactions and shared environments.
descriptions.approach: Data is collected through immersive observation and iterative analysis of real-time interactions within shared digital environments, identifying patterns in how decisions unfold and how tools evolve in response to human collaboration and context.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Refined Hybrid Plasma-Warp Propulsion (RHPWP): A Positive-Energy Subluminal Pathway to Interstellar Crewed Travel by 2070-2100

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the energy required for a vehicle to travel at a significant fraction of the speed of light, and compares it to the energy needed for other methods, in order to determine the feasibility of a specific approach.
descriptions.approach: The approach involves combining three components: a boost of energy, a layer of heated matter, and a mathematical model of how the vehicle moves. The model is used to simulate the vehicle's movement and estimate the energy required, with the goal of reducing energy requirements by orders of magnitude.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system is designed to move a payload across vast distances at speeds approaching the speed of light while maintaining physical consistency with known laws of motion and energy conservation.
descriptions.approach: It uses layered energy fields to enhance momentum transfer, combines focused energy bursts with sustained internal energy sources, and applies geometric transformations to reduce energy input while maintaining consistent velocity profiles over time.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Additional file 1 of Modelling the joint impact of early-life interventions on adult health: an illustrative example of multiple long-term conditions with role limitations in midlife using the 1970 British Cohort Study (BCS70)

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the impact of early-life events on adult health outcomes, comparing the effects of different types of events on the likelihood of experiencing role limitations in later life. It also predicts the absolute reduction in risk of these outcomes when certain events change over time.
descriptions.approach: The researchers use statistical models to analyze data from a large cohort study, comparing the effects of different types of early-life events on adult health outcomes. They then use these models to predict the impact of changes in these events on the risk of role limitations.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The task estimates how early-life exposures influence the likelihood of persistent health issues later in life, comparing outcomes across different exposure levels and identifying which early conditions most strongly affect long-term well-being.
descriptions.approach: It evaluates how changes in early-life conditions alter future health outcomes by modeling risk trajectories, using statistical adjustments for confounding factors and simulating interventions to predict potential health improvements.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Connotation and Path for High-quality Development of Contracted Family Doctor Services in Aging Society

descriptions.problem: This research aims to improve the accessibility and equity of health services for people who need them most, by identifying the best way to deliver these services. It estimates that current systems are not meeting this need, and proposes a new approach to address this issue.
descriptions.approach: The research proposes a new model for delivering health services, with a focus on door-to-door service and comprehensive support. It suggests that this approach should be supported by a well-designed policy framework and innovative use of technology.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system is evaluated to determine how well it meets the diverse and evolving health needs of a growing population, focusing on equity, access, and service effectiveness under increasing demand and resource constraints.
descriptions.approach: A framework is applied that integrates local implementation patterns with technological and structural innovations to enhance service reach, personalization, and operational efficiency through centralized planning and decentralized delivery models.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Socio-Cultural Animation, Territory, and Community Development

descriptions.problem: This work aims to improve community development by boosting intervention in a specific area, with the goal of strengthening community bonds and overall human development. It estimates the effectiveness of this approach and compares it to other methods.
descriptions.approach: The researchers use a combination of data and evidence to establish a link between community development, animation, and the area in question. They follow a procedure that involves identifying key factors and using them to inform their approach.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A process is designed to assess how human engagement in shared spaces fosters collective identity and long-term social cohesion among diverse groups.
descriptions.approach: A structured framework iteratively evaluates interactions between individuals and local environments, adjusting strategies based on observed patterns of participation and evolving group dynamics over time.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Effects and usefulness of taking Dementia Supporter Education Lecture for paramedic training students

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the usefulness of a training program for healthcare professionals who interact with elderly patients who may have cognitive impairments. It aims to improve their ability to assess and care for these patients.
descriptions.approach: The researchers developed a training program and evaluated its effectiveness by measuring the participants' understanding and skills in caring for patients with cognitive impairments. They also assessed the program's impact on the participants' knowledge of community resources and support systems.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The effectiveness of a structured training program is assessed in improving frontline responders' ability to manage complex patient interactions involving cognitive impairments.
descriptions.approach: A curriculum is delivered to individuals with limited prior exposure to such scenarios, using real-world case examples and community-based expert input to build practical response strategies and foster empathetic engagement.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

subfield: Public Health, Environmental and Occupational Health
topic_name: Legal, Health, Environmental and COVID-19 Challenges
title: What Can International Disaster Law Learn from Global Health Responses? : Workshop Report and Briefing Document

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the effectiveness of a global health response system in protecting people's health and wellbeing during times of crisis, and compares it to the current state of international disaster response. It aims to explain how a similar system could be developed for disasters.
descriptions.approach: The approach involves using data from global health responses to inform the development of a new system for disaster response, following a procedure that involves identifying key similarities and differences between the two fields.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A systematic framework is developed to evaluate how coordinated, large-scale, cross-border responses to sudden health crises have advanced in terms of preparedness, coordination, and accountability among multiple stakeholders.
descriptions.approach: A comparative analysis is conducted by mapping response structures, decision-making timelines, and information-sharing protocols across known events, then applying those patterns to assess how similar systems could be adapted for managing sudden, widespread societal disruptions.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Characteristics and Causes of Water Balance Variations during the Monsoon Period in Bamu Co on Qinghai-Xizang Plateau

descriptions.problem: This study estimates and predicts the changes in the balance of a closed system over a short period, comparing the results to historical data. It aims to explain the underlying mechanisms driving these changes.
descriptions.approach: The researchers use a combination of data from observations, reanalysis, and equations to analyze the dynamics of the system's balance components, including precipitation, inflow, evaporation, and level changes.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The system estimates how changes in surface inputs and losses affect a body's level over time, comparing the influence of different environmental drivers across months and years.
descriptions.approach: It uses observed and modeled inputs and outputs to compute level changes, applying a balance equation that tracks how input and loss components shift monthly and annually in response to environmental conditions.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Clinical Relevance of Psychrobacter Sanguinis: Occurrence and Characterization as an Emerging Pathogen in Patients with Sepsis and Pneumonia

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the occurrence and characterization of a rare, Gram-negative organism in patients with severe infections, and compares its antimicrobial resistance patterns to those of other common bacteria.
descriptions.approach: It uses molecular identification techniques to confirm the presence of the organism, and then tests its susceptibility to various antibiotics using a diffusion method.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A rare Gram-negative bacterium is being identified in clinical samples from patients with severe infections. Its response to various antimicrobial agents is assessed to determine potential treatment strategies and resistance patterns.
descriptions.approach: Samples are analyzed using mass spectrometry for molecular fingerprinting and genetic sequencing to confirm identity. Antimicrobial effectiveness is tested through diffusion-based assays to measure inhibition zones and infer susceptibility profiles.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Russia and Iran in the Shadow of Ukraine: Ontological Security, Authoritarian Regionalism, and the Politics of Alignment

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the nature of the relationship between Russia and Iran, comparing their interests and actions to understand the dynamics of their partnership. It predicts how their relationship will evolve in response to external factors.
descriptions.approach: The study uses two books as a starting point, combining their ideas to create a new framework for understanding the relationship. It then critiques this framework, adding new insights and perspectives to refine the analysis.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A pattern of sustained but non-integrated cooperation between two actors is analyzed, based on shifts in strategic behavior, resource flows, and external constraints observed over time.
descriptions.approach: A dual framework is applied: one maps evolving interactions through shared goals and mutual dependencies, the other evaluates boundaries and friction points using historical precedents and third-party influence.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman
